films.syn: Woody Harrelson is one of the most versatile actors around today: he is particularly valued for the formidable complexity of his acting craft, his intelligence and sense of humour. His Marcus in the delightful and heartwarming remake of the successful 2018 Spanish comedy of the same name is a noted basketball coach, whose career prospects are hampered by his own irascibility, stubbornness and lack of empathy. When Marcus’s foot fault becomes a series of missteps, punishment follows in the form of community service, which requires him to train a team of disabled basketball players. This cinematic lesson in humanity, with its masterful blend of humour and sentiment, is the work of Bobby Farrelly, co-creator of comedies such as There’s Something About Mary and Me, Myself & Irene.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: On the main square of a mining town stands a cross depicting a saint, regarded by the local miners as their protector. One day, the cross is taken down for repair and the statue of the saint suddenly vanishes. When a mysterious stranger subsequently appears among them, the residents put two and two together… In her third feature, a satirical parable about a saint who descends the cross to live among mortals, Tinatin Kajrishvili wonders what it is exactly that people want to believe in. Do saints have greater significance as inanimate symbols, or do they have the right to exist as living human beings? The carefully composed black-and-white images from experienced cameraman Krum Rodriguez underscore the oppression of life in the mining town and also the absurdity of the emerging situation.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: Are you what you eat? Of course you are! But don’t forget that how you eat is important as well. This is the message that Miss Novak (Mia Wasikowska) imparts on the young participants of her elective course in nutrition, through which she expands the students' horizons at a private high school. Her teaching method of “conscious eating” is unorthodox to say the least – and that is before her students learn that, after having ingested all her ideas, they can join the exclusive Club Zero. Jessica Hausner returned to Cannes with a dispassionately geometric film that incisively comments on man’s relationship to food – and the world. It is a brutal premise in a brutalist setting, tailor-made for the distinctive interior of the Hotel Thermal’s auditoriums.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: In celebration of its sixtieth anniversary, Contempt, one of the iconic films by tireless innovator and provocateur of world cinema Jean–Luc Godard, recently saw the release of its new 4K restoration. This loose reworking of Alberto Moravia’s novel is set in the film industry and examines the conflict between the desire to make money and the quest for creative freedom. Screenwriter Paul Javal (Michel Piccoli) is hired by an unscrupulous American producer named Jeremy to redraft a script for a screen adaptation to be shot by none other than Fritz Lang (who plays himself in the film). Yet the more Paul sells himself out, the more his wife (Brigitte Bardot) holds him in contempt.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1963

films.syn: Together with Jaromil Jireš’s The Joke, this directorial feature debut by Evald Schorm is the most incisive attempt to capture the all-pervasive moral enervation of Czech society in the early 1960s, when party bureaucracy prevailed and ideals simply became empty phrases. The victim here isn’t an opponent of the regime, but a loyal young labourer affiliated with the Socialist Youth Movement, who experiences a growing sense of painful disenchantment with the communist cause. This penetrating, psychological character study, heightened by a sober acting performance, renders the film a timeless statement of blind faith which, followed by disillusionment, leads to a destructive existential crisis. The film will be screened in its new, digitally restored version.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1964

films.syn: The second film by photographer and filmmaker Hossein Rajabian is an adrenaline rush which boldly seeks wisdom in madness. Rajabian signals to Ingmar Bergman from afar (in particular, his Persona) whilst, inspired by the master, he gradually transforms film reality into a psychiatric nightmare. The hero assumes the role of an animal, nevertheless, he still possesses the intuition that allows him to turn his isolation into a spiritual advantage. How can we free our hearts and minds from the errors of our predecessors? The answer lies in a woman, in her love, her pride and her vision.

ap.p: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now); production year 2019

films.syn: Sergio has remained at home to help his father run the family’s butcher shop. His brother Flavio never accepted his share of the responsibility, had a falling out with their father, and decided to leave home. When he comes back after a long time away, Sergio briefly believes that the rift in the family can still be healed. In the hands of Giulia Regini, the art of a butcher and the art of directing are both a sophisticated craft. Her multilayered Italian drama portions out different, equally dysfunctional attitudes towards an authoritarian father, reflects on the (in)ability to forge one’s own path, and captures fleeting moments of brotherly love.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2022

films.t: Dancing on the Edge of a Volcano
films.syn: A catastrophic explosion in the Port of Beirut on August 4, 2020, devastated not only a large part of the Lebanese capital, but also what remained of its inhabitants’ hopes for a dignified life in a country without corruption. The trauma also paralyses a film crew in the middle of production. The question of whether to keep on pursuing their dream project becomes increasingly obtrusive. And what of destiny, and its near-fatal impediments? A film about (the genesis of) a film; a vivid account of the state of an exquisite, ailing country; a dramatic ballad depicting a terrible dilemma: Should one remain in a beloved homeland, even if this means living below the threshold of human dignity? Should one press on with a journey rendered in the words of Lebanese poet Nadia Tueni: “I choose the sea in spite of shipwrecks”?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: An actor and actress are brought together during a casting for a mainstream film. They don’t get the roles, so they decide to make their own film instead. This will be a movie which defies the censorship rules, a film in which anything goes, and its makers won’t be held back by anything or anyone. The pair become a threesome when they get hold of a cameraman and director named Ziya, and the enchanting adventure can now begin. A burglary (the movie has to be financed somehow) marks the start of not only the shoot, but also a joyride, a game and a celebration of friendship and film. Dark Matter is a latter-day nod to the French New Wave and likewise a highly contemporary piece that reminds us why films are both a joy to make and to watch.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2023

films.t: Daydreaming So Vividly About Our Spanish Holidays
films.syn: The sun is a source of life, warmth, and health. But British teenagers live in a country where they don’t get enough sunlight. They suffer mentally and physically and compensate for the lack of sunshine by taking vitamin D supplements. They dream of escaping to the Balearic Islands – Mallorca in the case of the protagonist – to soak up as many rays as possible in the short time they have, so they can enjoy their effects even under the gloomy British skies. A surrealistically poetic film about warmth and dreams, about the stunned reactions of locals who take the sun for granted, and about the grim phenomenon of “balconing,” which has cost some tourists their lives, even though they only came to enjoy the sunshine.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2022

films.syn: Three girls – Ka, Malin, and Ira – set out to see the world after high school graduation. While traveling in Italy, they meet the mysterious Zoe, who takes them to an abandoned city. Why are the homes empty, the streets barren, and no people in sight? The young women find themselves on the threshold of adulthood, but they enter into it differently than they had imagined. This mysterious, haunting, and engaging coming-of-age story is a mature debut that is not afraid to add a surrealist touch to the lazy atmosphere of one hot summer.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: A little boy and his doggie Dede are inseparable friends. They go out for walks together, they snuggle up together, and they fall asleep together. One sad day, however, they have to say goodbye: Dede is no longer. But does that mean they’ll never meet again? After all, the memories won’t fade, and we’ll have new friends, who maybe can’t take the place of the old ones, but they can help ease the sorrow.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2023

films.syn: Two friends get into an argument. What will help them find a way to forgive one another?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: A potter named Martin Lepiš is the tragic hero of this parable about instinctive human hatred which, in seeking an outlet, has claimed many an innocent victim. The village community falsely accuses Lepiš, nicknamed the Dragon, of evil intentions, and not even his courageous act can save him from his destiny as an eternal pariah. The magical elements of the original novella are intensified in the film chiefly by the artistically expressive black-and-white camera, evoking the atmosphere of the wild mountain landscape, and by the restrained acting performances and minimalist, experimental soundtrack. The unforgiving scene, in which a herd of cattle is rescued from a forest fire, is a pure example of filmmaking mastery.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1967

films.syn: “It feels as though my camera is filled with despair, just like me; it is filled with sorrow, just like me,” is the suggestive assertion from Negin Ahmadi, the young director and protagonist of this mesmeric debut. Negin leaves Tehran and sets out with her camera in order to follow the lives of an all-female militia group fighting in Syrian Kurdistan. It isn’t long before she starts to identify with these women soldiers since she discovers that the motives which led to the point where her filmmaking has placed her life in jeopardy also apply to the young combatants, who are similarly under threat of attack. Thus, for Negin, the filming process becomes a soul-searching diary that provocatively denounces the established cinematic narratives of war.

ap.p: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now); production year 2023

films.syn: The Electra complex explored in an electrifying film. This soul-searching story about growing up too soon is told with an explosive imagination, which the director applies to immerse herself in the heroine’s traumatic memories, drawing them out in every conceivable shade of black eye. An enduringly playful and, in places, menacing film about establishing a relationship with one’s own body and much else besides.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2023
Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2023

films.syn: Penelope and Isidoros live in a world where today they are lovers but the following day they scarcely know one another. It is a place where time doesn’t flow, where the days appear randomly in the past, the present, and the future – if these concepts even apply here. Their relationship is constantly changing; it is one continuous uncertainty marked by shared searching and reassuring. Somewhere next to their world is another where time is linear. It is possible to travel from arbitrary time to linear time, but the conditions for such a journey are mysterious and the price is high… An imaginative film about the paradoxes of time and of romantic and other relationships.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: Amir and Narges, two people in love, who might be described as having been born under an unlucky star. The young man is from a poor family background and, after he is laid off from his job as a waiter, he is forced to find work in a fishing community. Narges has a higher social status and comes from a “good family”. For the time being, they are keeping their relationship a secret. In order for them to marry, Amir has to earn enough money for a dowry. To add to his problems, he discovers that the fishery employing him is also involved in dishonest business practices… Behrooz Karamizade’s feature debut is a realistic drama set in contemporary Iran which eschews embellishment in order to depict a struggle for the right to love, an entitlement that shouldn’t be contingent on money.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: Ahmed, a teacher originally from Tehran currently living in exile near the border with Afghanistan, tries to protect a young man in love and a girl trapped in an arranged marriage – all while also trying to reconnect with his estranged wife. The film, told in dozens of shades of gray, is set amidst an expansive mountain landscape that nevertheless feels claustrophobic. Winner of the Big Screen Competition at the Rotterdam International Film Festival, Endless Borders is a gripping drama in which danger lurks literally everywhere: within the family, amid the area’s ethnic and religious tensions, and inside the politically repressive regime.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: A look at the legendary Czech sound designer and his profession. Editor and documentary filmmaker Adéla Špaljová has her father Ivo Špalj talk about his life, career, and working methods. Over the course of his long life, sound designer Ivo Špalj (*1940) has collaborated on hundreds of films and become a mentor for at least one generation of men and women behind the mixing board. This gentle documentary also shows “Engi” (as he is known to his colleagues) again working with Jan Švankmajer, whose films he has lent their typical, dense, and sophisticated sound mix.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 2023

films.syn: The Lord of the Rings and Star Wars, Gremlins 2 and Hammer Film’s The Mummy. Iconic actor Christopher Lee died in virtually every other role he played. Jan Soldat’s nerdy short film compilation lines up one death after another and, amid this involuntary stream, reveals entertaining gems and various connections as well – not only those relevant to the advance of Lee’s acting career.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2023

films.syn: A searing account of the four-year siege of Sarajevo, which lasted from April 1992 to February 1996. Renowned French documentary filmmaker Jean-Gabriel Périot takes two different approaches to his film. First, he works exclusively with archival footage, letting us see the street fighting through the lenses of young filmmakers who defended the city with weapon and camera in hand. In the second part, the same people look back on the past a quarter century later. A sketch of the traumatic experiences of the civil war is thus transformed into a portrait of a wounded creative spirit. Facing Darkness is film as document and film as therapy; it asks whether, face to face with cruelty, we can escape the darkness.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2023

films.syn: A teenager in search of recognition, a worker ready to do anything to hit the jackpot, and a senior executive at the end of his career who wants to prove to himself that he is still alive. Three characters who are losing speed on the competition highway.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: Holappa works as a construction laborer, lives in a workers' hostel, and drowns his sorrows in the excessive consumption of alcohol. Ansa has a poorly paid job at a supermarket and returns home in the evenings to an empty apartment, where the radio is tuned in to news of Russia’s bloody invasion of Ukraine. One night, the trajectories of their lives intersect at a dingy karaoke bar… This year Aki Kaurismäki, a living legend known for his distinctive directorial style and extremely dry sense of humor, returned to Cannes in best form for the first time in twelve years. His melancholic romantic comedy, set to the rhythm of “Mambo Italiano,” melted the hardened hearts of even the greatest cynics and took home the Jury Prize from a panel headed by last year’s winner Ruben Östlund.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Four years after the successful arthouse gem Invisible Life (The Invisible Life of Eurídice Gusmão), Karim Aïnouz offers up another rousing and stylistically spellbinding account of woman’s invincible inner strength in a film which recently competed in Cannes for the Palme d’Or. We’re coming up to the mid-16th century and infamous Henry VIII continues to rule over Tudor England. His sixth wife Catherine Parr lives both in the knowledge that she may not necessarily be the tyrant’s last spouse, and also in the hope that she will realise her progressive ideas, particularly regarding her faith. Alicia Vikander and Jude Law are the mesmerising stars of this modern reimagining of a period film which is, at the same time, a psychological thriller of its kind.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Alicia Vikander); production year 2023

films.syn: Sicily in the 1980s. Seventeen-year-old Gianni faces harassment because of his sexual orientation. His life changes the moment he meets Nino. The two boys’ friendship slowly grows into a romantic relationship in which they can behave openly and without shame. But their relationship is rejected by their conservative families, who seek to put an end to it. Inspired by true events, Italian actor Giuseppe Fiorello’s directorial debut tells a deeply moving story about the painful struggles for a love that majority society disapproves of. But it is these struggles that fuel the greater fight for political change.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: Matthias is going on a weekend course of self-discovery called “My Value on Earth,” which was an expensive gift from his girlfriend. The course is supposed to help him deal with his chronic inability to finish things that he’s started. But before Matthias leaves, his girlfriend springs a surprise on him: he’s going to be a father. And so he hopes to use the weekend, which he has no real desire to go on, to answer new and pressing questions. The “alternative” therapist, however, doesn’t inspire much trust. The tragicomedy Frantic Attempts takes aim at the field of personal development, in particular, dubious therapists who offer quick fixes. After all, what if we should answer our existential questions ourselves instead of trying to find answers from others?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2022

films.syn: There's nothing better than cooking a wonderful soup and then sitting down to truly enjoy it. But what if the seasoning runs out and we haven't got what we need to make it just right? There's nothing for it but to jet off into outer space for a really great adventure.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2021

films.syn: Getting up after a sleepless night, greeting neighbours, going to work, where she spends her days making fortune cookies. This is the life of Donya, an Afghan immigrant who has now made her home in Fremont, USA. Loneliness and insomnia are problems the young woman is trying to address, initially on her own and later with the help of a quirky therapist. It’s unclear whether it’s harder for her to come to terms with her traumatic past or with her current unsettled existence. Will Donya find a solution by hiding a message in one of the thousands of fortune cookies that get sent out? A lightly wistful comedy about a quest of self-discovery that asks whether refugee status is a condition of geographical location or whether it’s a state of mind. It’s also a film about hope coming along when we least expect it.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: A photo of Timothée Chalamet is set on an improvised altar, while the narrative centres on the primeval legends of the Minahasa people of Indonesia. The film treads a fine line between playfulness and disarming naivety as it combines cultural traditions (animism meets the Spice Girls) and social commentary with a coming-of-age story. When you shave your eyebrows do you then start to see the spirits?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2022

films.syn: Copious corporate satires were released in the 1950s, but there was nothing like Giants and Toys, Masumura’s frantic, delirious and brilliantly acerbic tale of three caramel candy companies fighting for Japan’s hearts and pockets. Partially inspired by Elia Kazan’s A Face in the Crowd and set against the space race, Giants and Toys is both a product of its era and a timeless allegory of consumerist and celebrity cultures, the toxic dominance of America, and the moral price paid for modernity. Shot on garish Agfacolor film stock and intonated in a rapid-fire dialogue, Giants and Toys is a feverish sugar rush of a film: an onslaught of image and sound that feels eerily relevant in an age of social media influencers and spiritual vacuums.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Yasuzô Masumura); production year 1958

films.syn: This new (self-)portrait of the late genius among directors is the kind of film you hope will never end. Godard was generous in interviews yet, here, the creators were still able to discover and incorporate archival footage which even his aficionados will be seeing for the first time. With anyone else, meaningful provocativeness and intellectual directness would be seen as a contradiction in terms; however, in Godard’s case, they fully capture his charisma and expression, his uniqueness and unclassifiability. Arguably the most inspirational filmmaker of all time, he also fascinates contemporary novices in film direction – not only through his work, but also through his ability to analyse it, the demands he makes primarily on himself, and his uncompromising judgement, that all too rare quality.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 2023

films.syn: The fated story of the bond between two women, and of redemption for a transgression committed years before, is set in relatively recent troubled times, when the inhabitants of South Sudan fought for regional autonomy from the ruling Arab North. After her husband’s tragic death, young Julia and her little son Daniel end up on the streets, until the abandoned pair are taken in by Mona, a well-to-do former singer. The maid and half-orphan are gradually accepted as members of the family, while Mona and Julia become inseparable confidantes. Even a shocking event from the distant past, which only one of them knows about, seems to have been completely forgotten. At Cannes this year Goodbye Julia grabbed the attention of both the audience and the Un Certain Regard jury, which presented this stirring drama with one of its awards.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Life in Darjeeling in northern India passes by uneventfully. Every now and then, the quiet days are enlivened by a village ritual or an unexpected drama, as when nine-year-old Guras’s beloved dog Tinkle goes missing. Perhaps he was merely taken by someone from the neighboring village, and not eaten by the leopard prowling the area. The young girl’s family, however, has other things to worry about: the cardamon harvest is not going as planned, and they are struggling for their mere existence. Guras is left on her own to look for her four-legged companion, but in this magical land of tea plantations, good advice awaits in surprising places... A mystical odyssey of painful loss that shows the different ways of mourning of children and adults.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: Two women’s gazes randomly meet in an empty library. Two men talk about what the best kiss looks like. A couple is kissing and she bites him… Snippets of relationships, love, passion, rationality, disgust. Director Kim Allamand’s captivating film explores all these phenomena associated with romantic relationships. Allamand has decided to deconstruct clichés of cinematic love by breaking down relationships into tiny fragments so masterfully that the viewer’s expectations are gradually sublimated and can be inconspicuously replaced by a new and fresh viewpoint. The rapid-fire images of relationships are both funny and painful – exactly like the relationships all around us.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2022

films.syn: Two drifting souls, a construction worker and an expert on mosses and lichens, and the world that surrounds them – a moment lingering on nature, a moment spent in night-time Brussels. Winner of Berlin’s Encounters Award for Best Film, Here captures its heroes both in a state of uncertainty and in close contact with the commonplace. Devos, like Tsai Ming-liang, oscillates between a dispassionate, realistic approach with social emphasis and an illusory dreamworld, while also thematising something as elusive as the perception of passing time. A magical and serene piece shrouded in inner mystery; as homely and fragile as a treasured old coffee mug.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2023

films.syn: Framed by Jorge Luis Borges’s verse, this poetic collage is the work of an artist with a feel for shimmering ordinariness and seemingly conventional images and their structures. Random fragments are assembled to create an agreeable film prompting us to contemplate whether we can reproduce moments once borne away by the river of time.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2023

films.syn: How do foreign images make their way into our minds? What do they say about an era we have never lived in but nevertheless feel we know intimately? At a time when family snapshots have become an integral part of everyday life, the film’s young director takes an original look back at Portugal’s past. Through interviews with filmmakers, she uncovers hundreds of amateur images, fleeting “imprints of the culture” of her home country, and she asks how to work with these images further. Her sensitive essay explores the ambivalent nature of nostalgia, reveals the complexity of the creative process, and encourages us to stop and be in the places we call home.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2022

films.syn: Vehement anti-militarism was a recurrent theme in Masumura’s work, and Hoodlum Soldier is his most disparaging take on the subject – a sardonic attack on Japan’s imperialism and the classist, hierarchical military system. This buddy comedy centers on the unlikely friendship that develops between Kisaburo, a hell-raising ex-yakuza gangster unwillingly turned into a military soldier (Shintarô Katsu, star of the Zatoichi series) and Arita (Takahiro Tamura), a meek pacifist intellectual, as they venture to find a way out of the army. Shot with a vivid realism uncommon in Masumura’s films, Hoodlum Soldier is a precursor to Robert Altman’s M*A*S*H: an uproariously funny, immensely entertaining war picture that champions survival and individualism over hollow patriotism.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Yasuzô Masumura); production year 1965

films.syn: A futile voyage, or a journey from which everyone returns enriched? Director Helena Wittmann sends out a crew of five men and one woman into the Mediterranean Sea, yet no conflict arises during their expedition. Instead we follow situations, none of which has a dramatic edge over another. The procedural film respects the aimless nature of drifting and appears to capture the process of learning and discovery. This hypnotic, irresistibly shimmering work unobtrusively seeks poetry in the commonplace and, in its finest moments, touches upon the mythical archetype - among others, thanks to the way in which it is able, through detail, to convey impressions from diverse situations.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2022

films.syn: A children’s nursery rhyme that becomes progressively sinister. Even something so seemingly innocent and internationally comprehensible will have hidden meanings – and it’s this ambiguity that renders this miniature by Japanese artist Shigeo Arikawa truly memorable. Can a counting rhyme have fatal consequences? And from what age do we realise that not every game is innocent?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2023

films.syn: It would be difficult to find a more polluted city on Earth than the Mongolian capital Ulaanbaatar. Most of the city’s inhabitants live in yurts and use coal to stay warm during the cold winter months. Teenager Ulzii is used to these conditions, but he wants more. He excels in physics and dreams of studying at a prestigious foreign university. But when his mother leaves to work in the countryside, he is forced to look after his younger siblings and to put his plans on hold. While some bears hibernate all winter in a soothing slumber, others must dig in their claws and struggle against fate. This masterful debut is a subdued celebration of the power of human determination. Battsooj Uurtsaikh excels in his first major role.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: It is 1987 and the wind of change will soon also be sweeping across communist Poland. Ela is a young woman seeking refuge from the insipidness of a life hallowed by the regime, mixing with artists on the alternative scene, singing in clubs with her post-punk band, and attending alcohol-fuelled parties… In her second film director Olga Chajdas summons up vital energy to invigorate the music scene of the Baltic Tricity and, aided by the charismatic actress and co-scripter Lena Góra, she offers the viewer a vivid portrait of a multilayered character – an inspirational artist forever enveloped in cigarette smoke, a woman struggling with her inner demons, yet also a fragile creature yearning for motherly love.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: 20-something Aden has no other ambition in life than to become an actor. Most of his time is spent making videos as he applies for roles he’ll never get. After a string of dreadful auditions, where bizarre and humiliating requests are made of him, he comes up with a radical move: he will take full responsibility for finding a role that primarily he, himself, wants to play. This self-assured debut, playful in form and narrative with a fairy-tale edge to it, examines both the commercial work ethic and the concept of identity, which it presents as multilayered and also questionable. At the same time, in its exploration of the given themes, the film doesn’t deny itself a socio-critical tone, nor does it resist the temptation to tease the viewer a little.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: The Second World War is drawing to a close, but life in the Philippine countryside still resembles a nightmare. When a supernatural evil begins to infiltrate a home inhabited by a woman and two children, it is just another episode in an already extreme situation. Young Tala seeks refuge with a magical fairy, but even her goodwill remains in doubt. In My Mother’s Skin, which toys with a magical vision of the world that transforms the horrors of war into mythological monsters, is something like Pan’s Labyrinth mixed with Asian folk horror. A combination of horror flick and war movie, filled with slowly rising tension and eruptions of physical violence.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Midnight Screenings); production year 2023

films.t: In the Heavens and on Earth
films.ot: Dans les cieux et sur la terre
films.syn: Film material as an intermediary of spiritual immersion, as a way in which to appreciate the passing of time? The Canadian filmmaker (otherwise closely associated with the performance project Jerusalem in My Heart) brings a new dimension to limestone structures in Montreal, which she shot on reversal film over a period of seven years.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2022

films.syn: The latest film by Brandon Cronenberg, son of the famous Canadian master of body horror David, feels like White Lotus for twisted minds. The main protagonist, the stuck-in-a-rut author James, is vacationing at a tourist resort in a poor seaside country. There, he inadvertently causes an incident that sets in motion a series of bizarre events showing that there is no futuristic technology that rich elites won’t manage to abuse. In Infinity Pool – less horror than dark, understated sci-fi – Cronenberg has toned down his usually extravagant visuality, which only lends this cold and misanthropic satire an even greater sense of urgency.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Midnight Screenings); production year 2022

films.syn: In Jordan, inheritance law applies only to men. If a woman does not have any male heirs, she must split the property with the extended family. When Nawal’s husband unexpectedly passes away, she finds herself in just such a situation. Left alone with a young daughter, she must face her country’s unfavorable patriarchal laws, ravenous relatives, and her husband’s past. At the center of this social drama is actress Mouna Hawa, who has manifested a boundless range of emotions in a character who besides learning to drive also begins to take control of her own life on her journey towards more equal conditions. The first Jordanian film ever screened at Cannes features an outstanding script filled with twists and turns that is equal parts caustic, angry, and touching.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: A mystical cinematic pilgrimage about people who won’t cocoon themselves even under the burden of their mere existence. Thien is returning from Saigon to the region of his birth, transporting to his hometown his orphaned nephew and the body of his sister-in-law, who died in an accident. The journey to this forgotten corner of Vietnam invigorates his faith yet also conjures up spectres from the past. Debuting director Thien An Pham behaves in a way similar to that of celebrated architect Jan Blažej Santini-Aichel. He steers the continuous images patiently and serenely, conscious of the fact that a work of art’s spatial arrangement itself may ultimately lead to a spiritual experience. A major screening event at Cannes, the film was included in Directors’ Fortnight and won the Caméra d’Or for best debut.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: In July 2014, a passenger jet flying from Amsterdam to Kuala Lumpur was shot down over Ukraine, killing all 298 people on board. This documentary collage assembles a picture of the tragedy from a wide range of available materials – flight radar, transcripts of wiretappings, Russian television reports, amateur footage from the impact site, choreographed dances, and animated children’s drawings. Combining poetry with forensic analysis, the film is equal parts elegy and found-footage horror. Its title refers to the shrapnel of the BUK anti-aircraft system that pierced the plane’s hull and caused its crash.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: A short film about love and freedom. It’s 1981 in communist Czechoslovakia and a young man named Jindřich is surprised to encounter his childhood sweetheart Eva on board a charter flight to Cuba. They immediately strike up a conversation, and with every answer, with every glimpse and inadvertent touch, the old bond is rekindled. Little do they know that they will soon be facing what might be the most difficult decision of their lives.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: The metropolis of Brasília effectively grew up on a greenfield site and subsequently left its indelible mark on the ecosystem. Filmmaker Ana Vaz sets off into the city’s streets in the hours of darkness, into an urban wilderness, where animals move about between the constant stream of cars and within the interminable industrial zones. Vaz’s experimental cinematic form combines documentary and essayistic elements with an atmosphere of horror, intensified by an unsettling score. This atmospheric ride into the unknown possesses dream-like qualities while nevertheless maintaining a close connection with reality. Is the spectacle of a sleeping capybara disturbing or reassuring?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2022

films.syn: A solar eclipse has brought people to the edge of madness. The Earth witnesses extreme brutality manifested by the need to make terrible sacrifices to an unknown evil. How could this have happened? Is this the wrath of God? Such is the view of a group of extremists who are quick to deal with those responsible. But who decides who is guilty and who is not? Vahid Vakilifar’s fourth film offers an intoxicating, visionary sci-fi which, in spite of the darkness consuming the world, believes in the power of light. Even the goriest images conceal at least a sliver of hope; they serve as a necessary ritual if we are to accept the demons that inhabit us all.

ap.p: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now); production year 2022

films.syn: “Ever since my son was born, I have been having nightmares about my mother.” Without ceremony and with disarming sincerity, renowned French documentarist Émilie Brisavoine draws us into the universe of her somewhat distinctive family. After launching a charm offensive in Cannes eight years ago with a portrait of her half-sister and her family in Oh La La Pauline!, she now fixes her searching and troubled gaze on a fascinating and destructive element named Meaud: A punk mum who gave her daughter the gift of life and then kept running away from it. A spontaneous feminist and a beguiling grandma. A mesmeric, intimate odyssey into the very depths of the soul, and a powerful cinematic cry from a filmmaker seeking traces of withheld emotion.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: In this gripping historical drama, legend of Italian cinema Marco Bellocchio looks back at a case that began in 1858, when six-year-old Edgardo Mortaro was forcibly removed from his Jewish family on the basis of the Catholic authorities’ claim that he had been secretly baptized as an infant and must therefore be raised as a Catholic. Papal law is unrelenting, and despite the protests of the Jewish community, the boy is taken to Rome, where he is given a Catholic education. This story of a family divided becomes intertwined with the process of Italian unification, the rebellions against the rule of Pope Pius IX, and the Church’s desperate attempts to hold on to its unlimited power.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Boy meets girl. He is a delivery boy, she's an artist’s model. Their fathers are in prison: his is a politician accused of electoral fraud; hers is a governmental employee charged with embezzlement. Over the course of one day, the young pair hit the beach, go to the races, attempt to reconcile with their families, and fall in love. A snapshot of the aimless, post-war Japanese youth brimming with vitality and compassion, Masumura’s wondrous debut is a sublime piece of the popular 1950s Sun Tribe genre, significantly deviating from convention by featuring underprivileged protagonists. Laced with the kind of carefree optimism rarely figuring in his subsequent work and containing little of the artifice that would define his filmmaking, Kisses is a singular entry point to Masumura’s colossal oeuvre.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Yasuzô Masumura); production year 1957

films.syn: The 1980s. Disheveled, unshaven, in a faded white coat, always a cigarette between his lips. This is the Englishman Arthur (Josh O’Connor), who is on his way back to a seaside village in Tuscany. His job? Treasure hunter – he and a ragtag gang of compatriots earn their living robbing Etruscan graves. But hidden behind his unkempt exterior is an inner turmoil fueled by his inability to forget his lost love Beniamina. Fantasy film or eccentric, comedic dream? The Karlovy Vary festival program just had to reserve a place for Alice Rohrwacher’s fourth feature outing, characterized by her typically wild plot and unmistakably vibrant style.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Is it possible to interpret philosophical ideas through dance? The reflections of Alice Koubová and the physical performance of the Tantehorse theatre company come together in this elegantly directed film, which assails us both intellectually and through its elementary human comprehensibility. Crisis – transition – resilience.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2023

films.syn: A hangover dance and an allegory of a tough queer existence. A performative film which is as appealingly expressive (music by Hannah Holland) as it is bitterly sombre. Aesthetic shots of a male body amid deserted, neglected surroundings, where the well-honed torso contrasts with an expression of decay. A voyeuristic, yet also intimate experience, as exhilarating as a party, and as exhausting as the morning after.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2022

films.syn: The jaded detective Travis Hurley arrives in a small town in order to investigate the 20-year-old disappearance of the aboriginal girl Charlotte. The local inhabitants are initially skeptical of the white newcomer, but his stoic nature soon gets them to reveal old secrets and open up their hearts. This desert noir set in the bleak beauty of Australia’s opal fields explores the dark shadows of a long-ago crime and gives voice to those living on the segregated margins of Australian society. It is an atmospheric film that injects into its viewers’ veins just the right mixture of desperation and hope, with the seasoned Mentalist Simon Baker exceling as an unexpected fixer of human destinies.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Twins Kolya and Vasya make a fine pair: one is a small-time con artist, the other an upright police officer. But neither has had much success in life, so they decide to do at least one thing right: together, they set out for faraway Luxembourg to visit their dying father, whom they haven’t seen in twenty years and whose adventurous life is shrouded in legend. The director’s second, again partially autobiographical, film sensitively combines cheerful and melancholy scenes into a tragicomic tale of people looking for the things missing from their lives – and of losses that are ultimately rewarding.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.t: Mami Wata – A West Afrikan Folklore
films.syn: In the remote Nigerian seaside village of Iyi, the people still venerate the water goddess known as Mami Wata. One day, the waves wash ashore a stranger who is taken in by the local leader Mama Efe and her daughters. But instead of gratitude and respect, the newcomer Jasper seeks to subjugate the traditional matriarchy. A distinctive contribution to the Nigerian New Wave, Mami Wata tells of the cost of progress and explores the accompanying crisis of faith. One of the winning films at this year’s Sundance Film Festival, it stands out in particular for its stunning visual style and poetic black-and-white images.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Camil can’t cope with the world around him – which comes as no surprise, given that events take an unexpected turn at every opportunity. Sebastian Mihăilescu’s feature debut might seduce us with its parallels with the whacky films of Quentin Dupieux, or with the poetic charm of stylised banality familiar from the work of Roy Andersson, and in places it might seem to have emerged from the Black Lodge in Twin Peaks. Yet Mihăilescu creates his own poetics in which abstraction encounters the kind of ominousness that paralyses us in real life. Expressive moments conflict with familiar feelings of dejection. An imaginative, zany film which gives the impression someone might have tried to sedate it with ketamine.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2023

films.t: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
films.syn: 1805, the open sea. Napoleon is the master of Europe, and the British flotilla is the only thing standing between him and the rest of the world. Captain Jack Aubrey and the HMS Surprise are ordered to destroy the French ship Acheron, but their first encounter doesn’t go according to plan and Aubrey is forced to retreat. His uncompromising sense of duty nevertheless compels him to pursue the French at all cost, regardless of fog, storms, or the dangers of the ocean. Peter Weir’s famous film has withstood the test of time – thanks to a sensitive combination of epic story and multilayered dialogue that never loses sight of the human condition and takes us on a riveting journey into the sailor’s soul. Russell Crowe excels in one of his essential roles.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Russell Crowe); production year 2003

films.syn: What does the daily life of a midwife look like? Friends Sofia and Louise have their first encounter with a profession sometimes called the most beautiful job in the world. But besides witnessing the miracle of birth, midwives must also often deal with the difficulties associated with the immense responsibility of their profession, an unrelenting and hectic hospital environment, and sometimes also death – which often tests their emotional limits. An incisive and highly empathetic look (on the personal as well as political levels) at the lives of those whose important social role is often undermined by a dysfunctional healthcare system.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Seymour Moskowitz (Seymour Cassel), a long-haired parking attendant with an overgrown handlebar moustache, has just moved from New York to Los Angeles. Anxious beauty Minnie (Gena Rowlands) works as a curator for the local modern art museum and is involved in a degrading affair with a married man (John Cassavetes). She is rescued from a disastrous blind date by the elemental Seymour, who at length decides with unfeigned sincerity that Minnie is the one for him. A romantic comedy drama demonstrating that love declarations can also get heated, which Cassavetes himself dedicated "to all the people who didn’t marry the person they should have.” The roles of both protagonists’ mothers were performed with gusto by the actual mothers of John Cassavetes and Gena Rowlands.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1971

films.syn: “Don’t drink so much water, or you’ll get frogs in your tummy!” “Don’t eat melon seeds, or a tree will grow in your tummy!” How many times have we heard these and similar utterances from our mothers? You don’t want to believe it, but what d'you do when you know mom is ALWAYS right?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: Monica returns to her family home after a long absence to look after her ailing mother (Patricia Clarkson). It is the first time since her departure that she makes contact with her family, and the first time her mother sees her after her sex change. Will she be accepted for who she is, as she has always wanted to be? An intimate portrait of a woman forced by circumstances to face her past, Monica explores universal themes of forgiveness, aging, and the importance of a mother’s unconditional love. It offers an evocative “deep-dive” into the main character’s inner world, focusing on her pains, fears, needs, and desires while successfully illustrating the consequences that rejection can have on an individual’s self-image.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: Saori is raising her son Minato on her own. When Minato begins to behave strangely, she is determined to discover the cause of this change. The accusations land on his teacher, Hori, and an angry Saori rushes to the school to seek justice. But reality is not as simple as it at first seems… Yuji Sakamoto’s Cannes-winning screenplay masterfully assembles the individual pieces of the story, telling them from the perspective of the various actors and causing viewers to doubt themselves just when they think that they’ve figured it all out. Director Hirokazu Koreeda again shows a rare sense for guiding child actors and applies his typical humanist approach to convey a moving story about family, people’s yearning to be understood, and the burden of secrets.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Rin is a young woman growing up during a time of famine. There is so little food that her village cannot afford to welcome any newcomers, including newborn children. Her family is one of the last in the village, and their lives thus depend on remaining obedient to those who control the last kernels of grain. Rin’s only consolation comes from an alliance with the gods of the wilderness looking down on this human suffering. The period film’s impressive wide shots of nature truly bring to life and radiate with supernatural forces, thus intertwining the story’s balladic aspects with its more realistic line.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: Director Mehran Tamadon admits that the premise behind his film was somewhat naive. He had wanted to find Iranian refugees living in France who in the past had been interrogated by the Iranian police. His idea was to place them in the role of interrogator and himself in the role of prisoner. He would then take the footage back to Iran, where it would be confiscated. The interrogators watching the footage would then end up seeing themselves in a mirror and be forced to engage in self-reflection. But the filming process took him in a different direction, and the film became a form of therapy, a terrifying testimony about life in a totalitarian regime and about the dangers of power, even when it flows only from the script.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: What propels young men willingly to shed their identities for an uncertain objective? How far can men go to safeguard their vocation? Can morality realistically have a place in wartime? Masumura poses a myriad of thorny questions in this sober spy drama, stripping the genre of all its glamour and focusing on the cunning institutionalization of men too proud and too self-delusional to confront the legitimacy of their work. Set during the Sino-Japanese War of 1937, Raizô Ichikawa is Jiro, an idealistic young man who finds himself recruited in Japan’s first military intelligence school. Faced with stern ethical choices, Jiro is prompted to decide what kind of man he envisions himself to be.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Yasuzô Masumura); production year 1966

films.syn: A film full of bitterness, but it is not bitter. Critical but capable of self-critique. With No Bears, Panahi follows on from his previous works: in the role of his own film’s protagonist, he directs a new film about emigration – via long-distance, from a village near the border. And thus he could himself be justifiably suspected of seeking to emigrate. As if the complicated film shoot wasn’t enough, he also finds himself drawn into a village dispute. The story explores a director’s responsibility for manipulating reality and demarcates a negative space that cannot be depicted – a space occupied by silence, by the apparatus of the regime. No Bears was awarded the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: Nader Saeivar contributed to the screenplay of 3 Faces by Jafar Panahi, and the celebrated filmmaker returned the favour not only by assuming the same role of co-scriptwriter on Saeivar’s directorial effort, but also by collaborating as film editor. Central to this Kafkaesque nightmare is Ayaz, an honest, hardworking man, whose only dream is to have a home of his own. In order to achieve this goal he engages in a little act of deceit which, however, attracts the attention of the secret police. Using their relentless bullying techniques, the police force him into a state of psychotic constriction from which there is no escape. No End is a film which, through blunt realism, points a finger at the control and humiliation of chosen individuals on the part of any authoritarian regime.

ap.p: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now); production year 2021

films.syn: His family once called him the devil and forced him to leave for Europe. Now, eighteen years later, Koffi returns to his native Congo with his pregnant girlfriend, hoping that the culturally determined apple of discord has lost its former bitterness. But an innocent incident sparks a new wave of hysteria and misunderstanding. Meanwhile, a gang war rages on the streets outside. To watch Omen is to peer into a kaleidoscope of modernity in which somber reflections on the legacy of cultural traditions are transformed into a hypnotic dance of unforgettable images, colorful metaphors, and intuitive meanings. This consummately chaotic yet sensitive cinematic carnival was awarded the New Voice Prize at Cannes.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: A boat anchored in the very heart of Paris acts as a unique daycare center for people with mental disorders. The staff of this “Noah’s Ark” do not view mental problems as a stigma and offer their clients countless activities aimed at improving their dignity and creativity. After Every Little Thing (1996), the award-winning French documentary filmmaker again explores the lives of persons with an intellectual disability in order to show us a world in which everybody is seen first and foremost as a human being, without the need to categorize by class, race, or intellect. With his eloquent relativization of what is considered “normal,” Philibert earned the Golden Bear for Best Film at this year’s Berlinale.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: After being forced to leave Iran, Iman lives in a refugee facility with his family. Their bleak existence consists of constant moves and the long wait to be granted a visa. In an attempt at ensuring their future in Sweden, Iman returns to wrestling despite having promised his wife that he wouldn’t. It is a decision that not only brings physical pain but also opens up wounds in his soul. A psychological drama about a man caught between suppressed desires and his duty to his family, Opponent takes an incisive look at questions of uprootedness, freedom, and tolerance. Milad Alami’s second feature impressed audiences at the Berlinale thanks to its economical storytelling and an excellent performance by Payman Maadi (A Separation, 2011).

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: “Who are the contemporary Orlandos?”, asks writer and trans activist Paul B. Preciado, in reference to the famous work by Virginia Woolf. In his directing debut, a collective documentary portrait, he pays tribute to the first novel whose main character undergoes transition, written almost a century ago; he also invites twenty-five people, all trans or gender fluid, not only to recall passages from the book, but also to speak about what it is to be transgender or non-binary. This proud, intellectually uncompromising and shrewdly witty essay upends stereotypes, dismantles categories and gives the finger to an oppressive gender system which insists there are only men and women on this earth and nothing in between.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Mouths stay clamped shut like oysters. But as the shells crack and hands tear them apart, the truth rises to the surface.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: After completing his most recent film, Tomas begins an affair with the teacher Agathe. By giving in to his desire for the unknown – being with a woman – he tests the patience of his husband Martin, with whom he shares an idyllic but staid life. In his eighth film, Ira Sachs, a master at capturing even the most subtle nuances of relationships, explores the complicated nature of love triangles. Sachs has entrusted the lead roles to well-known faces of European cinema Franz Rogowski, Adèle Exarchopoulos, and Ben Whishaw. His cast breathes life into characters who, against the backdrop of contemporary Paris, repeatedly discover that human desire can be searing, but also fickle and constantly changing.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Writer Nora and her childhood love Hae-Sung live thousands of kilometers apart, but they are connected by a deep bond. After more than twenty years, these two kindred spirits meet again in New York over the course of a few days. The unexpected reunion forces Nora to ask herself, “What if?” Told in multiple timelines, director Celine Song’s sensitive modern romance is a unique tale of two people who feel an emotional closeness even though their paths in life seem fated to pass each other by.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: This humanist tale from contemporary Tokyo asks how we can live our lives regardless of all the difficulties we must face. Hirayama accepts a job cleaning public toilets with a surprising sense of humility. Although his life might strike us as arduous, boring, and sometimes even demeaning, his routine gives each day much-needed structure, and he takes joy from simple moments of contemplation in the park, reading a book, or listening to music. He radiates a sense of peace and happiness, but is it all just a defense mechanism? Kōji Yakusho’s portrayal of the taciturn toilet cleaner brought him a much-earned Best Actor award at Cannes.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: A feminist body-horror. A take on adolescence as a time when young women are continually forced to reassess their appearance and made to fit into the “nice, sweet girl” category. A detective story about young girls who vanish under mysterious circumstances in a small town, and it’s here that 17-year-old Jonny has been sent to live with her eccentric aunt (Alicia Silverstone). On her 18th birthday the aunt entrusts Jonny with a family secret, possibly both a curse and a gift, which might help to find the kidnapper. In her new film Jennifer Reeder preserves her unmistakably unsettling, bloodily poetic style, where she loosely blends elements of melodrama, dream and the horror atmosphere of an ordinary day.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: The quiet, brooding, but attractive young welder Lalo becomes a porn actor. On the set of a film about a Mexican revolutionary and his “boys,” he feels what is perhaps his first sense of comradeship with others like him who are “out,” but the experience also exposes him to the mechanical and soulless nature of the business of physical pleasure. Both sides of his new life become even more tangible when his career moves onto social networks. Besides the melancholy of its title, this thematically rich film – a blend of fiction and reality – also explores various levels of intimacy and sharing, and at times dares to engage in an entertaining polemic with traditional macho culture.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: The action horror film Project Wolf Hunting is not another of the genre mash-ups that Korean cinema is famous for. Instead, this tale of a prisoner ship that is also carrying a far more dangerous cargo is a straight-forward genre film at its core. A guilty pleasure full of bloody special effects and brutal action sequences that evolve in the second half into a struggle against a superhumanly strong and extremely tenacious opponent. The filmmakers have nevertheless managed to tell their simple and unrelentingly hardcore tale in a meticulously crafted style that most similar B-movie projects can only dream of.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Midnight Screenings); production year 2022

films.syn: An ageing footballer looks back on his career and wonders whether it is right to focus attention on the usefulness of the game or on its aesthetic qualities. What do the terraces want? And what would Croatian midfielder Robert Prosinečki have to say about it? An experimental film which dismisses the idea of football as ballet and instead presents it as a chaotic dance.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2023

films.syn: Forensic pathologist and anthropologist Cristina Cattaneo performs autopsies every day on nameless bodies, many of them of homeless people, sex workers, and others from the margins of society. But she also increasingly has to deal with the bodies of migrants washed up on Italy’s shores by the Mediterranean Sea. Determining their identity is all the more difficult since many travel without documents. This humanist documentary asks whether the dead have human rights and deserve dignity. With the growing number of anonymous bodies, however, it would seem that the only person asking this question is Cristina.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: The day Kelly-Anne has been waiting for has arrived. The trial begins for Ludovic Chevalier, accused of the brutal murder of three underage girls. Unlike most people, Kelly-Anne is fascinated by the man, she becomes obsessed with him and attends every single court hearing in the hope he’ll give her at least a fleeting glance. The border between reality and fantasy starts to blur, however, until Kelly-Anne ceases to be a mere passive observer. Pascal Plante once again expresses an interest in female subjectivity, nevertheless, this time he has come up with an arthouse thriller about the perilous attraction of evil. At the same time, the interplay between what we can and can’t see, and what is explicit and what is conjecture, develops into an almost physical viewing experience.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: It’s the year 2041, and humanity has reached the point where it can cheat death. Anyone who dies an unnatural death has the right to be brought back to life. All you have to do is to create a backup of your personality – a restore point – at least every forty-eight hours. But there exists a movement of people who try to sabotage this concept. Agent Em finds herself drawn into a case that is not as simple as it first seemed and the consequences of which reach to the highest levels of politics. Director Robert Hloz’s feature film debut is a gripping tale, an extraordinarily inventive visual experience, and a polemic with the idea that technological progress is always a good thing.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2023

films.syn: Michal was born with a cleft palate. Ondra comes from a socially disadvantaged family. Both are twelve, and neither fits in with their peers. Seeking to finally escape the role of outsiders, they have decided to undergo a rite of passage to join the local street gang. Together, they have one afternoon to prove to the gang that they deserve their respect. But the enticing adventure quickly turns into an initiation rite into adulthood.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: The saffron-colored robes of Buddhist monks shimmer against the lush green jungle. In the background, the buzzing of insects blends with the rushing of a waterfall and the sound of meditation bowls. And all along, one soul prepares to leave its body and set out on its future journey. In a calm tone devoid of fear or anxiety, Samsara guides us through a meditation on death and dying. The film’s exceptional sensitivity and documentary-like persuasiveness are outdone perhaps only by the boldness to ask viewers to close their eyes for a part of the screening and to let themselves be carried away by a stream of non-visual sensations. The film won the Special Jury Award in the Encounters competition at this year’s Berlinale. ​Warning: This film contains flashing lights which may not be suitable for photosensitive epilepsy.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Mína is quietly playing with her Toy in the sand box. But the terrible Totems invade and, in the blink of an eye, Toy is the victim of a kidnapping. Mína does not give up, however, and launches a daring plan to save her friend.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: “JLG is like a sun, as soon as you get too close to it, you burn. If you ignore it, you miss the light​.” Respected Swiss director Thomas Imbach on the “God of Cinema” who, as both man and filmmaker, has kept him spellbound his whole life. Chancing upon images of the ailing grand master, he was inspired to set off on foot on a pilgrimage from Lakes Zurich to Geneva to pay tribute to Godard and to attempt to persuade the latter to film with him. An original and playful diary filmed on an iPhone and on 35mm during the trip, where loyal pilgrim Imbach looks back at his own career and conducts a dialogue with his magnetic role model. A road movie conceived – literally, “on his own two feet” – as an informed Godard masterclass about perceiving the world through cinema and much else besides.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2023

films.t: Scream of My Blood: A Gogol Bordello Story
films.syn: Twenty-five years ago, New York’s Lower East Side was rocked by the phenomenon known as Gogol Bordello. These now world-renowned pioneers of gypsy punk famed for their explosive concerts are headed by the charismatic legend Eugene Hütz, who is also the main protagonist of this gripping documentary portrait. With Gogol Bordello, the Ukrainian-born world traveler with Romany roots has created a unique multicultural band founded on the shared immigrant experience and specific music of each band member – be they from Ecuador, Ethiopia, Belarus, or Russia. The artistic and political urgency so typical for Gogol Bordello and their frontman has become invaluable in the latest chapter in the band’s history – the musical struggle against Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2023

films.syn: Jirka and Aneta are a young couple who enjoy the routine of their quiet relationship and are in no hurry to make big decisions in life. One night in their inherited flat, the doorbell rings and standing at the door is Jirka’s mother Valerie. An initially brief call turns into a never-ending visit from an intense and caustic diva whose presence fundamentally disrupts the couple’s privacy. Certainties are shaken, boundaries broken. Although the film’s directorial duo works with a familiar premise, they subvert any dark humor with a sense of tension more commonly found in horror movies, all of it wrapped in the penetrating question: Is the mother’s unbearable smothering legitimate or are mothers sometimes the biggest monsters of all?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2023

films.syn: Stoic determination, resilience, bravery, equanimity, and tenacity of purpose – these are the characteristics of sisu, a concept that Finns associate with their “national character.” In the eponymous film, these qualities are embodied by a gruff man of few words capable of brutally and efficiently killing Nazis. Sisu is a survivalist action film stripped down to the bone in which a tired unit of Nazis at the end of the war fights a lone but practically indestructible gold prospector. A wildly exaggerated feast of blood and suffering, the film is part Western and part ironic Finnish answer to the dated action flicks of Sylvester Stallone et al.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Midnight Screenings); production year 2022

films.syn: One day, dancer Elena meets the sign-language interpreter Dovydas. She feels comfortable with him, as if she’s known him for a long time – and yet the bond that forms between them is like nothing she has experienced before… In her sophomore outing, director Marija Kavtaradze explores the themes of closeness and intimacy between two people in a relationship that defies stereotypes, expectations, and simple definitions, doing so with a remarkable tenderness, delicacy, and understanding for her protagonists and their feelings. Slow premiered in competition at Sundance, where it was enthusiastically welcomed by audiences and reviewers and also took home the Directing Award.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2023

films.syn: During its 2012 election campaign titled “Smiling Georgia,” the governing party promised its country’s poorest residents new teeth in exchange for their vote. Dentists began to pull people’s decayed teeth, but after the election defeat, the trusting public never received their new pearly whites… In his bitterly humorous documentary, Luka Beradze takes us to a sleepy Georgian village, introduces us to its inhabitants, and shows that it rarely pays to believe the promises of populist politicians and to vote for purely selfish reasons. In the broader context, the film asks questions regarding the value of ordinary people in the eyes of political leaders.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2023

films.syn: This loose adaptation of Joseph Conrad’s Heart of Darkness follows Robert Klein (Stanislav Majer) as he sets out to find his brother, who disappeared under mysterious circumstances. Klein finds himself on a journey where nothing is familiar or certain, a journey during which he is forced to reassess his relationship to his culture, to himself, and to his brother, whom he thought he knew so well… David Jařab’s latest film is a highly original exploration of the conflict of cultures that we are permanently forced to reckon with, about the patriarchal superiority of the “white man,” and about the right to plunder natural resources that are slowly but surely running out.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2023

films.t: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
films.syn: The heroes of the first and, to this day, most popular feature-length film to emerge from the Walt Disney Studio – which celebrates its 100th anniversary this year – deservedly won a unique Academy Award, consisting of one full-size statuette and seven accompanying miniature Oscars. Put more precisely, the awards went to the film’s animators, who set in motion over a million drawings in such a way that each dwarf has his own distinctive character, expressed not only in diverse physical features, but also in the very manner he is brought to life. They are all presented here in richly varied pantomime; also dazzling is the choreography of poetic forest scenes inhabited by a multitude of little creatures. The flawless craft of this cartoon masterpiece draws admiration even in an era of computer animation.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1937

films.syn: Chiloé Island off the southern coast of Chile, late 19th century. A 13-year-old indigenous girl named Rosa (the phenomenal Valentina Véliz Caileo) is forced to witness a German colonist brutally attacking her father. This story of the revenge of an aggrieved daughter, who renounces her Christian upbringing and strays towards a cult of her ancestors propagating witchcraft and rebellion, enjoyed a huge reception during its world premiere at Sundance this year. Christopher Murray provided one of the most rousing experiences of the festival; his mesmeric spectacle is, at the same time, an intriguing commentary on the folly of colonising aggressors, who chance upon the magic-infused bond between the original inhabitants and their natural surroundings.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: A mother squirrel tries to gather as many acorns as possible for the winter. But her twin children would rather play ball. What's it gonna be: fun or duty?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: Twenty-seven-year-old Anna lives with her mother Hana in a small town on the Slovak-Hungarian border. Hana tries to protect her daughter so that she will not repeat her own mistakes in life, but instead of earning her daughter’s gratitude, Hana’s actions fill Anna with a sense of frustration and lack of fulfilment. When the young Gergej enters her life, mother and daughter are forced to reassess their relationship… Slovak director Monika Mahútová’s stylistically inventive graduate film looks at the bond between mother and daughter with understanding and subtle humor.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2022

films.syn: Another dreary day in a small town. Viki, Sára, and Kiki, three inseparable friends since childhood, are planning to spend their free afternoon the same way they always do: vodka, cigarettes, talking about everything and nothing. But their group dynamic is different today, more explosive: one of them has reached the second round in a casting call for a modeling job, thus raising her chances of leaving this place of dashed hopes and dreams. Her friends might be willing to support her, if only their anger, sadness, and envy weren’t so powerful… A relentless but non-judgmental look at growing up without any prospects of a brighter future.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2023

films.syn: Little Suzie likes to visit her family’s plot in a nearby garden allotment. There’s something interesting going on in each of the little gardens, but the one right at the back seems to be shrouded in mystery – a mystery the little girl decides to unveil.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: Seventeen-year-old Suzume lives a quiet life on Kyushu Island, until she discovers a mysterious door standing in some ruins outside town. Suspicious objects appearing in films are best ignored, however – especially if they are guarded by a cute little animal… Makoto Shinkai’s fantasy tale about a catastrophe of unprecedented proportions was inspired by the tough experience of the Japanese tragedy in 2011. The film combines a disaster of epic proportions with a quirky, almost mischievous coming-of-age drama. After the successes of Belle at Cannes and Inu-Oh in Venice, this year Suzume brought Japanese animation back to the Berlinale, where it was shown in the main competition and immediately earned a reputation as the anime event of the year.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: Arine’s difficult financial situation forces her to return to her hometown, where she takes a job interpreting between a farm’s seasonal workers from Guatemala and their Canadian employers. Although she is supposed to remain impartial, when she repeatedly witnesses the migrant workers’ mistreatment, she cannot remain silent. She may possibly be the only person who sees them as more than wage laborers – for they are above all human beings. Pier-Philippe Chevigny’s self-assured debut is a gripping tale of injustice that emphasizes the importance of compassion and the determination to fight for what is right. In fact, it is empathy that has the power to unite us instead of dividing us.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2023

films.syn: Eric, Rachel, Maggie. Three siblings once connected by a strong bond, which was then broken by the process of growing up and separation. Eric repeatedly avoids any debate about the past, yet when he takes a brief trip back home, he can’t escape confrontation with his sisters. What’s more, the thought of getting together with his old poker group is too enticing for him to leave as planned. This acidly comic yet sorrowful sibling drama relies on a prosaic visual language and offers a subtle insight into complex family constellations, where there is love but no functional tools of communication. Is it possible to address the past through our childhood selves? After all, we don’t have to give up our children’s games in adulthood, or do we?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: The near future is the setting for the film which had the privilege of opening this year’s Un Certain Regard competition in Cannes. At first glance, it doesn’t appear all that different from our reality – so long as you overlook the mysterious phenomenon whereby part of the population mutates into human-animal hybrids. The creatures regarded as a threat are kept in isolation, away from “normal” people.
