These latter include the agreeably wacky François and his 16-year-old son Émile (the outstanding Romain Duris and Paul Kircher), who leave Paris and head for a small provincial town, where a centre has been set up for “the Others”… The spectacular and the intimate naturally coexist in an emotionally persuasive film that serves as an original contribution to the debate on human apathy towards the environment.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: The world of automobile espionage serves as a springboard for Masumura’s study of the decadence of post-war corporate Japan and the passing of imperialist DNA into self-serving manufactures in this highly suspenseful, deeply cynical noir. Asahina (Jirô Tamiya) is the ambitious young member of a spy team working for Tiger, a mega automobile firm, which is about to launch its latest deluxe sports model, the Pioneer. After a series of mishaps, the Tiger group realize that their staunch rival, Yamato, may have planted a mole in the company. A breathless cat-and-mouse game ensues – replete with double-crossings, triple-crossings, and capricious twists – which ultimately exposes the extent of industrial corruption.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Yasuzô Masumura); production year 1962

films.syn: With bankruptcy looming, Daiei, the pioneering Japanese film company where Masumura worked for most of his career, was seeking a commercial hit that would turn its fortunes around. With sexploitation in vogue at the time, Masumura was tasked to adapt a scandalous 1931 novel by crime writer Rampo Edogawa. The result was The Blind Beast, an erotic drama now ranked as Masumura’s last masterwork. He delivers a claustrophobic chamber piece centering on a blind sculptor (Eiji Funakoshi) who, with the aid of his mother (Noriko Sengoku), kidnaps an aspiring virginal model (Mako Midori) in order to create the world’s most sensorial sculpture. The Blind Beast is part pink film and part arthouse horror, with references to Baudelaire, the Marquis de Sade, and Hume’s evolutionary ethics.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Yasuzô Masumura); production year 1969

films.syn: Cape Verde as the setting for the archetypal tale of three sisters, who were separated by the eruption of the country’s “Peak of Fire”, the volcano Pico do Fogo. Left to the quirky imagination of Pedro Costa, however, the dramatic contours of the story swiftly crumble. A molten cinematic performance, engulfed by an inner flame, which sometimes warms us, while at other times it burns us.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2023

films.syn: Román, a bank clerk, hatches a plan which also requires the input of his colleague Morán. The aim is to put an end to backbreaking routine and start living a life of freedom, without the depressing need to keep on worrying about material concerns. But they can’t do this without committing an offence. A sensation at this year’s Cannes film fest, this stylish fresco is reminiscent in its structure of an unputdownable novel. The chiselled homage to 1970s American and French genre flicks doesn’t waste time moralising. Established Argentinian filmmaker Rodrigo Moreno offers up a crime caper with an existential overlap, sketched with a light hand slyly gesturing to Brecht’s maxim, namely that it’s a worse crime to establish a bank than to rob one.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: The vocabulary of documentary cinema has countless dialects, and one of the most compelling is spoken by Tatiana Huezo. Karlovy Vary audiences could previously see her films Tempestad and Prayers for the Stolen, both of which explored systematic injustice in Mexico – the first as a documentary, the second through a fictional narrative. With The Echo, which won the Documentary Award at this year’s Berlinale, Huezo once again explores the same landscape. This time, however, she poeticizes not suffering, but the most ordinary existence. Her film is a cinematic visit to the countryside, a place where people live in harmony with animals and where old and young look after one another. It is a film as warm as an unexpected embrace or a kind word from a caring grandmother.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Paris, 1887. Duels have been officially outlawed but are still regular practice. For many, they are the only way to defend their honor. Fencing master Clément Lacaze tries in vain to prevent his nephew from engaging in an uneven duel with the more experienced Colonel Berchère. Marie-Rose Astié de Valsayre, a feminist fighting for women’s equality, tries to show that honor is not just a male affair. Actor and director Vincent Perez’s historical film makes excellent use of various forms of duels – with épées, pistols, and sabres on horseback.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: “At least if I died tomorrow, you knew that I was here.” One of the many disarming statements voiced by the singular Irish actor, poet and singer Richard Harris (1930 - 2002), of whom it’s easy to speak in superlatives. Forty inimitable years full of fabulous and controversial moments from his private and professional life, dating from Harris’s iconic roles in the dramas This Sporting Life and Red Desert, to the wisdom, tenderness and dignity with which he imbued his Marcus Aurelius in Gladiator and Albus Dumbledore in the first two Harry Potter films. Seasoned filmmaker Adrian Sibley adopts an original approach to address the conventions of the documentary portrait, among others, assisted by Harris’s sons, Jared, Jamie and Damian.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 2022

films.syn: It’s summer and a group of young women head off for a week to a house in the country in order to rehearse a play. In the peace and quiet of their natural surroundings, which provide a refuge from the intense heat of the sun, the women go through the text and dress up in their ruched period costumes, while in easy conversation they share their secrets, and also have little adventures. This enchanting debut by Itsaso Arana, who co-wrote and starred in August Virgin (Official Selection – Competition, KVIFF 2019), provides an opportunity to stop for a moment, to breathe in the warm air and settle back in the open embrace of this company of women. After all, what kind of summer would it be without girls, a campfire, songs and a touch of magic?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: André and Vera are both life and business partners trying to get a women’s reproductive health mobile app off the ground. On the eve of a weekend programme for promising start-ups, where they aim to attract the attention of potential investors, Vera tries hypnotherapy to help her quit smoking. However, the experience comes with an unexpected side effect: she starts to lose all her social inhibitions. Ernst De Geer’s debut is a fresh, modern satire which profits from situational humour and piercingly precise dialogue. At the same time, the irony of what’s going on is plain to see. An individualistic society may well encourage us to be ourselves, nevertheless, it remains uncompromising in its demands as to how we ought to behave.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: Fred and Luisa have built their relationship on a foundation of equality and on rejecting outdated gender roles. But their beliefs are put to the test when it comes time to say “I do.” Not only must they face the clash of cultures resulting from the meeting of two families from two different continents, but they must also contend with the power of wedding traditions, which catch the couple-to-be off guard and make them strangers at their own wedding. In her relationship study, Sophia Mocorrea focuses on the struggle of the individual against social pressures that one can never entirely escape. She does so in an uncompromising manner, with a camera that gets up close and personal to her characters – so that not a single glimmer of love or doubt eludes her.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2022

films.syn: Enrico Ghezzi – film critic, populariser of arthouse cinema, film philosopher, journalist and also filmmaker – is just as important for Italian cinema as Rossellini, Visconti or Bertolucci. After viewing this three-hour-plus autobiographical magnum opus, on which the ageing and ailing bard collaborated with Alessandro Gagliardo, many will regard this assertion as less controversial. Ghezzi’s highly intellectual and, at the same time, elemental quest to discover life in film and film in life is reminiscent of an erupting volcano and prowling beast of prey; the sophisticated chain of spellbinding moments from across the history of film (Ferrara, Tarr, Straub-Huillet, Parajanov, Bene, Tsukamoto) is intersected with scenes from Ghezzi’s private life, whose intimacy is left undisturbed. An invaluable gift for current and future cinephiles.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2022

films.syn: A film within a film, a comedy and a drama, a feature and a documentary combined. The second directorial effort from Kiarostami’s pupil Faeze Azizkhani is all of these and more besides. Two women – a director and a screenwriter – are putting together a film which is highly personal for both of them, albeit a process which arouses the animosity of their families and a society that favours men; the women’s creative endeavour is a scourge for everyone concerned. Every single word in the written screenplay is the subject of discussion, while the scene of the pre-shoot preparations becomes a battlefield of aggression blurring the boundary between reality and fiction. Yet it is this conflict that provides fertile ground for the director’s authentic female perspective.

ap.p: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now); production year 2021

films.syn: Ten-year-old Audrey and her three siblings find themselves abandoned in an old house, where they were meant to be spending their summer holidays with their dad, but he disappears suddenly during the night. Initially, the kids wait in vain for him to come back, but they soon realise they’ll have to take care of themselves, which nonetheless won’t be easy. The forest surrounding the secluded house doesn’t seem to want to let the little castaways through, and bizarre things start to happen, especially after dark. Mysterious monsters afraid of the light, tunnels where time is simply lost – the youngsters have to face all this in a fantastical drama which unites the terror and distress of children and adults alike, sensations that, alas, can’t be relieved merely by shining a torch on them.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: One of the first propaganda films ever made, A noi! was shot in 1922 and covered the March on Rome, an important event in the rise of Italian fascism. A hundred years later, cinephile and documentarian Mark Cousins revisits this film and deconstructs its cinematic techniques, which are still effective today. Benito Mussolini didn’t even have to participate in the march of the blackshirts – it was enough for him to appear in a documentary about it. In his audiovisual essay, Cousins places the event and its visual depiction into historical, political, and cinematic contexts. Through actress Alba Rohrwacher, he presents the viewpoint of ordinary Italians.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: “I despise people who suffer in silence.” Alexandre is unemployed but he’s still full of opinions and impressions. He lives in an apartment with the older Marie, who owns a boutique. One day at a café he meets Veronika, a nurse. It gradually becomes clear, however, that one bed is too cramped for three people. This monumental yet, at the same time, almost painfully intimate exploration of the relationships between men and women takes place in the cafés and bedrooms of Paris. The spontaneous dialogues and, in particular, the monologues, flow freely like the smoke from cigarettes. Jean-Pierre Léaud again serves as the director’s alter ego, this time in Jean Eustache’s most celebrated film.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1973

films.syn: “Why don’t I have any photographs from my childhood?” This question marks the beginning of Moroccan director Asmae El Moudir’s search for family secrets, which won her the directing award in the Un Certain Regard section at this year’s Cannes Film Festival. Asmae reconstructs her family history with the help of her entire family. Just for the film, her father built a miniature reconstruction of the neighborhood where the family lived, and her mother sewed scarves for figures representing family, friends, and neighbors. As a result, everybody is suddenly confronted with a view of their younger selves – and with a past they had wanted to hide behind lies that, even when repeated a thousand times, could never become truth.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: A peaceful life without sex is better than a relationship which is all passion and arguments. That’s Xavier’s opinion yet, as soon becomes obvious, his view is certainly not shared by Sophia, his partner of several years. One afternoon she finds she can’t resist the electrifying magnetism of Sylvain, an unselfconscious maintenance man, who is hired to renovate their weekend house. What follows is an instant sexual rapport, coupled with an explosion of suppressed desire. Monia Chokri turns a film about love into a searingly brisk tragicomedy offering a fresh perspective on the shortcomings of monogamy; likewise she chooses the woman as the subject through which we experience eroticism and sensuality in the film.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.t: The Other Side of the Farmland
films.syn: Alcohol, folk costumes, dancing, and confronting unpleasant truths – all this awaits young Eliška when she gets stuck at a mysterious inn. Now she has to find an answer to the question of whether death is the end or just the beginning.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: A soup is boiling in a copper pot, a firmly clenched knife is chopping green herbs, and not far away a turbot is soaking in white wine. It is 1885, and a large home in the Loire Valley is awakening to a fresh morning. Famed gourmand Dodin is overflowing with fresh culinary recipes, which his faithful cook Eugénie turns into reality. Their perfectly balanced meals testify to their mutual understanding of more than a thousand gestures, and Dodin would like for Eugénie to become his wife. But his proposal threatens her independence. This sensual homage to French gastronomy and restrained romance spiced up by the purest form of love won Best Director at Cannes.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Monsters, magic, miracles, life-and-death struggles, revenge, true love. Rob Reiner’s cult classic The Princess Bride embraces all the elements of the traditional fairy tale but strips its characters of the naivete typical of the genre. With a sense of lightness and ironic distance, it recounts the fantastic adventures of the beautiful Princess Buttercup (Robin Wright) and the Dread Pirate Roberts (Cary Elwes) in a tale full of mischievous, absurd, touching, and chilling moments – all with an outstanding cast of actors. Besides the enchanting Robin Wright, the film also brought international fame to the “gentle giant,” André the Giant.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Robin Wright); production year 1987

films.syn: Life on a farm is quiet and somewhat monotonous, but even here a meteor could strike. Young adoptee Carl feels equally out of place, and should he ever forget, there’s always someone (even distant family members) willing to subtly remind him of it. His adoptive parents mean well, but the family doesn’t talk much about things. He is expected to take over the farm one day, but he would much rather get to know his native Korea. A gently reassuring film about the need to fit in, nostalgically shot on 16mm film.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Of the 55 features Masumura directed, The Red Angel is his most celebrated outside Japan – a film that has been amassing a sizeable cult following over the past decade. Set at the peak of the Sino-Japanese War, Ayako Wakao – in her most memorable performance – plays Sakura, a young nurse who is transformed from a rape victim into the titular angel when she starts gifting her patients with sexual relief before their inevitable death. The horrors of war – depicted in disturbingly graphic details unmatched by any other Masumura pic – are front and center here, but it’s the relationship between female agency and love/sex that emerges as the real preoccupation of the film. More than sixty years after its release, the power of The Red Angel has not waned.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Yasuzô Masumura); production year 1966

films.syn: Milo lives in a home for wayward girls. While the other residents struggle with their problematic behavior, Milo is fighting a much bigger battle, for they are seeking to transition behind the walls of the institution. The only person who notices their change and is supportive is Nicki, an attendant at the home who is Milo’s male role model and also the person onto whom they project their desired identity. But the institution’s walls are too thin for Milo not to hear a rumor that turns their life upside down. More than an exploration of the fragile nature of gender identity, The Shift above all looks at the importance of having a source of support at times when our perception of ourselves is changing.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2022

films.syn: The debut from the Ark brothers, hotly anticipated since 2017, when they won a Cinéfondation prize at Cannes for their short piece AniMal. This stirring film demonstrates the extraordinary talent of its makers; the characters and their story are captured with an almost scalding intensity, precisely in line with the creed of its directors, who regard the film as “the skin in which we live”. Only by confronting the sins committed by members of his family and the curse which has plagued them for generations can the hero attempt to deflect the evil spirits that threaten his mother. An innovative fantasy horror flick blending genre elements with local folk legend.

ap.p: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now); production year 2020

films.syn: For many years Rocío thought her mother Alba was dead but now she reunites with her for the first time since her childhood. She wants to tell her that she is pregnant. Alba, however, suffers trauma from the war she experienced firsthand and has stopped talking. While Rocío searches for a way to communicate with her mother, people in the vicinity are dying and tension is growing in the face of an uncertain future. For her feature debut Camila Rodríguez Triana drew on her familiarity with visual art and documentary filmmaking, conceiving the piece as an oppressive audiovisual work, in which the nightmarish events are kept out of shot. This intimate study of maternal love thus unfolds in a powerful atmosphere of fear and distress induced by a premonition of evil.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: Long before the modern female revenge genre came into existence, there was The Spider Tattoo, Masumura’s mysterious, ferocious Edo-era fable. Ayako Wakao is Otsuya, the daughter of a wealthy merchant who gets kidnapped and forced into prostitution. A demented tattoo artist engraves a large, black, human-faced spider on her back that turns her into a murderess, hell-bent on annihilating the men who abused her. A star-studded collaboration adapted from renowned author Jun’ichirō Tanizaki's novel by writer-director Kaneto Shindô (The Naked Island, Onibaba) and photographed by the legendary Kazuo Miyagawa (Rashomon, Ugetsu) in entrancing, sumptuous Eastmancolor, The Spider Tattoo is Masumura’s most visually striking film.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Yasuzô Masumura); production year 1966

films.syn: A barren, sun-scorched desert. In the middle of nowhere stands a cage with a dark-skinned woman locked inside. Day turns to night, yet the woman appears to be waiting with infinite patience for someone to come and rescue her. In vain. On the verge of exhaustion, she decides to take her fate into her own hands and to set out on a journey through a dystopian world that seems to have lost all sense of humanity. Dutch-born Australian director Rolf de Heer composes haunting images through which he meditates on the cruelty of life in a segregated society while also telling a thrilling adventure of the wanderings of a “pure soul” in a story full of twists and turns and a surprisingly subtle sense of humor.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: The Sweet East, the directorial debut of cinematographer Sean Price Williams (e.g., the Safdie brothers’ Good Time), is a genre-defying indictment of the idealistic image the United States has of itself. High school student Lillian (rising star Talia Ryder) abandons a school trip under dramatic circumstances – and apparently leaves her old identity behind. From that moment on, she becomes whoever it is people see in her on her aimless wanderings. An ironic commentary of contemporary life in the United States, the film is also a dig at the country’s indie film scene – all with the help of postmodern references to, among other things, Edgar Allan Poe.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.t: The Truth Is All There Is
films.syn: Screenwriter, director, poet, essayist, and university teacher Eduard Grečner turns ninety-two this year. This documentary profile gives him the main word, and despite his age he manages very precisely to outline the salient features and common denominator underlying all stages in his career. Numerous Slovak film historians similarly reflect on these periods, and they confirm that Grečner’s enduring efforts at achieving a “truthfulness of expression” were of great importance for Slovak cinema. His work helped to overcome the rigidity of socialist realism, it introduced existential themes, and responded critically to contemporary events in society.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 2023

films.syn: To mark the fiftieth anniversary of the death of Bruce Lee, the Karlovy Vary film festival is screening one of the most important action films in the history of cinema. The Way of the Dragon is the third and most distinctive of the Hong Kong films that made Lee an international star. Unlike The Big Boss or Fist of Fury, it is set not in Asia but in Rome, where Lee's character comes to the aid of his relatives against a mafia syndicate. From today’s perspective, the film is a survey of Lee’s iconic scenes, including his screams imitating the meowing of cats and his final battle against Chuck Norris in the Colosseum. For this outing, Lee sat in the director’s chair as well and thus had full control over his last film.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Midnight Screenings); production year 1972

films.t: The Way Through the Bleak Woods
films.syn: A strongly lyrical, quasi-balladic black-and-white piece that acquaints us with fragments of the lives of people from a small village hidden in the depths of the Bohemian Forest. The characters appear to move about in a state of timelessness; their inner solitude, frustrated desires, and the sense that they are condemned to perpetual wandering do not inspire hope that they will find a way out. The visually powerful leitmotif of the sylvan labyrinth, in which paths disappear between the tall trees or beneath a mantle of snow, thus acquires symbolic value. News of the outbreak of World War I at the end of the film only heightens the bleakness of the message conveyed by documentarist Ivan Vojnár in his feature film directorial debut.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1997

films.syn: Masumura has directed various unsettling films about women, and The Wife’s Confession is his greatest: a courtroom drama/film noir/melodrama about a young wife Ayako (Ayako Wakao) who stands trial for the suspected murder of her abusive husband during a fateful mountaineering accident. Whether Ayako was attempting to save herself or deliberately murder her husband becomes the central mystery around which Masumura concocts his treatise on the consequences of free will, the vanity and phoniness of self-sacrifice, and the hypocrisy of a patriarchy unchanged by the promise of a post-war capitalist boom. Anchored by one of the most fascinating femme fatales of all film noirs, The Wife’s Confession is Masumura’s most morally and emotionally complex picture.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Yasuzô Masumura); production year 1961

films.syn: Dumitru dreams of traveling far beyond the horizon, to the America of his dreams, so he and a friend stow away on a trans-oceanic freighter. Dumitru is quickly discovered by the Filipino sailor Joel, who is thus faced with a difficult decision. The uncompromising Taiwanese officers do not tolerate stowaways, but Joel’s steadfast religious beliefs tell him to help those in need… With this ambitious debut inspired by true events from 1996, Romanian director Mihai Mincan has produced a hypnotic thriller about the strength of faith, morality, and fearing for one’s life. The film premiered in the Orizzonti section at last year’s Venice Film Festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.t: Trailer of the Film That Will Never Exist: "Phony Wars"
films.ot: Annonce du film qui n'existera jamais: "Drôles de guerres"
films.syn: The announcement of the death of Jean-Luc Godard last September came like a bolt from the blue, since, as in the case of figures such as David Bowie, we simply regarded this exceptional artist as immortal. The decades-long, unrelenting quest within his oeuvre for new definitions, and his explosive and, at the same time, profoundly intellectual polemic with the world as well as with himself, likewise pulsate through this 20-minute piece, one of JLG’s last creative eruptions before his death by assisted suicide. This work will be screened together with another new production, the exclusive archive film compilation Godard by Godard.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 2023

films.syn: Boushra, a Syrian girl who works picking potatoes in Lebanon, returns from a long day in the fields, only to learn that, today, her childhood will come to an end.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2021

films.syn: Preparations for a birthday celebration in a multi-generational household are accompanied by confusion, bickering, and the sounds of children and animals. But joy is mixed with a quiet sorrow, for this will probably be the celebrant’s last birthday. Director Lila Avilés invites us into a busy home that feels more like a vibrant ecosystem than a human dwelling. Her tirelessly roaming film hews to the perspective of seven-year-old Sol, who despite her small size sometimes sees farther than the adults. With Tótem, it is not enough to just peek inside – one must tune into the film’s natural tempo of everyday life, in which the hours flow like the seasons of the year.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.t: Umberto Eco –⁠ A Library of the World
films.ot: Umberto Eco –⁠ La biblioteca del mondo
films.syn: A cinematic monument, erected as an homage to a man who was fascinated with history and with the miracle of human communication. Told in various chapters, Ferrario’s film takes us on a tour of the mental world of a man whose insatiable sense of amazement and insightful intellect ensured his legacy in Western culture not just as a leading academic but also as a widely recognized author of fiction. The director intersperses archival footage with a tour of Eco’s famous personal library, interviews with members of his family, and excerpts from his writings, while also touching on themes that have taken on greater importance since Eco’s death in 2016.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.t: Watch the Fire or Burn Inside It
films.ot: Il faut regarder le feu ou brûler dedans
films.syn: If everything around us is heading for extinction, are we just going to stare at the fire or are we going to start one? A naivist, fanciful piece with documentary elements which follows a woman who, to the sound of pop and the experimental saxophone of Bendik Giske, starts fires in Corsica and, through the medium of film, changes our perspective as we witness things familiar to us only from news reports.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2022

films.syn: Amidst a thriving Baťa-esque town, nestled in the scenic foothills of the majestic Tatra mountains, stands a factory, whose young director is, for his day (it's 1937), pleasingly modern in approach. Yet, don’t be fooled, the film’s protagonist is actually his wife Helena (Eliška Křenková). The aspiring doctor is soon to give birth, yet her resolute gaze into her family’s rosy future is suddenly darkened by the discovery of the body of a newborn baby in the vibrant factory's courtyard. Helena’s innate empathy, intensified by her pregnancy, isn’t satisfied by the conspicuously prompt solution to the mystery. A stirring detective drama with a progressive and profoundly human perspective on a theme controversial not only shortly before the unexpected war, but also decades later.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: Eva returns to her home village with a large block of ice hidden in the back of her car. How does this relate to her memories of the long-ago sunny summer that changed her life for good? Established Belgian actress Veerle Baetens makes her directorial debut with an adaptation of Lize Spit’s bestselling novel The Melting – the story of a young woman for whom one summer vacation culminates in a painful transition from childhood to premature adulthood. The film, whose strength rests in a carefully constructed contrast between the carefree summer atmosphere and the cruelty that people are capable of inflicting on one another, premiered at this year’s Sundance Film Festival, where it received a Jury Award for Best Actress.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.ot: Kapag wala na ang mga alon
films.syn: Pearly waves wash away the last remnants of Filipino innocence, the sun’s rays are replaced by a foreboding night, and two men approach one another in the eternal silence of an exotic landscape. Lieutenant Hermes and Sergeant Macabantay were once members of the government’s most effective tool in its war on drugs, but these enforcers of the law have become victims of their own conscience and enemies awaiting a day of reckoning. Lav Diaz’s Dumas-esque epic speaks to viewers like a hypnotic danse macabre, with the director masterfully weaving together a noir aesthetic with Western tropes while challenging the questionable regime of President Duterte and the sick morality of a country with a habit of glorifying its criminals.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2022

films.syn: “…You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going,” Jesus tells Nicodemus (The Gospel According to St John, 3:8). This subtly pervasive film by Marco Righi presents a provocative and exceptionally mesmeric interpretation of a key passage in the New Testament. In a small village somewhere in the Apennines, taciturn Antimo divides his time between the local church, his tedious work on the farm and his chaste meetings with his girlfriend. His pivotal encounter with the wild loner Lazzaro awakens in the devout young man the desire to reach the very core of a faith far removed from the regular Sunday sermons delivered by a representative of the Church – a powerful institution for which freethinking and devotion to God represent incompatible ideas.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: Budapest, 2123. All plant and animal life has died out. Humanity is living inside a plastic-roofed dome whose inhabitants must pay a high price for survival: When they are fifty years old, they must allow themselves to be injected with a seed that will turn them into trees to provide society with food and oxygen. When Nora, the 32-year-old wife of psychiatrist Stefan, decides to end her life and to donate her body, her husband decides to go against the system in order to save her. An animated dystopian odyssey featuring evocative images of the inhospitable landscape “out there,” White Plastic Sky stands out for its urgent environmental message.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Alexandre O. Philippe is famous for his analytical documentaries about iconic works of cinema. This time around, he trains his lens on William Shatner, who left his mark on popular culture among other things as Captain James T. Kirk of Star Trek. As he looks back on his career, the television great known for captivating work with his own voice goes far beyond sharing tales from the set. You Can Call Me Bill presents the testimony of a man who intensely feels his own mortality and by the force of his personality and talent manages not only to endure this situation, but also to convey its weight.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 2023

films.t: You Sing Loud, I Sing Louder
films.syn: Beauty and tenderness hidden behind subtlety. A father and his twenty-year-old daughter, two people who have been separated from each other for too long, set out on a trip from San Diego to New Mexico. After years apart, they try to re-establish their relationship through the daughter’s problems with addiction. With every passing mile, they find that they have more in common than just a weakness for sweets. This road movie’s charismatic duo is portrayed by Ewan McGregor and his daughter Clara, and the two manage to imbue their characters with an inimitable charm and authenticity. A drama full of subtle humor and parental love, You Sing Loud, I Sing Louder had its premiere at SXSW.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Ewan McGregor); production year 2022

films.syn: The third outing for Danesh Eghbashavi was filmed with two iPhones, a small hand-held camera, a GoPro action camera, and the appreciable influence of Roger Corman. This rousing genre blend of comedy, detective story and mockumentary demonstrates that, even in the present day, independent film can incorporate aspects of the revolutionary gesture. In a brisk and complex way it tells a story which might suggest it was filmed by its protagonists as a live broadcast. The sophisticated narrative composition is akin to the process of opening out Chinese nested boxes – the characters know what is going to happen and they provide the appropriate commentary as well. Archive shots are also added to the mix. An explosive world premiere.

ap.p: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Another Birth. Iranian Cinema Here and Now); production year 2023

films.syn: Alexei is released on parole after fifteen years in prison. But the sweet scent of freedom is poisoned by an enduring sense of guilt that keeps him from growing closer to his daughter, who in the meantime has become a prostitute. Rinaldas Tomaševičius’s social drama looks at the difficulty of making up for lost time and finding one’s place in a new, dark, grainy, and fragmentary reality. The film lends a voice to antagonistic figures rejected by society, awakening their emotions and exploring their chances for a new beginning. Clear and empathetic, it presents us with the important message that even an antagonist can become a hero.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2023

films.syn: Are we watching a concert, an endearingly manic fairground skit, or a Dadaist demolition derby, which might have come out of a film by Quentin Dupieux? Lolo and Sosaku are two sound artists, whose enchantingly ineffective mechanical instruments, whacky escapades and destructive creativity are brought together in a Western odyssey as conceived by Sergio Caballero. The result is an entertaining piece of interaction between performance, documentary and artistic installation, at whose centre lie the creators themselves. A film, in which senseless machines are reined in, but certainly not the imagination.​

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2024

films.syn: A 16mm film strip damaged by the electrical discharges from the protagonist’s voice recording tells the story of a nuclear power plant worker who focuses his obsession with counting on one single goal: to calculate the maximum limit of his energy consumption. A poetic film in both style and content, 3 MWh is a meditation on man’s relationship with nature, a reflection on what might happen if we retreated into the background and submitted to the natural cycle of life. What might things be like if we were to disconnect from technology and just be?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2024

films.syn: Edward acquires his dream face but then discovers that, in his pursuit of a new self, he has lost touch with the old one. As he falls into a spiral of obsession, he pulls the audience in after him. Does appearance matter or not? And which option is more frightening? A brilliantly cast thriller infused with a disturbing sense of the grotesque, A Different Man is sure to attract audiences, and not just among fans of Lynch and Cronenberg. Sebastian Stan – winner of the Silver Bear at the Berlinale for his performance – lends his face to Edward in a film that turns the concept of the body horror upside down and right side up again.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.t: A Good Mind Grows in Thorny Places
films.syn: Twelve-year-old Adam from the Slovak village of Utekáč can do any job you ask of him. He is strong, brave, and very active. He earns his own money, his life is completely in his own hands, and his friends admire him for it. Adam says all this about himself, but the truth is perhaps a little different. Set to a folk rhythm, Slovak director Katarína Gramatová’s hybrid documentary brilliantly uses the tools of cinema, a sense of subtle humor, and provocative irony to tell the story of one Romani boy and one remote village where life is far from easy.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2024

films.syn: Penelope is working on an art project about empathy, and Dana is one of her subjects. But the meeting between the two women does not turn out as Dana had hoped. The initially harmless experiment forces the young woman to question her own emotions and thus herself. It isn’t until the opening of Penelope’s exhibition that we see the many different forms empathy can take. Named Best International Short at the 2023 Locarno International Film Festival, the movie explores the limits of emotional vulnerability and the nature of emotion itself. A meditation on how much our perception of ourselves is dependent on our surroundings, the film naturally approaches its subject with both empathy and a subtle sense of humor.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2023

films.t: A Sudden Glimpse to Deeper Things
films.syn: One of the most important women in British modern art, the painter Wilhelmina Barns-Graham was a highly inspirational figure, whose work was deeply impacted by a pivotal event in her life. In May 1949, this leading representative of the modernist St Ives group of artists climbed to the top of the Grindelwald glacier in Switzerland, an experience which was to transform the way she saw the world. She spent the rest of her life capturing its shapes and colours, indeed its very essence. In his essayistic portrait documentarist Mark Cousins delves into complex themes of gender, climate change and creativity, while laying bare the artist’s character and vast imagination so pervasively that he creates the impression we are seeing the world through her eyes.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2024

films.syn: Can we see time if we slow it down? The concept of “mindfulness” became synonymous with human happiness only recently, while Tsai Ming-liang has been leading us towards a closer awareness of the world for years. The tenth in his series of films about a Buddhist monk walking extremely slowly across rural and urban landscapes, is set in Washington, DC. On this occasion, the figure of a second man moves through similar locations. The two solitary journeys might conceivably intersect yet, to attain solidarity, the mere knowledge of a parallel existence would surely also suffice… A well-rounded film meditation, in which the Taiwanese master of radically slow cinema heightens the senses so as to enrich and colour our upcoming festival days.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2024

films.syn: Theodora Remundová’s documentary portrait looks at Iva Janžurová’s dramatic and comedic roles in both film and theater, as well as the roles she has played in her family and in social and political life. The director (Janžurová’s daughter) has created a film filled with the truthfulness, sincerity, and capacity for self-reflection of a woman who has devoted her life to acting. The use of clearly staged scenes is combined with an openly acknowledged effort to avoid the kinds of clichés usually found in biographical documentaries to create an organic whole that provides an overview of Janžurová’s pivotal roles while also sharing highly personal and intimate moments from her life.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 2024

films.syn: At the end of yet another tedious day, bored word processor Paul Hackett goes into a bar, where he meets an unusual girl. At this moment his life suddenly becomes a nocturnal sprint through the dark recesses of New York as he experiences a series of inexplicably linked events which, at first glance, transform his real world into an absurd parallel reality. The connection between Scorsese’s lesser-known masterpiece, which won Best Direction in Cannes, and Franz Kafka’s writings is self-evident, while it undeniably comes closest to his short story Description of a Struggle. As Kafka might have put it, After Hours is a film in which life is something that induces dizziness, something that is “recognised no less clearly as a nothing, a dream, a dim hovering”. We present the movie in its brand-new digital restoration.

ap.p: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema); production year 1985

films.syn: While a gamer is uploading a testimonial video to denounce the harassment she has been suffering in a war video game, a stranger enters her home and hacks her computer, blurring the boundaries of the real and the virtual with chaotic consequences. Prize for Best Film in the Labo Competition at the 18th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2024.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2023

films.syn: A cinematic ode to all those who have been caught in the gravitational force of Mumbai. Who have lived here for years and yet are reluctant to call the city home, for they can never shake the feeling that one day they will have to leave again. Is this Indian metropolis robbing them of time? Perhaps. Does it refuse to give them even one moment of tenderness? Absolutely. It has been thirty years since India has had a film in competition at Cannes, and now Payal Kapadia deservedly took home the Grand Jury Prize for her lovingly feminine, brightly lyrical story in which the beating of a broken heart is imprinted in the red sheen of a newly unpacked rice cooker and infinity is expressed by all the shades of blue we can count in Mumbai at night.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: A wild landscape of rocks, flourishing woodland and deep chasms. The soil beneath the ferns comes alive with edible, medicinal and deadly colours; restlessness merges with unexpected kindness. Fungi as the magical spirits of the forest and guides to the collective unconscious, and this in a hypnotic form created in Mexico’s Laboratory of Experimental Cinema.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2024

films.t: Always Show Courage When Burning To The Ground
films.syn: Roses, glitter, jockstraps. God’s gaze is everywhere, even in a gay sauna, especially when the steam rising above it veils a hint of danger. In his latest film, Joseph Wilson confirms once more his status as a filmmaker with an extraordinary sense of queer aesthetics; here he again shifts between elements of camp and authentic experience, between provocation and endless playfulness. An exhilaratingly intense adventure, with more kick to it than a puff from a bottle of poppers.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2024

films.syn: For his feature film debut the director took on an extremely challenging assignment – to transfer one of Franz Kafka’s novels to the big screen. He settled on the early prose work The Man Who Disappeared, which nevertheless already contains all of the author’s key motifs, primarily the angst-ridden, solitary hero, and the surrounding reality as a labyrinth full of absurd situations and incomprehensible demands. In order to evoke the protagonist’s grievous states and the perils of his estranged world, Michálek made inventive use of expressionist film idioms: copious details of faces and gestures, scenes with no backdrop, steeped in chiaroscuro, and a score brimming with dissonance. The sets depicting the American urban landscape are markedly reminiscent of Fritz Lang’s Metropolis.

ap.p: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema); production year 1994

films.syn: In his latest film, Victor Kossakovsky looks at architecture as something that tells us more about the future of humanity than its past. Architecton is a meditative yet excitingly compelling audiovisual spectacle, framed by the philosophical views of Italian architect Michele De Lucchi. Is stone as a building material truly what unites the world’s nations across the continents? What is the relationship between the temple ruins at Baalbek and a prefabricated housing estate in contemporary Ukraine? Kossakovsky invites us to ponder these and other questions through observational as well as captivating and stylized documentary footage.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: It’s certainly no coincidence that moviemaker and militant revolutionary Masao Adachi opted to make a film based on one of Franz Kafka’s last and undeniably most exquisite short stories, A Hunger Artist, which the writer was still editing the day before he died. The body of the fasting artist does, indeed, show signs of sacrifice in the form of a real and metaphysical struggle against everyone and everything – like the film director, who decides to leave his homeland, put down his camera and take up arms in the battle for the liberation of Palestine. The hunger artist – just like the filmmaker or the fighter – expresses the ascetic concept of creative art, according to which the artist’s truth and destiny lie in his ability to come as close as possible to death. Once we make the decision to fast, we have to fast forever.

ap.p: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema); production year 2015

films.syn: A look back into the past, at scenes from the history of a family marked by the serious illness of a child. In footage from dad’s video camera, hospital visits become a game, practice for actual medical procedures. A child’s-eye view of an illness whose path to a cure is filled with much pain and suffering, Baldilocks is director Martha Peters’s self-portrait of her own childhood spent battling cancer. The disease itself may have disappeared, but the memory of it has not. Fragments from the family archive produce a diverse collage of emotions, ranging from sadness, pain, and compassion to humor, courage, and – most importantly – hope.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2023

films.syn: In 1907, Afonso arrives on a tropical island not far from the African coast, where he has been tasked with treating a group of workers plagued by a mysterious affliction called banzo, also known as slave nostalgia. Those affected feel an intense homesickness, fall into apathy, lose the strength to live, and eventually die. Afonso slowly discovers that it is not enough to treat the physical symptoms; he must understand the soul of those who have been uprooted. The oppressive atmosphere of the isolated tropical island forms the backdrop for a story from the dark colonial past in which humanity is put to the ultimate test. Banzo is also a reminder that there is more than one way to interpret the past, and that behind every story is a person telling the story.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2024

films.syn: Battery Mommy works at a nursery, operating the soap bubble gun, camera, and thermometer. One pre-Christmas day, however, an accident occurs at the nursery that gives Battery Mommy plenty to do.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2023

films.syn: The woman’s dead, but her hair still looks great. This film compilation arranges scenes from the series A Case for Two in chronological order and demonstrates how the fetishisation of the female body developed or, rather, froze to death in this popular German crime series. Bare ankles, lace necklines, perfect make-up: even hanged women have to look good.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2024

films.syn: Some magical worlds can be hidden behind the mirror; others exist between the walls. This lo-fi mystery by Caroline Poggi and Jonathan Vinel takes us to a constricted wall space, to liminal places and dreamlike states, which might provide asylum in situations that go far beyond our comprehension.​ At once a chaotic and contemplative piece, which puts video game aesthetics to good use, the film functions as an expedition to uncharted territories. As in the previous opus by the filmmaking duo, music plays a prominent role here, which helps to intensify the provocative and disquieting nature of a work which is, however, also somewhat melancholy, yet undeniably reassuring.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2023

films.syn: While Ben, a cantor at his Jewish temple who still lives with his two mothers, is losing his faith and his voice, his former music teacher Carla has decided to discover hers. These two lost souls, who are both teacher and student to each other, grow closer than they might have expected, much to the chagrin of their families. Director Nathan Silver’s playful film is not afraid to bite the proverbial apple as it sets out, with a good dose of satire and humor, to destigmatize different periods in our lives. A bittersweet comedy that asks what it means to be a mensch, Between the Temples left an impression on audiences at the Sundance and Berlinale film festivals.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Bliss Point indicates the optimal dose of food additives required to achieve desired palatability for the consumer. Bliss Point is also the culmination of a trilogy, in which Gerard Ortín Castellví traces the journey undertaken by food products as they make their way to our table. Buffeting us with alluring images, this aesthetically honed film follows the various stages a food item has to go through in order to stimulate our taste buds. At the same time, however, Castellví calls into question the scramble for perfection, where functionality is placed above humanity.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2023

films.syn: After a random encounter outside a nightclub, a young house painter ends up at an afterparty with a charming couple, only to find himself trapped in a power game between the two, who use him as a prop to relight their flame.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2023

films.syn: When Shuo is injured at school, his classmate Wein invites him home to his place. After getting to know his parents, Shuo keeps returning for visits – and, surprisingly, they welcome him as a part of their family. But the more their lives are intertwined, the clearer it becomes that not everyone is happy with the new situation, for they all have their own secrets. This unsettling drama touching on China’s one-child policy premiered in the Panorama section at this year’s Berlinale, and although History of a Family marks the director’s feature film debut, it is a formally focused film directed with a steady hand and with a carefully arranged structure.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: The European Space Agency forms a team of scientists to craft a message to send to alien civilizations. As they work to compile a comprehensive report on humanity, the team is faced with unexpected challenges, including debates on what should be said and how it should be expressed. The film takes a humorous look at the complexities of human existence. Special Jury Mention in the National Competition at the 18th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2024.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2023

films.syn: “I wish my mother was here so I could ask her...” When Hiam Abbas (Succession, Munich) was twenty-three, she decided to leave her native village in Palestine to pursue a career in acting. Several decades later, she returns home alongside her daughter Lina Soualem to complete a cinematic portrait of her family that is also a chronicle of four generations of indomitable women facing voluntary and forced separation. In her extremely personal and, in its level of openness, highly moving film, Soualem tells the tragic story of all of Palestine through the stories of her mother and other women, affirming that no amount of destruction can break the bonds of family.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Two young people, Soundouss and Jaâfar, arrive at a luxury villa in the resort of Cabo Negro rented by Jaâfar’s lover, who is supposed to join them later. But something is wrong – he still hasn’t turned up, and they can’t reach him on his phone. Left on their own, they decide, despite their uncertain financial and personal situation, to enjoy their holiday as much as their minds and bodies will allow. On vacation, with time seemingly non-existent, they take the opportunity to reflect on their relationships back home – and on the future, which feels so distant here on the sun-drenched beach. Writer-director Abdellah Taïa presents a queer ode to the seemingly carefree time of youth.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2024

films.syn: Bruno Anković’s feature film debut is set in an impoverished Croatian village between the years 1926 and 1945. The constant deprivation, repeated changes to the regime, and war pervaded the forests and shrouded the place in a miasma that obscured all visions of a better future. Village life was also tough for Mijo: His young, innocent soul was burdened by the outside world and troubled by inhumane orders, and he then fell prey to the false sheen of right-wing ideology. This film adaptation of the successful novel of the same name by Damir Karakaš presents us with wonderful shots of the rural landscape, but it is also a testimony of commonplace brutality and demonstrates the reasons why innocent people become easy quarry for ideological crusaders.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2024

films.syn: Green-haired Maia is tired of city life and, driven by a desire to be among nature, she decides to spend the summer picking oranges. In the orchards she is greeted by the gardener, an eccentric loner called Teo, who notices that Maia isn’t like everyone else. In the same way he tends his plants, he devotes his time and energy to her, too, and the young woman starts to blossom. Their burgeoning friendship, however, is unsettled by the arrival of Teo’s father and older brother Arturo, who are planning a celebration in a neighbouring village... In her richly coloured story, which shows it’s sometimes difficult to find someone who could help us to discover our true selves, director Ivana Gloria awakens within us senses that we didn’t even know we had.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2023

films.syn: A masterpiece by Jean-Marie Straub and Danièle Huillet, based on themes from Kafka’s novel The Man Who Disappeared. For the cinematic version of the tale of young Karl Rossmann, from his arrival in the New World to his encounter with the Theater of Oklahoma, the legendary filmmaking duo went for a distinctly political angle, clearly reflected in the film’s title as well. “For us, Kafka is the only great poet of industrial civilisation, namely, a society in which people depend on their work to survive.” America represents something of a dream for Rossmann, adrift in a world which is difficult to understand, and strewn with blind optimism and untold violence. Straub-Huillet shot almost the entire film in Hamburg and, in order to achieve the authenticity of the original text, they incorporated the specific dialect favoured by Kafka.

ap.p: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema); production year 1984

films.syn: It’s been twenty years since filmgoers first saw this stylistically polished relationship drama for four players, based on the celebrated play by Patrick Marber. Through this cinematic endeavour, director Mike Nichols, already well respected at that time, if not fully appreciated, sparked memories of two key films from his early career, Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf and Carnal Knowledge. Jude Law, Natalie Portman, Julia Roberts and, above all, Clive Owen who, in his role as Larry, earned one of the film’s two Oscar nominations, shifted an erotically charged story of love, manipulation and betrayal to the realms of a modern classic with its critically acclaimed combination of magnetic performances and disarming stellar potential.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Clive Owen); production year 2004

films.t: Cross My Heart and Hope To Die
films.syn: Mila struggles as she remains unpaid at work and a love interest becomes a source of comfort through his constant phone calls. But a promise of hope may also lead to tragedy and sad love songs. Special Jury Mention in the International Competition at the 18th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2024.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2023

films.syn: Before the death of her sister, retired teacher Lia promised to find her niece Tekla, who had been rejected by her family because of her trans identity. Along with her young neighbor Achi, she travels to Istanbul, where Tekla is thought to have gone. The city plays a central role in the story, and its winding streets, close-knit neighborhoods, and distinctive residents become a symbol of hope: not only for finding Tekla but also for discovering new friends and exploring new horizons. Crossing opened the Panorama section at this year’s Berlinale and rightfully became one of the festival’s most popular films. Swedish director Levan Akin approaches this difficult subject in a very human way, using humor and empathy to explore a story that touches us all.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Violence begets violence, and 14-year-old Jessica knows it. She lives with a father who is quick to anger, especially if there isn’t enough food in the house – and Jessica, her younger sister, and her mother all have the mental and physical scars to match. She would like to live as carefree a life as her friends, but fitting in is hard. All of the family’s problems come to a head one afternoon when Jessica is supposed to pick up the shopping but would also like to go to a party. A film about the power of sibling love, about minor misfortunes with disproportionately negative consequences, and the yearning to break free from the vicious cycle of a dysfunctional family.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2023

films.syn: Curiosa tells the story of overly curious Mary, who visits her boyfriend’s flat for the first time just to discover it’s been stripped bare of all personal belongings. After being denied an explanation, she climbs into his head. Winner of the Audience Award at the 18th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2024.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: Vladimir 518, uncompromising rapper, artist, stage designer and activist, is a rare phenomenon, who not only writes books, but publishes them as well. Today also a respected authority primarily on pre-1989 architecture, he has written not only a major publication on the subject, but also the story for two audiovisual works treating the same theme, which were shot by Jan Zajíček, renowned director of music videos. In addition to the recent TV series we have the eagerly anticipated feature-length film which, through its fascinating and impressive exploration of Czech and Slovak architecture of the latter half of the 20th century, offers exclusive insight into extraordinary buildings and unique individuals living below the Tatra Mountains.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2024

films.syn: A concentrated look at one of France’s most important militant communities – a group of activists, farmers, anarchists, and “eco-terrorists” who have spent more than twenty years defending the fragile ecosystem of the marshes in northwestern France against the construction of a regional airport. Named Best Film in this year’s Encounters competition at the Berlinale, Direct Action skips the tabloid aesthetics of violent clashes and instead depicts the community members’ everyday tasks: kneading dough, sharpening saws, keeping watch at night. A hypnotic observational documentary that finds a hopeful symbiosis of man and nature at a time of environmental crisis, it also sheds light on the sensitive relationship between a film’s subjects and the people behind the camera.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: It’s the dormouse’s birthday party, and its friend the bear wants to bake a cake. But they are both unexpectedly overcome by the need to hibernate.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: Dying is the story of a family that long ago stopped being a family. Lissy cares for a husband with advanced dementia, but she is not in the best of health herself. Their son, Tom, is a conductor working on a difficult new piece. He has also become a surrogate father to his ex-girlfriend’s newborn son, leaving him with no time to care for his parents or his sister Ellen, who has alcohol and relationship problems. Winner of Best Screenplay at the Berlinale, this majestic fresco is not nearly as bleak as its title and summary might suggest. Humor as dark as diabetes, kidney failure, and cancer combined is interspersed with moments of pure tenderness and love in places where we would least expect it.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Teenagers Anna and Josef grew up in a strict religious sect. When the whole group gathers by a forest lake to perform a baptism on its youngest member, the two of them decide to run away. They disappear into the woods, but soon discover that they are completely unprepared for life outside their community. Special Jury Mention in the National Competition at the 18th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2024.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2023

films.syn: A masseuse returning to the dating scene falls for a man who turns out to be the ex-husband of one of her clients in Nicole Holofcener’s charming, perceptive rom-com – one of the century’s finest. The initial meet-cute and intermittent splashes of zaniness give way to a gentle, bittersweet meditation on middle-age anxieties, loneliness, and the lingering emotional void parenthood can only cover temporarily. Holofcener’s first collaboration with Seinfeld and Veep star Julia Louis-Dreyfus, who received a Golden Globe nomination for her role, this is the director’s biggest commercial hit to date, notably featuring the penultimate performance of The Sopranos icon James Gandolfini in the warmest, most affable turn of his storied career.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Nicole Holofcener); production year 2013

films.syn: Oral exams. A question. Panic, fever, sweating. As young Abel grasps for words, his teacher asks him a seemingly innocent question that changes everything. Gábor Reisz’s third feature outing is set in contemporary Hungary, but given the rising social tensions throughout the world, his Explanation for Everything is – unfortunately – a universal story. Reisz approaches the subject of strongly divided opinions, of a societal powder keg ready to explode, with a sense of humor and understated ease. And yet he does not shy away from showing the deep and difficult-to-heal wounds that divide families and strangers alike. Winner of the Orizzonti Award for Best Film at last year’s Venice Film Festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Director Ruth Beckermann’s latest documentary takes us into a primary school classroom in Vienna’s Favoriten neigborhood. As at other schools in the Austrian capital, more than half of the students do not speak fluent German. And so the students and their devoted teacher spend their time learning not just mathematics, science, or other traditional subjects, but also patience, understanding, respect, and how to communicate in such a diverse group. At times serious as well as humorous, Beckermann’s film asks whether rounding to tens is really the most important skill schools should teach us.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Are you looking for reassurance that your beloved is The One, that your partner is truly for life? Then visit the Love Institute, a scientific organization that will test the mutual compatibility of people who have decided to embark on life’s journey together. It is here of all places that the incurable romantic Anna finds a job, temporarily mentored by the thoughtful and sympathetic Amir. Greek director Christos Nikou’s tender and absurd romance with a touch of sci-fi will delight even audiences who tend to avoid anything that is even remotely “science fiction.” Co-produced by Cate Blanchett, the talented Nikou’s second outing (his debut Apples instantly made him one of the most sought-after directors today) features disarming performances by Jesse Buckley and Riz Ahmed.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Loosely inspired by General Custer’s defeat at the Battle of Little Big Horn, the first Western in John Ford’s “Cavalry Trilogy” presents the ambitious Lieutenant Colonel Thursday (Henry Fonda), who is bitter at being reassigned to a distant outpost. When the Apaches go on the warpath, all the warnings of the hardened Captain York (John Wayne) are in vain. One of the first films to portray the original inhabitants of the North American continent with respect and understanding, Fort Apache is one of many films that contributed to the iconic status of Monument Valley, using the local scenery as the stage for a thrilling depiction of watershed moments in the history of the conquest of the American West.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1948

films.syn: This short film by eminent Japanese animator Kôji Yamamura, adapting Kafka’s short story of the same name, re-creates the Kafkaesque experience – a combination of unnatural terror and incredibly dark humour – with the aid of the traditional Japanese comic theatre known as kyōgen. All the action is distorted and, at the same time, subjected to unsustainable ridicule.

ap.p: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema); production year 2007

films.t: Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life
films.syn: Franz Kafka is working on his Metamorphosis, but he’s suffering from writer’s block; he can’t get off on the right track. While trying to decide what Gregor Samsa is going to wake up as, he is constantly interrupted by door-to-door salesmen, young women, and his own inexplicable hallucinations. The film, whose title combines the name of the celebrated author with the cult family classic by Frank Capra, won the 1995 Oscar for best short live-action feature.

ap.p: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema); production year 1993

films.t: François Truffaut, My Life, a Screenplay
films.ot: François Truffaut, le scénario de ma vie
films.syn: Almost a quarter of a century separates François Truffaut’s debut The 400 Blows and his final film, Confidentially Yours. A life dedicated to film; twenty-one feature films largely reflecting the life of an ultimate cinephile obsessed with cinema. Shortly before his tragically premature death, Truffaut shared the ups and downs of his childhood and adolescence with his longtime friend Claude de Givray, without shying away from more painful memories. Unfortunately, the ailing filmmaker did not live to complete the planned autobiographical “Screenplay of My Life.” David Teboul has woven much of Truffaut’s life into a documentary portrait full of previously unpublished material from the life of one of the most beloved French directors of the 20th century.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 2024

films.syn: Five teenagers set off in a beat-up old van on their last summer vacation before their adult lives engulf them. They want to finally see the Pacific Ocean, but they’re hundreds of miles – and dozens of adventures – from their destination. The latest film from the American directing duo The Ross Brothers tries to capture the teenagers’ sense of freedom and friendship, but also their intangible anticipation of the future. This visually captivating road movie, which was shown in the Orizzonti competition at the Venice Film Festival, feels as if the filmmakers had simply set out on a journey with their protagonists, for whom the most important thing is to live in the here and now.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Sixteen-year-old Mira, an ambitious and successful student at a strict boarding school, is slowly growing closer to an older classmate. Their initially cautious romance is soon dominated by sexual curiosity and desire, which the young couple must keep hidden from their teachers and from Mira’s mother, within whom Mira’s relationship also begins to awaken something previously dormant. An exceptionally sensitively shot and subtly acted film, the sense of humor, depth, and tenderness with which Girls Will Be Girls portrays the fragile period of adolescence made it an audience favorite at this year’s Sundance, from where it ultimately took home the Audience Award.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: “I found you a suitable widower – he has ten children and needs to take a rest.” Life wasn’t easy for women in Italy in the year 1800, and it didn’t matter that (like the heroines of Gloria!) they were putting together a new piece at the music institute for the recently elected pope. For her directorial debut, Italian actress Margherita Vicario has chosen to explore this forgotten chapter of history. Her film, which was shown in competition at this year’s Berlinale, reminds us that music history is not just about male composers, and that sometimes even an art school can be a place from which we need to escape into dreams and fantasies.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: “It’s a mystery to me how anyone can be so tenacious,” Edward says of his fiancée Molly, who relentlessly pursues him across the Asian continent in 1917 after he leaves her. The same could be said about Miguel Gomes’s directing, recently recognized at the Cannes Film Festival. Indeed, in Grand Tour, one of the most original directors of our time does not merely present us with the tragicomic tale of one relationship but, as in his previous films, he approaches the cinematic medium as a place where one can travel through space and time thanks to creative editing and a big dose of cognitive dissonance. A true treat for cinephiles, his latest film (which does not shy away from Hollywood studio film tropes) is part love story, part imaginative travelogue, and part contemporary documentary.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: This mature French debut is set in the heart of the Jura, a rural region known for its dairy cows, agricultural festivals, and delicate Comté cheese. It is here that Totone spends his youth, mainly just hanging out with his friends. But after his father’s tragic accident, Totone will have to stand on his own two feet and support himself and his little sister. To this end, he decides to make the most delicious cheese and to hold his own against the tough local competition. An unexpected audience hit at this year’s Cannes Film Festival, Holy Cow excels thanks to its graceful direction and authentic performances from its young non-actors. Like any story of adolescence, this one is filled with emotional ups and downs, including the euphoria of first love and the power of boyhood friendships.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Is family something we are born into, or is it something we build over the course of our lives? Who creates family? And can it be created artificially? Goran Stolevski’s third feature film tells the story of Dita, a social worker who is forced to take on the role of mother and to deal with various steps necessary for giving a group of “dropouts” family support. But this diverse bunch of characters bursting with energy is like a bomb waiting to go off. A crushing portrayal of the complexity of interpersonal relationships and social roles, Housekeeping for Beginners premiered in the Orizzonti competition at the Venice Film Festival, where it won the Queer Lion award.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Debut director Annick Blanc’s psychedelic horror presents hunting as a phenomenon that is equal parts toxic and intoxicating. Five men on a hunting expedition in the Canadian woods encounter a young woman in trouble, who begs them to let her join them. They agree on the condition that she become a part of their pack and agree to all its rules. A hallucinatory, menacing, and simultaneously caustically ironic trip through the rocky terrain of archetypal machismo amidst a ruthless and unpredictable wilderness, Hunting Daze flows steadily between fever dream and a disillusioned awakening to harsh reality.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Midnight Screenings); production year 2024

films.syn: The self-contained world of the swimming pool forms the stage for a conflict between Vio and her classmates, with whom she does not get along. The worst is Sara, a master of subtle innuendo, which each time becomes more personal and thus more painful. The entire situation leads to an inevitable clash that might just bring catharsis and change the two girls’ relationship forever. The pastel-hued setting of the swimming pool contrasts sharply with the darkly sad world of adolescent girls searching for their place in the classroom and in life.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2024

films.syn: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan led to a massive flight of Afghans to neighboring Iran, which – since they hoped to find a new home there – they called the “Land of Brothers.” But the dream of fraternal coexistence soon faded, Iranian law never accepted them as equal citizens, and so even the descendants of the first refugees still carry the burden of otherness. Alireza Ghasemi and Raha Amirfazli’s wistful, beautifully shot feature debut about a family who will never feel at home in the country where they live won over audiences immediately upon its premiere at Sundance.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2024

films.syn: Federico Fellini is at Cinecittà Studios making a film based on Kafka’s novel The Man Who Disappeared; during breaks between scenes, he responds to questions put to him by a Japanese television crew. Fellini reminisces about the past and about a certain brand of filmmaking which has possibly disappeared forever. Together with Marcello Mastroianni he sets off to visit Anita Ekberg at her villa, where they re-live the era of La dolce vita. In the meantime we are given an increasing number of references to the works of Franz Kafka, whom Fellini often described as his favourite writer.
