Every morning, she goes to her job as a supermarket cashier, and every day after work she goes straight home to look after her ailing mother and the rest of the family. Nobody, however, seems to care. Then, the mysterious murder of her boss sets off a chain of events at the end of which she can be free and find her own worth. How to describe her journey? Perhaps best as a sexual odyssey, an exploratory expedition to places where an important role is played by carnality, desire, and its gratification. Tropicana is a subtly enigmatic reflection on conservatism, prudery, and the false ideal of physical beauty.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2024

films.syn: The aging Pietro is to receive a presidential award for his essays on teaching. His former student Teresa, now a distinguished professor herself, is to deliver the commendation speech at the ceremony. However, the two are former lovers who, one night long ago, shared their greatest secrets with each other, and now Pietro fears that his quite devastating secret may come out. In his latest drama, Daniele Luchetti presents a sweeping saga about a relationship in which dangerous liaisons unravel across multiple timelines to a soundtrack by Thom Yorke. All the while, he asks: Can we really trust anyone?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2023

films.syn: Two people drive a red Hummer through the seemingly endless California desert near the town of Twentynine Palms. He is American, she is Russian. They speak French together, although neither can speak it well enough to express how they feel. They make love, fight, and make up. Two characters lost in a stunning rocky landscape, claustrophobically bound to one another, enclosed in the space of the car. A bad omen has haunted them since they began their journey, but it’s impossible to say whether the imagined horror is any worse than the real one – quite the opposite, in fact. Bruno Dumont’s third feature film is both atmospheric love story and oppressive horror, and doesn’t shy away from explicit nudity and nerve-wracking violence.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 2003

films.t: Twin Peaks: A Limited Event Series
films.syn: We encounter FBI agent Dale Cooper once again in a dark cavern, where a woman with no eyes protects him from an invisible threat. Cooper manages to escape. The agent’s doppelgänger and another artificially created double, Dougie Jones, get sick. Dougie succumbs to the Black Lodge and disappears, while Cooper is released; he takes Dougie’s place, but his memory is erased in the process. Via a fascinating web of convoluted events we find ourselves at FBI headquarters in Philadelphia, in the office of Deputy Director Gordon Cole (David Lynch), namely, the most Kafkaesque interior we could have imagined. Likewise, David Lynch is the most Kafkaesque filmmaker ever to have lived, despite the fact that he never adapted any of Kafka’s work.

ap.p: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Wish To Be a Red Indian: Kafka and Cinema); production year 2017

films.ot: Les deux Anglaises et le continent
films.syn: KVIFF and MK2 present the world premiere of a restored version of Truffaut’s Two English Girls. Somewhere in the middle of Truffaut’s remarkable career lies this charming and tenderly poignant lyrical drama of a love triangle, based (like Jules and Jim a decade earlier) on a novel by Henri-Pierre Roché. “While filming I learned many things about cinema but also things about life, about love, sentimental violence and the cruelty lovers can innocently inflict on each other,” Truffaut wrote of the film, which is set in early 20th-century France and Wales. The role of a man caught between two women was brought to life by Jean-Pierre Léaud, who began his amazing career exactly 65 years ago in Truffaut’s legendary The 400 Blows.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1971

films.syn: Observation and destruction. Primarily from a vertical perspective, this collage of archive material depicts human settlements, the natural landscape, and children playing, yet it also captures a series of controlled explosions. Calmly yet urgently the seemingly apolitical shots convey a clear, political message. In the light of the relentless uprooting of Palestinians, what might be taken for an innocent period picture postcard acquires darkly contradictory contours and meanings.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2024

films.syn: We can watch a film, we can experience it, or we can devour it. But Minh Quý Truong knows that some films can be dreamed. His fog-shrouded tale of Viet and Nam, two miners who share a profession and a fleeting tenderness, follows the rhythms of delicate, spiritual storytelling. The damp mine shafts hide danger, but their darkness can also be a refuge. At the same time, the two young men dream of a future elsewhere. One imagines a life overseas, while the other must first plumb the depths of his family history. Shot on 16mm film, Viet and Nam meanders slowly through the hardships of contemporary life in Vietnam without forgetting that beneath the surface lies hidden a troubled past.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Within the first month of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, more than 12.5 million people were forced to flee their homes and 5 million fled the country altogether. Documentary filmmaker Antonin Peretjatko returns to Lviv with Andrei, who has left with his family for France, to retrieve Andrei’s personal belongings and to explore his own roots, but most importantly to record eyewitness testimony from people who have remained in Ukraine. Part reportage documentary and part poetic road movie with an aesthetic style reminiscent of the early French New Wave, Voyage Along the War tries to share with the viewer what everyday life looks like in a war-torn country.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2024

films.syn: One might think that Czech and Slovak filmmakers have already said all there is to say about the period around 1968 in Czechoslovak history. As Jiří Mádl’s latest outing shows, however, this crucial era in our modern history still has forgotten stories to offer that are worthy of our attention. The film revolves around the international news office at Czechoslovak Radio, a place full of talented individuals possessing broad insight, linguistic skills, and above all a commitment to honest journalistic work with a focus on the truth. An epic, dynamically shot, rewarding film, which embraces uncommon heroism in the face of an oppressive regime, the strength of fraternal ties, and the eternal themes of love, betrayal, morality, and hope.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2024

films.syn: Just 24 hours are enough to turn the life of performing arts student Una upside down. And not just hers. When Reykjavík is paralyzed by the greatest transport tragedy in its history, like many other people Una is confronted with sudden loss and pain. But unlike those around her, she cannot openly express and experience her emotions. Rúnar Rúnarsson’s sparse yet emotionally complex film focuses on the moment when someone close to us, someone with whom we had planned a future, disappears from our lives. It tells a story of grieving, of the fragile tangle of human emotions, and the vulnerability and resilience of youth. To the strains of Jóhann Jóhannsson’s Odi et Amo, it then reveals the fleeting beauty that emerges in moments of unexpected loss.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Aïcha lives on a farm in northern Tunisia with her husband and three sons. The two older ones, Mehdi and Amine, leave the family to fight jihad in the name of ISIS. Aïcha wants to protect her youngest offspring from the cruel truth, but her efforts are complicated by Mehdi’s return – alongside a mysterious woman in a niqab. Debut director Meryam Joobeur introduces magical-realist elements into an otherwise raw story, an unsettling tale of family, cruelty, violence, and forgiveness. The film, shown in the main competition at this year’s Berlinale, isn’t afraid to get truly close to its protagonists, and thanks to its evocative cinematography you will be sure to remember their faces long after the credits have rolled.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Minna is a home care nurse. With undying kindness and optimism, she visits all her clients, providing them with mental and physical comfort. She has a fifteen-year-old daughter, but she is aware that she is unable to give her the time she deserves. And then there is Alvar, a sick man who desperately needs care and support – things his illness prevents him from asking for. Who Stands Up for Alvar is a critique of an overburdened welfare system that drains caregivers of valuable energy they could be devoting to their clients, as well as a poignant look at the need for “ordinary” human kindness.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2024

films.syn: After years away Kaloyan returns to his native Bulgaria in order to sell his late father’s flat. What at first seems like a routine task devoid of emotion gradually develops into a journey to the depths of his being, where he is confronted with distant traumas, yet he also strikes a new path towards self-discovery. While childhood is filled with sensations and the rustling wind, adulthood is a state of fragile, windless and fading memories of those closest to us. Vesnakov delivers colourful existential reflections on the nature of family bonds and personal identity over the course of time. Yet he also muses on modern-day Bulgaria, where the cemeteries of its original inhabitants are being replaced by shady casinos, and where cultural memory is waning in a country deceived by an illusory vision of economic prosperity.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2024

films.syn: Xoftex is a Greek refugee camp, where Syrian and Palestinian asylum seekers anxiously wait for news of their refugee status. To pass the time between interviews with the immigration office, Nasser and his friends film satirical sketches and make preparations for a zombie horror flick. Except that the reality of the camp could be taken for a horror scenario itself. The tension between its inhabitants gains momentum and every conflict removes one more brick from the wall which divides reality from dream – or, indeed, nightmare. Fragments of real life, humour, and the unimaginable suffering of people risking their lives to escape their own country, merge into an explosive, at times, surreal spectacle which invites the viewers to immerse themselves in the story and the lives of immigrants in a way they will never have experienced before.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2024

films.syn: After scoring her first Oscar nomination as co-writer on Can You Ever Forgive Me? in 2018, Nicole Holofcener reteamed with Julia Louis-Dreyfus for this delectable comedy about a novelist whose marriage is thrown into disarray when she overhears her therapist husband dismissing her upcoming book. While Enough Said touches upon the fears of new adult romance, You Hurt My Feelings focuses on the debilitating stillness of marriage. Moreover, Holofcener’s latest is about the disappointments of middle age: professional, personal, and marital – the lies we tell ourselves and each other to continue leading a life that is nowhere as fulfilling or invigorating as we assumed it would be. With its astute observations and fine detail, Feelings cements Holofcener’s status as one of America’s great chroniclers of bourgeois life.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Nicole Holofcener); production year 2022

films.syn: A film about the end of the world and the end of a roll of toilet paper. In his deftly playful work shot on 16mm, filmmaker (and musician) Ondřej Vavrečka reminisces, says his farewells and also reflects on the limits of progress. Via three fictional characters, each of whom responds differently to the impulses of their surroundings, he simultaneously enhances the sensitivity of the film audience. Will a pain we experience leave a scar or merely a colourless memory? And will someone remember the old Vysočany station a hundred years from now? In its poetic charm this cinematic piece is almost tactile in nature; it awakens all the senses and, in places, bears the hallmark of Jan Švankmajer, if the latter had been born an essential optimist, that is. Film as a whisper emanating from smiling lips.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: An ordinary sports day at a primary school. One seemingly trivial conflict between two young football players sets in motion a chain of events that culminates in a violent clash between adults. Swiss director Sinan Taner’s 1:10 looks at the crowd and individuals from inventive angles: at one moment, the people are little more than chaotically moving particles, but in the very next they become individuals with their own specific stories. Taner brilliantly captures the psychology of the crowd and the uncertainty of children who are still learning to navigate the world and to understand problems that far transcend them.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2024

films.syn: Two kilometers are an almost imperceptible distance in times of peace. But in the midst of fierce fighting for a strategically important village in eastern Ukraine, every inch counts, and suddenly those two kilometers are packed with everything – splintered trees, devastated nature, hostile worlds, despair, and above all a ruthless fight to the death. After 20 Days in Mariupol, Oscar-winning director Mstyslav Chernov again redefines the war documentary. Reporting from the frontline, he not only captures the bitter aftertaste of a Pyrrhic victory in a scorched land, but most importantly he shares haunting images of war as a nightmare from which there is no waking. 2000 Metres to Andriivka won the Directing Award: World Cinema Documentary at this year’s Sundance Film Festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: A black screen – yet so many colours within it. A magical two-minute miniature which summons up the spirits of legendary animator and director Norman McLaren and tests to see how many percepts our mind can interpret. In a unique cinematic form, handcraft blends with unpredictability, analogue vibe with timelessness. Blink and you’ll miss so much of it.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2024

films.syn: In 2013, director Tom Shoval was present at the Berlinale with Youth, a drama about twin brothers whose strong bond is tested by the dramatic events of a kidnapping. By a twist of fate, one of the actors, David Cunio, was kidnapped by Hamas ten years later during the October 7 massacre and has been held captive ever since. Shoval’s documentary A Letter to David is half remembrances and half a message to David from his family, friends, and the director himself. Working with a large number of archival materials and heart-rending testimony about the events of that day, the film had its premiere this year as part of the Berlin film festival’s prestigious Berlinale Special section.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Are we watching a folk tale or listening to memories distorted by dreamlike logic, or did Jodorowsky perhaps decide to shoot some television propaganda? In his playful yet unsettling short film, Lin Htet Aung returns to his childhood, to the time he was exposed to the dictatorial regime’s brainwashing television broadcasts. These he now transforms into a fascinating, variegated form, in which politics encounters echoes of folkloric mires and, above all, lullabies that don’t help us get to sleep. A film that is fidgety and persistently absorbing in equal measure.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: As Paris pulsates with excitement on the opening day of the Olympic Games, Elisabeth moves around the city with an equal air of anticipation. She works for an Airbnb broker, and the sheer number of arrivals makes this a critical day for her. Elisabeth is tired not just of constantly running between clients, but also from the pressures she faces from her employer. A surprising sense of calm comes when she meets a man named Elijah. A Second Life is an ode to friendship, an urban fairy tale, and an almost documentary portrait of a city in the grips of a massive sporting event. The fragile authenticity of the main protagonists’ experiences is further amplified by an intense soundtrack that practically lets us touch the world of Elisabeth, who must deal not only with work-related difficulties but also with her hearing impairment.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2025

films.syn: There are many films about artificial intelligence, but only a few in which AI, besides being the film’s subject, is the screenwriter as well. Polish director Piotr Winiewicz trained AI on the films of Werner Herzog, who once said, “A computer will not create a film as good as mine in 4,500 years.” The result? A truly unique foray into an unpredictable space, with “Herzog” investigating the mysterious death of a factory worker while another character forms an intimate relationship with a toaster. A hilariously subversive reflection on authorship and the limits of human expression in an age of algorithms, featuring interviews with various artists, philosophers, and scientists.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Nineteen-year-old Sonja is a junior champion in shooting. Her mother lives abroad, and her father, a war veteran, has fallen so far into debt that he, Sonja, and her older brother may be forced out of their home. Her brother tries to solve the situation through shady dealings, but when he ends up witnessing a crime he becomes the target of a local thug. In order to protect her family, Sonja decides to take justice into her own hands. After a four-year hiatus, the festival has again included a miniseries in its program, this time in the form of a dynamic thriller with political undertones, directed by well-known filmmaker Srdan Golubović and three of his former students.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2025

films.syn: A year after the premiere of her documentary debut Lapilli, Paula Ďurinová returns with an entirely different, yet equally sensitive film entitled Action Item. This activist anatomy of burnout, set in Berlin, interweaves the observation of community sharing with a more experimental montage. The work takes note of the myths associated with individualistic society yet, at the same time, it conveys sincere moments of solidarity between individuals who aren’t afraid to speak of their anxieties. This is both a personal and also very human film, which invites us to take a break in these hectic times, when burnout doesn’t necessarily mean the end; on the contrary, it might be a new beginning, where individual pain is gradually transformed into the power of collective sharing.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: The West Bank, 1988. A Palestinian teenager eagerly joins local protests against Israeli soldiers. Suddenly the scene freezes and, with fervour and anguish written on her face, his mother turns to us – witnesses to the dark chapters of the past century – to start telling the story: seven decades in the life of one uprooted family, beginning in 1948, when Zionist paramilitary organizations expelled more than 700,000 Palestinian Arabs from their homes. But this epic chronicle about a family’s struggle to remain together and preserve its dignity in the face of more powerful forces neither judges nor lays blame. In sharing the Palestinian experience with wisdom and in an unusually captivating manner, it touches the heart all the more intensely.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2025

films.syn: The Animanimals want to do a big musical performance but somebody got the wrong notes.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: When an infant dies during birth, doctor Nina finds herself subject to an inquiry by the hospital. She nevertheless continues to help village women who want to terminate their pregnancies, which is a serious crime in Georgia. Dea Kulumbegashvili’s second film depicts the clash of many worlds through images that stay with us long after the lights come back up. Like Nina, we wonder whether we are watching reality, a dream… or a nightmare. This mature work of cinema won the Special Jury Prize at last year’s Venice Film Festival, where it also attracted much critical acclaim.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.t: Archipelago of Earthen Bones – To Bunya
films.syn: Volcanic landscapes, rainforests and fascinating scenery from eastern Australia are transformed by Chilean filmmaker Malena Szlam into an imaginary landscape, shaped not only by the centuries that have passed, but also by the director’s work with 16mm film. Multiple exposures erase the disparities between night and day and enhance the magical qualities of the region and its flora. The mystique and instant magnetism of the piece derive not only from the director’s sense of detail and atmosphere, but also from the soundscapes created by Australian ambient magician Lawrence English.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2024

films.syn: Galician director Lois Patiño has quite a career behind him. His most recent film, Samsara, redefined the possibilities of sensory experiences in cinema by inviting audiences on a journey between death and reincarnation in the form of a fifteen-minute meditation with closed eyes. Where Samsara explored Buddhist culture in Laos, Ariel presents a postmodern adaptation of Shakespeare’s The Tempest, set in the tropical volcanic landscape of the Azores, where Augustina finds herself in a strange reality full of Shakespearean characters incapable of breaking free from their predefined roles. The film is a seductively captivating walk through literary forests and a humorous metanarrative homage to the inhabitants of fictional worlds.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Frequently criticized upon its release, Barry Lyndon is in hindsight a brilliant, timeless tale of an eighteenth-century rogue, soldier, deserter, womanizer, spy, and cheater at cards. Its title character’s vain search for fortune and fame, dotted with the occasional upswing and one giant downfall, stands out for its caustic irony and brilliant visuals that bring to mind the works of the old masters. A showpiece of Kubrick’s legendary perfectionism, shot in natural light on a specially produced camera using sensitive lenses from NASA, the film earned four Oscars and a reputation as a feared duelist in the battle for the best film of all time. The Karlovy Vary festival will be screening a brand new restored copy.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1975

films.syn: Jérémy and Baptiste encounter one another quite by chance, yet they quickly realise they have something in common: the desire to feel good about themselves once again and to find a solution to their receding hairlines in order to achieve this goal. Their shared journey to Istanbul to receive hair transplants develops into a surprisingly intimate experience during which, alongside new heads of hair, a fragile bond starts to grow as well. In his feature debut Manoël Dupont follows the two men with a sense of empathetic detachment and an appreciation for fine detail and humorous dialogue. The film likewise gently explores the themes of queer identity, vulnerability and human intimacy. The pair’s meanders through the Turkish metropolis heighten the atmosphere of the quest – namely the search for beauty in things that aren’t perfect.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.t: Better Go Mad in the Wild
films.syn: The uniqueness of filmmaker Miro Remo resides, among others, in the originality of the questions his films raise. His latest outing, a work which loosely develops the theme explored in the book of the same name by Aleš Palán and Jan Šibík, provocatively asks whether it’s possible to spend your whole life in a single place. As if harking back to a bygone era, twins František and Ondřej Klišík have made the stubborn decision to do just that. Crazy eccentrics or charismatic, possessed storytellers? It seems that they never grew up; viewed through the lens of so-called civilisation, their world shows signs of absurdity. Yet, in their genuine bucolic enchantment, they offer us all the chance to distil our source of inspiration, those of us who sometimes tire of conformist adherence to order.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Seti loves music and singing, and she yearns for her voice to be heard. But in Iran, it is against the law for women to perform in public, and so the young girl decides to engage in her own personal protest. The street becomes her stage, and random passers-by become her enthusiastic audience. Her star rises. Seti becomes an idol of her generation, of young people who no longer want to live under ruthless political oppression. Director Soheil Beiraghi’s fourth film, produced independently, looks at life in contemporary Iran in a way that the local censors would never allow. His film fights for all those whose voice remains unjustly silenced.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Errol and Sasha are studying at university; each is different, both are looking for closeness, someone to truly connect with. This tender and measured film, ostensibly set somewhere between vigorous impulses and lethargy, endeavours to capture the way in which we wrestle with our senses as one day flows into the next. The shared experience in this case doesn’t derive from emotional connection or dramatic action, but from an appreciation of time passing, a feeling for detail and for rendering fragments of the everyday, when a silent gaze tells us everything we need to know. Watching this film is like lingering in the shower, alone with our thoughts.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2024

films.syn: One of the most famous boxing dramas of all time, this film marked the beginning of a brief but important period in Garfield’s acting career. Thanks to celebrated movies such as Body and Soul, Force of Evil and The Breaking Point, he became an essential player of the film noir genre; yet this reputation would not have been so exclusive if Garfield had not created the key titles of his repertoire as independent productions. The gripping story of a boxer who, yearning for a life of luxury, gradually casts aside his ideals and succumbs to corruption, reflects the candid rejection of the capitalist system by the progressive left, championed not only by Garfield but, above all, by screenwriter Abraham Polonsky. His superb and highly evocative performance as the main character earned Garfield his second Oscar nomination.

ap.p: The Life and Times of John Garfield
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Life and Times of John Garfield); production year 1947

films.syn: Jake Williams was the protagonist of the short film This Is My Land (2006) and also the feature-length Two Years at Sea (2011). Together with director Ben Rivers, we now return to the world of this hermit of mythical proportions, someone who might, in fact, be our neighbour. This measured and harmonious film mediates the extraordinary and, for the most part, silent experience of a man, whose inquisitive gaze nevertheless begins to show traces of weariness as the years pass. No matter how lyrically Rivers captures the magic of carefree slumber on a bed of moss, Bogancloch doesn’t offer cheap escapism. There is no need to have things in order for serenity to pervade your lives.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2024

films.syn: It’s the early 1990s and 13-year-old Karolína, a gifted novice singer, is given the chance to become a member of a world-famous girls’ choir, taking her place alongside her older sister and her other rivals in the ensemble. Everything points to the fact that Karolína’s exceptional talent has caught the attention of the formidable and much admired choirmaster. This highly anticipated psychological drama calls to mind not only the notorious case of Bambini di Praga, but also other devastating situations involving the clash of innocence and abusive authority. In a work entirely free of sensationalism, Provazník demonstrates focused humility and extraordinary sensitivity towards his fledgling actors as he depicts an exclusive world, in which desirable prestige goes hand in hand with premature coming of age.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.ot: Ani se nenaděješ a už se jmenuješ
films.syn: Six-year-old Viktorka tries to understand the complicated relationships in her family. Not only is she expecting the birth of a new sibling, but she must also prepare for her first day at school. In dealing with all these challenges, she is helped by her optimism, playfulness, and imagination. The camera sticks to a child’s perspective, from which every day is full of little miracles. Special Jury Mention in the National Competition at the 19th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2025.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: Alina and her son Serik arrive at an elite military school – she as a history teacher, he as a cadet. But the boy has a hard time adapting to the school’s unwelcoming atmosphere and strict discipline, and immediately becomes the target of bullying. When a student is found dead at the school, a local investigator is called upon to unravel the mystery. Was it murder, suicide, or perhaps even the school’s ancient curse? And what role do Serik and motherly love play in it all? Adilkhan Yerzhanov, one of Kazakhstan’s most fertile contemporary filmmakers, returns to KVIFF with a chilling, well-crafted post-horror in which festering suppressed traumas from the regime of the past become even more cruel and vicious in the present.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2024

films.syn: Ester, 45, has devoted her life to caring for her son David, who has an intellectual disability. A trip to Italy to stay with friends brings an opportunity to escape her soul-destroying routine, yet not even a change of scene can alter the fact that life with David isn’t easy. Ester impulsively fires up the old caravan that was intended as their holiday home and it becomes a means to find freedom. The journey through sun-drenched Italy proves therapeutic for both of them. Perhaps only briefly, deep inside, Ester will rediscover someone who has a right not only to give love, but also to receive it. This personal road movie, which saw Czech feature film return to Cannes after an absence of more than thirty years, shows fondness and unsparing openness as it explores themes of body and soul, freedom and resignation, and hope and powerlessness.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2025

films.syn: Alexandre O. Philippe and his films have become a fixture at the world’s leading film festivals, including Karlovy Vary. In his documentaries, Philippe engages in a masterful dissection of cult films that offers audiences an in-depth look at influences, references, and contexts across the decades – and his insightful analysis of that cornerstone of the horror genre, The Texas Chainsaw Massacre, is no different. Through interviews with such figures as director Takashi Miike and author Stephen King, Philippe underscores the revolutionary nature of the now fifty-year-old horror classic while simultaneously expressing his fascination with an often trivialized genre – and with cinema as such.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 2024

films.syn: Young Christy is thrown out of his group home after getting into a fight. While looking for a new place, he finds shelter with his brother, his brother’s girlfriend, and their young child in a rough part of the Irish town of Cork. In his feature film debut, which premiered at the Berlinale, director Brendan Canty shows that flashes of light can be found even in the shadows of the city and the human soul. Christy is an honest, visually compelling drama about fragile ties, sibling loyalty, and the ability to find a home even where one might not expect it. It is an unassumingly powerful film with characters capable of making the most with very little.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Afghanistan under the brutal rule of the Taliban. After surviving her family’s massacre, Leila has just one goal in life: to find her son Omid. But in a country where being a woman means being less than nothing, her chances are desperately slim, and so she chooses an extreme and dangerous solution. She radically changes her identity and sets out on a path where even the slightest hesitation can mean death. In her masterfully crafted second film, Turkish director Gözde Kural applies her familiarity with Afghan society in order to tell a story of oppression that forces individuals into roles – be it borrowed masculinity or forced femininity – that they would never accept in a free country.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Bizarre science fiction or an unbridled burst of Bangkok imagination? While everyone moves within the infinite possibilities of Blank Clock and must turn into its mysterious surface, a new invention unexpectedly comes along to help find the impossible Good Seconds with Crazy Lotus. Special Jury Mention in the Labo Competition at the 19th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2025.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: A person should be a friend and not food. But the psychopath Tucker thinks differently. The shark-obsessed young man lures women onto his boat in order to subsequently toss them overboard to the oceanic predators. But the rebellious Zephyr refuses to give up without a fight. She also hopes that the good-looking Moses whom she met on the shore will manage to save her. While the sharks’ jaws bite, the audience’s jaws will drop. Sean Byrne surfs on the waves of films such as The Silence of the Lambs and Saw, and yet his movie is an original, fine-tuned machine full of action, suspense, and great gags. It also fixes the reputation sharks have had ever since Spielberg, rightfully realizing that sadism is a characteristic not of animals but of man.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2025

films.syn: One day, a lonely Gravedigger, shunned because she stinks of dead bodies, meets the Lover – an elegant aristocrat whose sister has recently died. But their passionate relationship is short-lived. When the Lover tragically dies at sea, the Gravedigger is determined to do anything – anything! – in order to bring her lost love back to life. Canadian actor and director Grace Glowicki has succeeded in creating a stylistically unique and bizarre comic film whose absurd humor and visual style inspired by black theatre celebrate the distinctiveness of independent cinema. Dead Lover pays homage to such cult stories as Bride of Frankenstein while simultaneously updating them and stripping them of their heteronormative standards.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2025

films.syn: Ángela and Héctor are expecting their first child. Ángela is deaf, and the doctors cannot predict whether the child will be able to hear or not. Together, the couple tries to prepare for parenthood and an uncertain future, but already the birth reveals the barriers that Ángela will have to overcome. The arrival of their child tests their relationship, and she gets a taste of what it is like to raise a child in an environment where she does not always feel fully accepted. Director Eva Libertad’s award-winning debut explores not only the complicated relationship between hearing and hearing-impaired individuals, but above all the difficulties of being a mother. The main role is played by her sister, whose point of view of a character with a hearing impairment is underscored through the use of sound design.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Mária, a lonely 55-year-old plastic surgery addict and nail technician, one day finds her former love from her youth, Kálmán, on Tinder. They soon arrange a meeting, but due to Maria’s altered face, Kálmán has no idea that he is preparing to go on a date with his former lover. Special Jury Mention in the International Competition at the 19th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2025.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2023

films.t: Dissection of an Incoherence in Crisis
films.syn: In the hands of director Nausica Serra, a seemingly quiet holiday in a campervan becomes a meticulously crafted, ironic take on how easily we pass on our insecurities without even realizing it. The father always has to be right, the mother would rather agree than argue, and the kids incorporate their parents’ behavioral models into their games. Everything plays out in a friendly, decorous tone, though with a clearly intended subtext: even innocent advice about how to make the best paper airplane can lead to conflict and shake one’s ego. Dissection of an Incoherence in Crisis is a subtly ironic exploration of a world in which behaviors are inherited faster than genes, and where the final word can disarm us completely.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2025

films.syn: War is primarily a human tragedy, but we should not forget that nature typically suffers with us. The documentary film Divia is a darkly immersive meditation which brings to light Russia's unprecedented aggression on Ukrainian soil and its grievous impact on places that issue their indictments in silence: forests turned to ash, fields ravaged by explosions, flooded towns, or rusted hulks of military hardware in devastated regions, where life has faded away. But nature doesn’t just give up and, like her, neither does man and his ambiguous existence. As one side brings destruction, the other – mine clearance personnel, people searching for bodies, ecologists – quantifies the aftermath of the tragedy and restores fragile Ukrainian ecosystems, even while the horizon rumbles on.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Anything can happen in the hour “between dog and wolf” – when the night is ending but the day has yet to begin. Director Terézia Halamová serves up a delicate, stylistically confident character study of a man who exists between the worlds of the stage, the body, and silence. Rudolf works as a stripper, but what truly shapes him is his life off the stage. Dog and Wolf is a charismatic, visually captivating film fully in tune with today’s generation trying to find its way somewhere between cigarettes, melancholy, and the yearning for more. It is a film that will seduce you not only with its story but also, and especially, with its emotions.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2025
Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2025

films.syn: Eva is a popular teacher who is married to the local mayor. Although he has betrayed her trust, she still plans to support his election campaign, and so she starts to volunteer at a local refugee center. Here, she grows close to eighteen-year-old refugee Amir, who charms her with his poetic talents. But the closer they get, the less control she has over the situation. A drama about forbidden love, Don’t Call Me Mama confronts its protagonists with a moral test while provocatively exploring how hypocrisy can masquerade as generosity. Taking full advantage of her experience as a casting director, Nina Knag gets outstanding performances from actors Pia Tjelta, Kristoffer Joner, and Tarek Zayat.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Fragile eighty-year-old Elsie and the vibrant Colleen are separated not just by half a century, but also by the shared wall of their semi-detached house in a small English town. One day, the two women – otherwise accustomed to living in solitude – begin to notice each other’s existence, and an uncommon friendship is born. But although their bond provides mutual comfort, it alarms their previously indifferent surroundings. “I wanted to tell a story about the marginalised and forgotten people in society,” says director Paul Andrew Williams. “I wanted to create an atmospheric and uncertain world and constantly ask the audience to challenge their preconceptions of others.” Come and see two great British actors – Brenda Blethyn and Andrea Riseborough – as you have never seen them before!

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2025

films.syn: Mexican ballet dancer Fernando dreams of moving to the United States and making it on the international scene. Convinced that his lover, the successful American philanthropist Jennifer, will support him, he risks his life to cross the border. When he suddenly appears at her door, he disrupts her carefully guarded world, in which there is little room for Fernando’s dream future. Michel Franco’s provocative, meticulously directed love story full of passion and destructive energy shows the wall that exists between people – Mexicans and Americans, immigrants and those with privilege, men and women – who need each other but cannot find a common language.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Johanna is seventeen and is in love for the first time, although it is a platonic love for her teacher. She confides her feelings, which range from excitement and intoxication to confusion and frustration, to her diary – but the book then falls into the hands of her mother and grandmother. Founded on open dialogues about the characters’ intimate lives, the latest installment in Dag Johan Haugerud’s relationship trilogy won the Golden Bear for Best Film at this year’s Berlinale. With this film, Haugerud again shows that the strength of his work lies both in his ability to create realistic characters and in his use of evocative written and cinematic language.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Czardas of Two Hearts, In the Slovak Valleys and I Love You are just some of the hits which turned pop singer Karol Duchoň into a household name more than four decades ago. At a time when the young generation is rediscovering the legacy of the “Czechoslovak Tom Jones” outside the context of his heyday, Peter Bebjak (The Line, Nineties) presents a stirring portrait proving that the concepts auteur cinema and big audience can coexist in a single, highly appealing endeavour. The film version of Duchoň’s dramatic fate relies on the stage play by Jiří Havelka and Róbert Mankovecký The Earth Remembers (Zem pamätá), and preserves the way in which it looks back at the Normalisation era, without rash judgement, yet with subtle irony.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2025

films.syn: “If travelling all over the country looking for work means being tramps, that’s us,” impulsive Joe Bell responds irritably to the judge’s confrontational tone. Garfield’s hero once believed in good people and good deeds, until he was accused for a crime he didn’t commit, which resulted in a 16-month spell behind bars. People describe Joe as “a nice boy, too. All he needs is someone to believe in him”. When that someone materialises in the form of the attractive, kind-hearted Mabel (Priscilla Lane), Joe senses that fortune hasn’t forgotten about him after all, and he’s finally ready to settle down, despite America’s economic crisis. That is, until fate throws another tragic obstacle in his path. The screenplay for this stirring social drama was written by Robert Rossen, who later directed John Garfield in Body and Soul.

ap.p: The Life and Times of John Garfield
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Life and Times of John Garfield); production year 1939

films.syn: Who could forget the heartrending yet also sarcastic cinematic finale involving two dancing couples, whose gestures and expressions essentially elicit a duel being fought between irreconcilable parties. Here we have Heduš and her mother-in-law coercing their husbands into dancing round a cramped living room at the end of a disastrous Sunday. Of the celebrated Forman-​Passer-​Papoušek trio the one with the keenest sense of satire, the director essentially preserves the unities of action, place, and time; a single day is sufficient for him to wryly demonstrate to what extent destructive behavioural stereotypes and hostile interaction are the product of base materialism. The young twins, in their unruliness hinting variously at the mood within the family, are played with a child’s spontaneity by the Forman brothers.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1969

films.syn: Every Young Man follows the everyday life and dreams of young men serving in the socialist army. Premiered sixty years ago, this film remains poignantly relevant in today’s haphazard world. Its absurdist tone had critics wondering: was this a “politically correct” story or a smartly veiled anti-militaristic message? Applying contradictory points of view from opposing sides, the film is an intellectual provocation to engage in discussions on sensitive themes. FIPRESCI awarded the work at the Karlovy Vary IFF in 1966 and, to mark the Federation’s 100th anniversary, Every Young Man is returning to the big screen to challenge contemporary audiences as well.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1965

films.syn: “Telling a love story may be more difficult than living one,” says popular Italian actor Valerio Mastandrea in relation to his second directorial effort, whose main protagonist (played by the director himself) spends his days in the hospital without a worry in the world. He’s been hospitalized for quite a while, but he has no complaints. He is sheltered from the world, without any responsibilities. Some of the other patients are not as happy, but unlike them he doesn’t feel trapped – until, that is, a young temperamental woman is admitted to the same ward who refuses to accept the unwritten rules of this unusual situation. Mastandrea’s atypical, melancholy romance balances on the boundary between a life full of palpable beauty and the suffering that comes from a state from which there is no return.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Most people are convinced that fish spend their entire lives never making a single sound. But what about those whose journey has ended in a fishing net and who now lie in the refrigerated section of your local supermarket? Everybody deserves to speak at least once in their lives – to sing, even. An elegy to beings waiting for their customers just before closing time, Finnish director Veera Lamminpää’s charming stop-motion animation asks fundamental questions of life: Can an individual’s value be measured in price per kilogram? And do we truly have to swim against the stream?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2024

films.syn: “Just think of him as being the same person you were in Body and Soul, only with a college degree”​ is how Abraham Polonsky (here both screenwriter and director) responds to Garfield’s reservations about playing Joe Morse, the main character in the cult film noir Force of Evil. His seasoned lawyer works for influential mobster Tucker, head of a gang controlling the numbers racket in New York City. Nevertheless, as in the case of the above-mentioned boxing masterpiece, the corrupt, cynical and seductive world of big money clashes with a moral dilemma, represented in Force of Evil by Joe’s complex relationship with his older brother Leo. This arresting film, which Martin Scorsese often cites as a major influence on his work, entered the cinematic pantheon as a standout crime drama with cardinal ethical dimensions.

ap.p: The Life and Times of John Garfield
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Life and Times of John Garfield); production year 1948

films.syn: The signing of the peace accord between the Colombian government and the FARC guerrillas in 2016 led to the formation of the Search Unit for Missing Persons. The act of finding and identifying the missing was thus seen as essential for rebuilding a nation, whose identity is shaped by those who disappeared. This experimental essay interweaves three stories: a female director reconstructing the life of a dead transgender woman through film; an intimate study of the filmmaker’s family, who also dealt with a missing relative; and the testimony of forensic pathologist Karen Quintero. This formally unremitting work finds a compelling balance between the personal and the political, adding conceptual reflections on the texture of the region, on cartography, and the unspoken traumas of Colombia’s modern history.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: One of the most highly regarded films in the Hollywood career of John Garfield is, in fact, his debut, which launched a productive collaboration with directing legend of Hungarian origin, Michael Curtiz (Casablanca). The breezy, joyful atmosphere in the home of music professor Adam Lemp (Claude Rains) and his four talented, musical daughters shifts towards stirring realism with the unexpected arrival of embittered, young Mickey Borden, long-time buddy of one of the girls’ suitors. The likeable outsider with his sarcastic vision of the world, shrouded in a darkly romantic cloud, is the first of Garfield’s irresistible “rebels with a cause”, whom fate didn’t deal an enviable hand. The film earned five Academy Award nominations, one of which went to novice John Garfield.

ap.p: The Life and Times of John Garfield
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Life and Times of John Garfield); production year 1938

films.syn: Rosy young AP learns from multiple psychics that there is a curse on her. In order to rid herself of it, she needs to get a thousand dollars and sacrifice a lamb. So begins her electrifying nighttime ride through the dreamlike industrial streets of Trashtown. It’s a journey filled with improbable encounters, absurd situations, and all kinds of games. American actress Annapurna Sriram’s titillating directorial debut, a reimagining of the Tarot’s “Fool’s Journey,” is an homage to B movies whose sugar-coated exterior hides an intimate, feminist, and in many respects progressive interior.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2025

films.syn: In his fourth feature film Davi Pretto takes the viewer into the near future, where the development of artificial intelligence has brought with it increasing neurological problems. And this is what’s troubling 40-year-old protagonist K, who has lost his memory and can’t remember where he is from. The desolate man has to find out where he really belongs, and his journey through an unidentified city proves absurd, almost tragic. In the context of the ruling caste system, this low-budget dystopia articulates class inequality in contemporary Brazil, moreover, it touches on environmental issues and uses AI to create scenes in the film. The result is formally stimulating, engagé and, at the very least, cautionary.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: “The ghost of the past destroyed the deceptive illusion of the present.” A melodramatically playful and melancholically sombre short film, which reinterprets the incomplete silent picture Survivre (1923, Édouard Chimot), establishing a new order in the tale of a daydreaming passport officer while also adding a musical accompaniment. The hypnotic composition by jazz guitarist Bill Frisell underscores the mood of the film, while time has supplied its patina. How does a work crafted over a century ago speak to us now? And how might disintegrating film stock enhance the story? In his dream-like piece director Bill Morrison skilfully summons the chimeras of a myriad species and demonstrates why iconic Kenneth Anger described his work as “compelling and disturbing”.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: In this visually expressive film that balances between action and drama, the harness worn by actors in wire-fu films becomes a metaphor for our relationship to family and to the heroes of our past. The wire is a guide that allows us to fly, but it also pulls us back to the ground over and over again. Tian Tian and Fang Di are cousins, once almost like sisters, who must reconnect in order to jointly face the past and stand up to a group of ruthless gangsters – in the hopes that one day they might end their frantic flight. The film was shown in the Competition section at this year’s Berlinale.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Karlovy Vary’s ongoing Cassavetes master class continues with this crime drama that put the king of independent cinema decades ahead of the trend towards strong female protagonists in film. His heroine, former mafia lover Gloria Swenson, is elegant, direct, and does not like children. This seemingly controversial attitude is shaken by circumstance, when she crosses paths with six-year-old Phil, who has been orphaned by a mafia hit. This character study possessing elements of neo-noir, for which the recently deceased Gena Rowlands received an Oscar nomination, is less challenging than Cassavetes’s other iconic films. Even so, his signature style characterized by a great emotional intensity achieved through the unconventional use of cinematic language is strongly felt here as well.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1980

films.syn: At first it looks like Mak’s night shift at a gas station will be as uninteresting as all his previous shifts. But the sleepy boredom is unexpectedly interrupted by the arrival of the female truck driver Nada. The at first routine conversation between sales clerk and customer becomes friendly when they discover that they are both from Macedonia – from the same village, even. As the air fills with memories of home, a bond forms between this seemingly incompatible pair. One of the main roles in this story of alienation is played by Labina Mitevska, who made her debut in 1994’s Oscar-nominated Before the Rain.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2024

films.syn: John Garfield was an outstanding actor in many respects; among others, he awakened in viewers a certain fondness even for protagonists who weren’t overly concerned with moral scruples. These include small-time thief Nick, Garfield’s final (anti)hero who, on the run from the law, hides out with a family he takes hostage. The haze of inevitability rising above his character is more palpable than before; Garfield’s prior heart attack and his unofficial blacklisting as a liberal supporting communist influences in Hollywood certainly added to the increasing hopelessness of Nick’s fate. The script for this worthy film noir, today seen as tangible proof of political pressure at the time of production, was co-written by Dalton Trumbo, then using several aliases as another artist who had fallen from grace.

ap.p: The Life and Times of John Garfield
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Life and Times of John Garfield); production year 1951

films.syn: Small hooks dig into the flesh and tear the human body into pieces. Blood flows, an eye pops out of its socket. And all because of one little cube that could just as well be a paperweight. Naturally, the house where this tragedy took place is full of evil, and one drop of randomly spilled blood again feeds the evil forces. In his low-budget directorial debut, author Clive Barker introduced the world to the cult figure known as Pinhead, leader of the “explorers in the further regions of experience” – in other words, those incapable of distinguishing between pleasure and pain. Now, Hellraiser is back in a restored version, but never fear: the blood still conspicuously resembles ketchup, and the torn skin looks like pudding that’s been out on the kitchen counter too long.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 1987

films.syn: In a shiny winter wonderland, friends Piglet and Cow are having a blast ice-skating on a lake. But suddenly a strange and unfamiliar world cracks open underneath them.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: A picturesque coastline, cute animals – yet seen in the context of a contemporary world which no longer offers so much beauty. In their latest film writing/directing duo Poggi–Vinel once again combine surprising aesthetics and moods, and it’s this unusual disconnection which makes their work so exceptional, convincing and provocative. A monkey with a piercing and a penguin with homicidal tendencies underline the fact that loudness and softness aren’t necessarily in contradiction with one another. And the same applies to laughter and sorrow. It’s high time to catapult ourselves into the real world.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.t: How Come It's All Green Out Here?
films.syn: Nikola, 34, is a commercial director, he’s about to become a father for the first time, and he dreams of one day taking his young family on a road trip in an old van he wants to convert into a camper. Over the course of one weekend, however, accompanying his father and extended family to a small village in Dalmatia, where his grandmother’s remains are to be buried, he finds himself looking to the past instead of the future. Ostensibly, nothing remarkable happens during the course of the journey. Yet Nikola Ležaić’s second, quasi-autobiographical work uses subtlety to explore family relationships marred by the passing of time and by communication breakdown. In its own way, the film is also a contemplation of recollections, memory and post-Yugoslav reality.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: John Garfield’s last role undertaken as part of his exclusive seven-year contract with Warner Bros. was Paul Boray, a fiendishly talented virtuoso violinist from a poor background. In this artfully composed melodrama by Jean Negulesco, the master of sweeping emotions, the film's darkly romantic microscope is trained primarily on Paul’s complex love affair with wealthy patron of the arts Helen Wright (the stellar Joan Crawford, shortly after her Oscar for Mildred Pierce). And like the most famous of Dvořák’s Humoresques, the seventh, which lent the film its title, Negulesco’s poignant drama also offers a sparkling array of contrasts – the playful and nimble, graceful motif, set against the exquisite and heart-wrenching emotional tsunami.

ap.p: The Life and Times of John Garfield
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Life and Times of John Garfield); production year 1946

films.syn: Hurikán rushes to save his favorite beer stand from closure by fetching a new keg to impress the bartender he has a crush on. In a wild Prague district, he faces cops, robbers, and his own thirst. Winner of the Audience Award at the 19th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2025.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: On the morning of 24 February, my boyfriend and I decided to travel from Kyiv to Irpin to see his parents. It is hard for me to recall the events of those days. My mind blocks and minimizes all the memories, it erases them, but the only thing I know for certain is that every day everything rapidly became worse. Best Film in the National Competition at the 19th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2025.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.t: I Saw the Face of God in the Jet Wash
films.syn: “I love films that foreground the fact that you are watching film,” states British director Mark Jenkin, who in his film diary returns, among others, to the Cornwall locations which gave rise to his mesmeric Enys Men. The series of Super8 shots taken from his travels and the comprehensive voice-overs make for a fascinating mosaic of encounters, observations, formative quotations from cinematic and other works, and also possible fantasies. Here, Jenkin demonstrates his ability to give his films an appealing timeless quality and to connect the familiar with the curiously enigmatic. One hundred and one interesting facts from the filmmaker’s diary.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.t: If I Had Legs I'd Kick You
films.syn: Her life is crumbling all around her – literally. When a crack develops in the ceiling of her home, she and her sick daughter end up in a cheap motel where her suffering only gets worse. And there is nobody anywhere who might help her. If I Had Legs I'd Kick You is a raw deep-dive into motherhood on the edge – where love is not enough and waves of frustration, helplessness, and anger crash down onto the viewer from the screen. Rose Byrne’s painfully candid performance earned her a Silver Bear at this year’s Berlinale. Shining alongside her are Conan O’Brien and A$AP Rocky. The camera’s hallucinogenic rhythm and the film’s oppressive atmosphere open up cracks between reality and madness until all that is left is an uneasy silence… and the ceiling, falling again and again.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: The life of a young man (Jan Cina) is defined by order and modern technology; the closest he gets to any form of real communication is when he sprays his pet snail with water in its terrarium. But then the most common of all household appliances ceases to function and the man has to go out and be among people. In her short piece set in a familiar future, director Tereza Vejvodová conceivably builds on the aesthetics of her sculptural film accompanying the production Land of Body at Prague’s National Theatre. Intertwining limbs and torsos are extensions of the silent protagonist’s mind; his world is polished down to complete emptiness. What's the point of us having control of our every step if no-one else accompanies us on our walk?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: The most terrifying sound at Cannes this year? The rubber squeaking of an artificial leg. It is the sound of the dreaded torturer in the prison to which Vahid was sent after a show trial. After his release, Vahid one day hears the sound again, and he decides to act: he impulsively knocks the man out and loads him into his van. But can he be sure that he has the right man if he’s never seen his face? Before long, the van fills with other former prisoners to help with the identification. Together, they face a question that haunts many nations: can we exact revenge against a cruel system by taking it out on one individual who loyally serves it? This moral thriller with elements of the darkly grotesque earned legendary Iranian dissident filmmaker Jafar Panahi the greatest award of the festival season: the Palme d’Or.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Willem has just gone through a break-up, and January is the month when everything hurts just a little bit more. Day after day, we watch him pull himself back together, surrounded by friends, family, and unexpected touches of closeness. Director Jetske Lieber’s January is a gentle, sensitively shot film about losses that cannot be measured and relationships that go farther than just romance. It is a subtle portrait of the vulnerability of the young generation, of the queer experience, and of the fragile yearning to be understood. Each gesture has weight, each scene knows its tension. January does not judge; it only sees. And it offers a space for empathy, which sometimes is bigger than love.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2024

films.syn: Jimmy Jaguar, aka Jagu, is a demon who drifts from soul to soul, awakening something dark within. His hosts become vessels of revenge. But whose revenge? And why do their victims, chosen with no clear pattern, all seem to share the same eerie trait? They are alive only because “it is against the law to kill them”. Bence Fliegauf’s latest film – following his acclaimed works from Berlin and Locarno – unfolds across the vast, unforgiving plains of Hungary, where silence hangs heavy and secrets sleep beneath the soil. Listen closely, and you might hear the silence rumble with threat… or catch echoes of a buried past. Or perhaps it's the demon calling – because Jagu needs us all.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Twenty-year-old Lucette works at a karaoke bar. Besides the bar’s song-happy customers, she is kept company by her fairy, who wants nothing but the best for Lucette. But careful! One evening, Diana enters the bar, and Lucette’s world is turned upside down. Is there a song on the karaoke list capable of describing the return of a long-lost love? And what about the fairy? Will she break her magic wand trying to help Lucette? From Belgium comes a musical about breaking up and finding each other again that sparkles in the bright light of a disco ball.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2024

films.syn: A group of individuals each live in tiny, isolated rooms far from the hazards of the outside world. They make a living through live video streaming, connecting with others in the virtual realm. Yet, on one fateful day, a chubby boy stumbles upon a secret. Special Jury Mention in the National Competition at the 19th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2025.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: Social worker Kika suddenly finds herself in a situation that she is used to seeing in her clients. After her partner’s sudden death, she ends up alone with her daughter, pregnant, and without money or a place to live. In a brief moment of hopelessness, she remembers one of her clients, who earned extra money selling used underwear. And so the young woman slowly and hesitatingly becomes part of a profession that couldn’t be farther removed from her original job. Nevertheless, a client is a client, regardless of whether you help them fill out a form or strike them with a long leather whip. Kika is a comedy that humanizes the world of (among other things) BDSM and erotic services in general while giving a voice to those who usually hide beneath the light of red lanterns.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Remo Manfredini is a legendary but hopelessly indebted jockey who is constantly drinking and doing drugs. One important race can still save him, but it ends in tragedy and Manfredini finds himself on his deathbed. Will he get one last chance? Luis Ortega’s genre-busting film follows its silent, self-destructive hero as he is hounded by a mafia boss and his henchmen, and also by his pregnant girlfriend. All along, this absurd tragicomedy somewhat resembles its charismatic protagonist, refusing to follow a strictly defined path, constantly changing direction, and eluding any attempt at categorization.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.t: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II Cinematic Cut
films.syn: The world-famous RPG developed by Prague’s Warhorse Studios makes its cinematic debut as a film specially created for the Karlovy Vary festival. It’s the year 1403, and the Bohemian Kingdom is in chaos. While roaming marauders sow fear and terror through a kingdom without a clear ruler, Henry of Skalitz seeks to avenge his murdered parents. As an ally of the rightful king, he is sent to accompany Sir Hans Capon on a diplomatic mission. After they are brutally attacked, however, Henry and Hans undergo a series of dangerous adventures that subject them and their friendship to the ultimate test. This distinctive piece offers a powerful viewing experience – a treat both for fans of the cult computer game and for those who have yet to enter its intriguing world.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2025

films.syn: A court bailiff in the Transylvanian town of Cluj is having a bad day – the eviction of a homeless man from the basement of a building ends in tragedy, and she begins to wonder, “Was it my fault?” But the people with whom she shares her burden can’t offer an easy answer. Director Radu Jude, winner at KVIFF and the Berlinale, is back with his typical dark humor, aimed straight at a contemporary society full of neglect, nationalism, faith, and shaky moral positions. Shot on a mobile phone over the course of ten days, Kontinental ’25 won the Silver Bear for Best Screenplay at this year’s Berlinale.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: A tadpole somehow misses out on becoming a frog and is left behind, alone. But there is much to discover in the pond, and spring is sure to come again next year. A little story about growing up.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2018

films.syn: A journey to the bowels of the Earth might guide us through our own entrails. In her hypnotic short film, Bolivian artist Luciana Decker Orozco finds inspiration in the work of Peruvian writer Gamaliel Churata, while her mesmeric, strangely tremulous piece exerts an appeal without the need for specific knowledge of the local context. Details of the face and hands of an old woman and the food she eats, and the exploration of caves seemingly shrouded in an aura of horror, play out against a ground plan of personal archaeologies, which connect familiar experiences with something that has transcended our everyday experience for centuries.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: Introverted Princess Saira, daughter of the Queens of planet Clitopolis, is ditched by her charismatic bounty hunter girlfriend Kiki. When she discovers her ex has been kidnapped by the Straight White Maliens, who demand as a ransom the most powerful weapon known to lesbiankind – the Royal Labrys – Saira sets out on an inter-gay-lactic mission to rescue Kiki from the clutches of the evil incels. Along the way she encounters songstress Willow and a questionably macho spaceship, travelling on a journey that becomes a quest of self-discovery. With catchy melodies and pleasing irony, this animated sci-fi comedy by filmmakers Leela Varghese and Emma Hough Hobbs, which won this year’s Teddy Award at Berlin, takes us on a candy-coloured odyssey as it explores the vast reaches of the queer universe.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: No-one shoots like James Benning. Here, the master of contemplative film, whose inner life is much richer than the static shots might initially suggest, dons a more conspicuous suit of political armour and unexpectedly loads his soundtrack with songs – from Sinéad O’Connor and Tracy Chapman to Ricky Nelson. What began 81 million years ago emerged into a bleak 20th century, full of political speeches which often ended merely in words and nothing more. little boy is a stroll through both the director’s and historical memory; watching it is like assembling a construction kit of Benning’s life and much else besides. The dinosaurs got it over with; when’s our turn?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: Lucia is a shy sixteen-year-old girl growing up under the watchful eye of her mother. During a Catholic choir summer retreat, however, she crosses paths with the fiery Ana Maria and a dark-eyed restoration worker. Nature is in full bloom, the scent of rose blossoms wafts through the air, and Lucia discovers the previously unknown language of her body. But are these new feelings at odds with her chastity and her naively pure faith? The intense imagery of Urška Djukić’s debut feature recalls the films of Céline Sciamma and her sensual and imaginative style mixes Christian symbolism with pure physicality, but hers is a distinctive cinematic language that tastes the grapes of our sins. Are they really so sour, or is there something sweet to them as well?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Clémence is separated from her husband and shares custody over their son Paul. The couple has a good relationship, and so Clémence has no problem telling him that in her personal life she now prefers women. But from this moment on, things change. Paul doesn’t want to see his mother, the husband no longer communicates, and the situation culminates in the father being granted sole custody. In order to reconnect with her son, Clémence finds herself forced to defend not only her privacy but also her decision to quit her stable job as a lawyer and become a freelance writer. As brilliantly portrayed by Vicky Krieps, Clémence is a woman who, in her writing, explores motherhood and the status of women while trying to find the boundary between maternal devotion and preserving one's integrity.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Vicky Krieps); production year 2025

films.t: Mad Bills to Pay (or Destiny, dile que no soy malo)
films.syn: Welcome to the Bronx, where people speak loudly and grow up faster than you can say “responsibility.” Mad Bills to Pay, one of the most distinctive films of this year's Sundance and Berlinale’s new Perspectives section, is an energetic mix of humor, melancholy, and social empathy. When fate brings two teenagers together and places them before a crossroads in life, they find that selling Nutties on the beach and immediately spending all your earnings with your friends is hardly a long-term plan. A love letter to the Bronx’s Latino community, the film is a story about the fleeting nature of childhood, the first clashes with reality, and the fact that growing up hurts… even if we laugh at the same time.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: One summer evening in Rome, a table set for dinner, and anticipation. The latest outing by Paolo Genovese, a master of original and intelligent audience favourites, is reminiscent of his global hit Perfect Strangers (incidentally, the film with the most remakes in the history of cinema). This time around, he lets us sit in on a couple’s first date – though certainly not the first first date of either one. Who, however, are the four men and four women bickering about how Pietro and Lara should behave at their romantic dinner? The often contradictory thoughts of the evening’s two protagonists take on human form, and the act of pondering one’s next steps in a delicate situation has never been so much fun. The big audience hit of the year features the cream of Italy’s acting crop, both at the table and “in the head.”

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.ot: C'est arrivé près de chez vous
films.syn: This low-budget film, today a cult classic, is a clever, playful, and cynical postmodern tale and a timeless commentary on the phenomenon of true crime and serial murderers. Shot by three Belgian film students, its style imitating the documentary methods of cinéma verité was a perfect fit for its shocking concept: a group of filmmakers shooting a documentary about a narcissistic killer. The nihilistic, confrontational, and brutally ironic Man Bites Dog caused a scandal in its time. Its central theme of media ethics is typical for the 1990s, but the directors’ approach has lost none of its provocative edge.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1992

films.syn: It’s the year 1872 and the Emperor of Brazil is travelling to Portugal. His comfort will be assured by Maria Henriqueta de Mello Lemos e Alvelos, owner of the grand hotel, whose portrait, however, is absent from the documentation relating to the emperor’s visit. Unlike the letters which gradually reveal the negative aspects of the whole expedition. With the aid of contemporary shots filmed on 8mm, this enchanting short piece allows us the chance to experience this place, with its tangible air of romance, but also to appreciate the dramatic story unfolding in higher social circles. Flawless emotional archaeology.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: Director Celine Song follows up her lyrical Past Lives (2023), a film that made it into the hearts of more than a few viewers, with another look at relationships – this time from a slightly different perspective. Materialists takes us into a world centered not on memories but on possibilities. Dakota Johnson is an exclusive matchmaker who balances between the past (Chris Evans), the present (Pedro Pascal), and what might be if… In a sun-drenched New York full of beauty, glamor, and wealth, beneath the surface of glitzy parties hides the question of whether love can be a matter of choice and what things we are willing to exchange for an illusion of certainty.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: “Envy is the companion of glory” could well be the life motto of Belgium’s Eddy Merckx, one of the most successful cyclists in history. During his career, Merckx won 525 races and was repeatedly tested to the limit. Working with archival footage and interviews, this documentary – screened at the Rotterdam film festival – is a thrilling watch built not around shocking revelations but on a powerful and captivating story.
