ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: The legendary Chinese beings known as jiangshi are something like zombies or European vampires – except that they move around by jumping, they can be stopped with a piece of paper containing a magic spell, and their bite can be counteracted by sticky rice. During Hong Kong’s cinematic boom in the 1980s, producer Sammo Hung built several outstanding horror comedies around the jiangshi, drawing – as he did in most of his films – from the tradition of American slapstick. Director Ricky Lau’s Mr. Vampire is one of the best examples of the typical Hong Kong approach to physical humor with supernatural elements, and it is no wonder that it inspired a number of sequels and other films featuring jiangshis.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 1985

films.syn: Nigeria, 1993. A father leaves his village for Lagos, where he has to take care of some work-related duties. It is the first time he takes his two young sons with him, whom he otherwise doesn’t see very often. But an important election is underway and an explosive political crisis looms in the background. What at first looks like an ordinary day slowly becomes a formative experience that the two boys will remember for the rest of their lives. The first ever Nigerian film to be shown at Cannes is a partially autobiographical impressionist remembrance with a touch of the transcendental in which images of loving parenthood are mixed with the pulsating colors of Nigeria’s largest city and drops of blood spilled for a better future that may never come.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Village girl Bára returns home from the city to introduce her new friend Áňa to her boyfriend Škudlajz and her friends Fox and Houska. But in the end, she discovers that she is ashamed of them and her hometown – and thus of herself as well.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.t: My Undesirable Friends: Part I – Last Air in Moscow
films.syn: Five independent media outlets, seven journalists labeled “foreign agents” by Putin’s regime. In 2021, Soviet-born American filmmaker Julia Loktev documented the everyday reality of independent media in Russia with the aid of her friend Anna Nemzer, a host at Russia’s last independent television station, TV Rain. Screened in this year's Berlinale Special section, the film explores the lives of these bright, witty, and daring women, whose struggle for the truth becomes more complicated and dangerous following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The result is a unique and exceptionally powerful witness to Russia’s escalating totalitarianism bordering on fascism – but above all, it honors the regime’s often neglected opponents.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: In the near, familiar future, where will memory be stored and is it possible that experiences which come back to us have been modified by someone? The film debut of artist Oliver Torr follows a figure wandering through an urban environment, whose dystopian character is further enhanced by an opaque sound design. A work capturing moments when dreams flip over into nightmares and memories feed into the panic of the present. Collapse starts with a single crack.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.t: One Flew over the Cuckoo's Nest
films.syn: Producer Michael Douglas showed considerable courage when he entrusted the rights to a film adaptation of the stage play based on Ken Kesey’s novel to a director from Eastern Europe who was, at the time, virtually unknown in the USA. Miloš Forman repaid him for this decision by delivering a fairy-tale success of a film that took home all five major Academy Awards. The strength of the drama set in a psychiatric hospital also lies in the fact that the escalating psychological duel between a rebellious patient and the institution’s despotic head nurse is a variation on Forman’s key theme – the clash of the free-thinking individual with the power of the ruling establishment. Both lead actors performed their roles of a lifetime here, while the movie marked a crowning achievement in the filmmaker’s career.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Michael Douglas); production year 1975

films.syn: After many years, Suzanne and her two children unexpectedly show up at the home of her sister Jeanne. It initially looks like Suzanne is tentatively attempting to re-establish a relationship with her sister. But this illusion is shattered with the morning light: Suzanne is gone… Nathan Ambrosioni’s intimate film is a portrait of a woman forced to become a mother to children she barely knows. His minimalist, yet profoundly empathetic storytelling lets the audience observe the slow process of coming together, the fears and hesitations of the newborn family, and the absurdities of the non-functioning state apparatus. A French reflection on the fragile nature of co-existence born of necessity, and how strong it can be when born out of love.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Newsreels, recruitment programmes and propaganda films, in combination with commentary from Palestinian refugees in Lebanon. Here, images and words are separated by almost a century in some cases, nevertheless, this conceptual film compilation by anthropologist Diana Allan clearly addresses today’s situation. Shot on 16mm, archive footage of Palestine under British colonial administration encounters the recollections, commentaries and, above all, the songs of recently displaced people; the tragedy of their fate is further underscored by an unpleasant soundscape. Thanks to the concentrated form, the stories of forcible separation acquire a voice they should no longer have been granted.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: Austria in the early 1980s. Perla, a refugee from socialist Czechoslovakia, tries to make art and raise her daughter in a free world far from political oppression. She gradually finds her footing in the artistic community and in a new relationship. But one day the phone rings, and she hears the voice of her former partner and the father of her child, who has remained behind in Slovakia. Perla takes a fresh and highly disturbing look at the recent past. Carefully composed shots, an oppressive atmosphere, and a meticulously crafted story remind us that only recently the world was still divided by borders that cut not only through Europe but also through the minds of people forcefully separated by them.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: It’s a balmy summer evening; we hear insects chirping and girls’ laughter. Yet the Perseids of the title remain on the periphery; the night-time forest is not lit up by comets, but instead by torches and the glow of cigarettes. We don’t see much, nevertheless, our senses are working overtime even so. From the darkness – with the aid of music – director Natalia del Mar Kašik ignites a sense of momentum and a truly joyful mood of affable solidarity somewhere on the border between innocence and adulthood, both offering a hint of adventure in the shadow of the night.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: I saw the best minds of my generation… This verse could describe the ordinarily unordinary day of photographer Peter Hujar. Peter Hujar’s Day is a quiet, focused portrait, told through Hujar’s interview with journalist Linda Rosenkrantz. Their conversation brings to life New York in the 1970s, including the era’s community and the spirit of the times. Hujar’s description of one day is populated with figures such as Susan Sontag, William Burroughs, Glenn O’Brien, and Allen Ginsberg – people whom he knew, admired, and photographed. Director Ira Sachs’s masterpiece, which invites us into Rosenkrantz’s charming West Village apartment, is perhaps best followed up by a glass of wine, a Bob Dylan album, and a few lines from Howl.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Keanu Reeves as young FBI agent Johnny Utah. Patrick Swayze as the free-minded surfer and leader of a group of bank robbers Bodhi. Two men on opposite sides of the law – but also two adventurous souls looking for an adrenaline rush. Their unexpected friendship forms the pulsating heart of this exciting thriller about freedom, loyalty, and moral dilemmas in which Kathryn Bigelow, as so many times in her career, took full advantage of genre conventions while simultaneously redefining them. Action films in the 1990s had no shortage of fearless masculine heroes, but Bigelow created complicated protagonists who develop strong bonds, making Point Break one of the best bromances of all time.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 1991

films.syn: In this captivating drama based on the book telling the story of real-life marine Al Schmid, a simple Philadelphian labourer returns home a hero of the Guadalcanal campaign, where he is permanently blinded in battle. Before he decides to join the Marines, however, this somewhat arrogant charmer falls for the kindly Ruth (Eleanor Parker). Garfield’s fascinating range as an actor is exercised on both an intimate and epic level; he expresses himself in a myriad ways, conveying charm, sex appeal, humour, also bitterness and fear, self-pity and anger. Although lesser known, Pride of the Marines is considered one of America’s finest war dramas, from today’s perspective adopting a remarkably modern stance addressing Americans’ attitude to national minorities.

ap.p: The Life and Times of John Garfield
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Life and Times of John Garfield); production year 1945

films.syn: An unusual green youngling hatches from an egg, and piggy Rosalia enthusiastically takes on the maternal role. This proves to be quite difficult, however, for the youngling has an irresistible appetite and breathes fire. Life in the forest becomes so dangerous that Prince Ki-Ki-Do has to step in.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2020

films.syn: A harsh winter has come to Ki-Ki-Do’s forest. Kind-hearted piggy Rosalia tries to help the animals by knitting warm clothes for them, but the clothes are either too big or too small and completely useless. What a mess. But with the help of tiger mosquitos Tine and Bine, Prince Ki-Ki-Do finds a unique solution.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2017

films.ot: Hore je nebo, v doline som ja
films.syn: 15-year-old Enrique, or Eňo to his friends, is spending the summer with his gran. His time with her is interspersed with rather infrequent visits from his mother Martina, who works far away; all the same, the boy hopes she’ll take him back with her soon. However, contact with his mother dwindles, and her presence is gradually replaced by unflattering village gossip. Enrique decides to investigate the truth. Like her previous short film A Good Mind Grows in Thorny Places (2024), director Katarína Gramatová’s feature debut is also set in the desolate village of Utekáč, where the flaking walls of the houses bring to light the often sombre reality of present-day Slovakia. The leads are played superbly by non-actors, real inhabitants of the Slovak valley, from where it seems an endless distance to the sky above.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2024

films.syn: Three women, three stories of flight from various corners of Africa. They find refuge in one building on the outskirts of Tunis, where they form a fragile alliance and a silent bond of solidarity. But when an abandoned child that has survived a shipwreck appears in their lives, it changes not only the atmosphere in their home but also the inner balance of each of them… Shown in official selection at Un Certain Regard in Cannes, director Erige Sehiri’s film takes a sensitive look at the everyday lives of people united by loss, uprootedness, and the need to find their place and their purpose in a new reality. Highly empathetic yet with a good dose of realism, it forces us to consider questions of community and personal responsibility and to ask ourselves when it is time to take one’s future into one’s own hands.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.t: Put Your Soul on Your Hand and Walk
films.syn: How do the inhabitants of the occupied Gaza Strip live – and how do they die? Young Palestinian photographer Fatma Hassona spent several months recording everyday reality in the volatile territory. In long-distance interviews with renowned Iranian director Sepideh Farsi, she makes the impression of an energetic young woman reporting terrible news as an eyewitness. But their conversations – frequently interrupted by poor signal or hampered by poor video – are also marked by a genuine interest in mutual understanding and closeness, in overcoming the artificial borders of military conflicts. The film will live on, but in April the life of the innocent young photographer was extinguished in an Israeli air raid.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.t: Rain Fell On the Nothing New
films.syn: David has served his time in juvenile detention. His sincere attempts to restart his life as a free individual with better prospects, however, are hindered by a society that can’t overlook the fact that he has a criminal record, nor is it particularly willing to give him a second chance. Will David be able to cope with his increasing feelings of frustration, or will he succumb once more to the lure of crime? Steffen Goldkamp’s feature debut relies on surgically precise direction, carefully constructed atmosphere, and also the discreet empathy with which the filmmaker discovers the intimacy of his antihero hovering on the edge of society. With his softly nuanced performance Noah Sayenko excels in the main role.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Three years after the lyrical romance A Love Song, Max Walker-Silverman demonstrates his genuine kindheartedness as he invites us back to his native Colorado. He acquaints us with the reticent Dusty (Josh O’Connor), whose ranch has burned down in a devastating wildfire. Where will he find the strength to start again? Does the answer lie within the community of people impacted by these same destructive fires? Who knows, maybe he’ll be given the opportunity to try to form a stronger relationship with his daughter, who lives nearby with her mother. This tale of the power of community spirit in difficult times, interwoven with a fine strand of melancholy, is as disarming and subtly engaging as the director’s unshakeable faith in human decency.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: In her previous film, Plan 75 (2022), Japanese director Chie Hayakawa explored a bleak near future. By comparison, Renoir turns its inner eye to the past, specifically to the year 1987 and one chapter in the life of eleven-year-old Fuki. Besides the usual childhood worries, the young girl’s life is affected by her father’s serious illness and her mother’s anxiety due to her husband's absence. Thanks to her passion for the supernatural, Fuki gets into various secretive, often dangerous and confusing, situations. Hayakawa says that she made the film in order to return to her own childhood, when her father was dying. His gift to her in the form of a reproduction of a painting by Renoir gave this exceptionally poetic film its title.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: 29-year-old Ilona and her boyfriend have just moved into a new apartment in a block of flats. When the building’s renovation begins soon afterwards and she befriends Oleg, one of the Ukrainian construction workers, her idyllic notions of a fulfilling life as she approaches thirty start to crumble, like the old plaster on the walls. Gabrielė Urbonaitė’s feature debut is a masterful, contemporary portrayal of the lives of millennials, who on the one hand are exposed to modernity, endless possibilities and Western Europe's constant pressure to perform, while on the other they still carry the traumas of previous generations brought up in the Soviet Union, whose shadows are still alive in the face of current political events.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Every great artist has his own unmistakable signature style. China’s brilliant filmmaker Gan Bi works on the boundary between dream and reality, with cinephile specters from the depths of the subconscious that reimbue the cinematic medium with its forgotten transcendental charm. In his latest opus, he travels through the history of cinema, making five halts along the way: opium-drenched expressionism, a rainy film noir, an Oriental comedy, a metaphysical heist, and above all a hallucinogenic vampire karaoke at the turn of the millennium. Each chapter works with one of the senses, but they all reflect the gripping imagination of the sixth art, cinema, which gives physical form to the unseen – to something that needs to be experienced rather than understood.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Emma and Hasan don’t know each other, but they have much in common. Most importantly, they are both sand thieves. Emma steals it for kitty litter, Hasan for making homemade glass. One day, their lives are disrupted by the discovery of a severed finger, and they learn that the human psyche can shatter as easily as glass… William Blake saw the entire world in a grain of sand, infinity in the palm of the hand, and eternity in an hour. In his debut film, Bangladeshi director Mahde Hasan plucks Blake’s words from the page and blows them across Dhaka until they stick to his protagonists. It is an oppressive portrait of a city full of sand, blended with a stylistically refined elegy about the flow of time, personal privacy, destruction, and the tear-filled valleys of our inner worlds.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Following the great success of The Worst Person in the World (2021), this year director Joachim Trier returned to Cannes with the no less ambitious, sensitive, humorous, and touching Sentimental Value. His leading actress Renate Reinsve is here joined by an ensemble cast of established names, including Stellan Skarsgård and Elle Fanning, in a story about a house full of one family’s memories, joys, and troubles. A bright cast of charismatic characters wanders the cold interiors and complex destinies fill the overgrown garden. The question as to whether it is possible to forget old grievances and build new relationships with others and oneself echoes from wall to wall. Trier’s lyrical audiovisual novel took home the Grand Prix from Cannes.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Stellan Skarsgård); production year 2025

films.syn: The true story of journalist Stephen Glass, who in the second half of the 1990s made up numerous stories he wrote for The New Republic, remains uncomfortably relevant today. Perhaps, in fact, it is more relevant today than ever. Then as now, people’s tendency to mistrust the media reflects not just individual but also systemic weaknesses. While Hayden Christensen plays the naive, sensation-seeking Glass, the film’s emotional center is the excellent Peter Sarsgaard as the magazine’s editor-in-chief, who's gradually losing his patience. More than a drama about one man’s failure, Shattered Glass is a chilling snapshot of the time when the truth began to be defined by how well it reads.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Peter Sarsgaard); production year 2003

films.syn: More than nine hours long, Claude Lanzmann’s monumental documentary consists exclusively of interviews with direct eyewitnesses of the Holocaust and quiet images of a bucolic landscape that looks like an idyllic intermezzo – until we identify various inconspicuous but sinister topographic details: train tracks, a brick building in the background, or a sign reading “Treblinka.” The film’s rigorous form, specifically its refusal to depict the Holocaust through scenes of horror, underscores the rawness of the survivors’ detailed recollections of the most horrific crime in human history. As Lanzmann himself said, “The proof is not the corpses; the proof is the absence of corpses.” One of the most celebrated films of all time, it is being shown at KVIFF to mark the 80th anniversary of the end of the Second World War.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1985

films.syn: Thirty-something Irene is trying to make it in the Italian capital when she is forced to briefly return to her native Rimini. Her parents will be out of town, and Irene’s older brother has autism and can’t be left alone. But the lively forty-something has made up his mind that, once the parents are gone for good, he is not going to live with his sister. Everything he does is aimed at furthering his dream of becoming a pop singer. Siblings is a charming comedy-drama about various diagnoses, the courage required to see the world with open eyes, and how it is never too late to get to know your own sibling.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: The hot sun sears the thumping sound systems, deafening beats echo from the Moroccan rocks, and sweaty bodies abandon themselves to ecstatic dancing. Luis’s search for his daughter has led him here, to this illegal rave, but he is unsuccessful once again. A new trail leads him deeper into the desert, where another rave is planned. But the journey there risks the lives of Luis, his son, and the five nomads they have joined. Oliver Laxe’s transcendental parable tests not only the cinema’s sound system but also the level of tension the audience is willing to bear. The most explosive film shown at this year’s Cannes Film Festival, Sirât is a hypnotically suggestive audiovisual experience with a chilling vision of a world on the brink of collapse, where freedom is merely an illusion, a temporary state without any guarantees.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Brutal yet perfectly impersonal, almost sterile. That is the slaughterhouse where the lives of two men – security guard Jakob and employee Boris – come together. In this place where animals are turned into meat, a different kind of evil is growing, the kind that plays out between people. Exploitation, the abuse of foreign labor, unpaid wages. But even in such an inhospitable environment, there is a place for tenderness and love. The German social drama Skin on Skin is as raw as the meat that comes off the slaughterhouse’s assembly line.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2025

films.syn: We live in a world which is bombarding us with images, stimuli, sensations and demands – what are the possibilities of escape, and which of them are the right ones? Director and artist Anastázie Rainischová responds to the situation with another form of saturation – her short film is surprising for its mutual communication of seemingly contradictory animation techniques. The vibrant playfulness and mischief, and also the palpable unease beneath a veil of melancholy, shift the film’s aesthetics somewhere closer to David O’Reilly. Might the path to Zen take us past absolute overload?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: Even snakes can do yoga and meditate. Join us in a snake meditation, but be careful not to get tangled up.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2018

films.syn: Despite the limitations he faces because he has Down’s syndrome, Beniamin dreams of becoming an actor. He shares a home with his father, who is a fixed point in his life, his safe harbor, someone who will always help and protect him. But now there is more at stake. Acting is a public activity, and as such it will subject Beniamin to the judgment of others. Will the father still protect his son, or will he allow him to follow his dreams even at the risk of being hurt? Dominik Mirecki’s tender drama explores questions of parenthood and the choices we must make in order to give others the freedom to grow and mature.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2024

films.syn: ​Sorry, Baby is the directorial debut of actress Eva Victor, who also portrays the main character, an English professor whose quiet life in a New England university town is disrupted by a traumatic event. Told in non-chronological order, Victor’s drama avoids the clichés usually associated with depictions of trauma, taking a senstitive yet slightly humorous look at the process of personal change and recovery. Characterized by both mature acting and directing, Sorry, Baby excels thanks to the nuanced psychology of its characters. Winner of the Waldo Salt Screenwriting Award at Sundance and shown in the prestigious Directors’ Fortnight section at Cannes, the film is yet another confirmation of Victor’s multifaceted talents.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: It isn’t often that a film, when screened at the very beginning of the Cannes Film Festival, ends up being debated throughout the festival. But Sound of Falling is one of the cinematic events of the year, a film that isn’t afraid of its own ambitions and offers an uncompromising and innovative vision. At the center of the story are a farm in eastern Germany and the loosely intertwined lives of four generations of women, spread out over an entire century. A dark chronicle, a living nightmare, and a stylish polished obsidian taken from the hellscape of the twentieth century, the film explores warped desires, generational traumas, patriarchal rule, and the sad events of modern history, which tear the human soul like a roaring combine shreds the ears of grain.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Ella and her best friend Spider love using their imagination to make spiderweb drawings together. But creative cooperation doesn’t always come easy…

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: Two married couples and a common dilemma – their relationships aren’t what they used to be, and each partner is perhaps yearning for something else. The idea of having open relationships shakes up their friendship and questions certainties that they had previously considered solid. Working with a light touch, director Michael Angelo Covino (who also plays one of the leads) has created a relationship comedy full of provocative chaos, lively characters, and fresh directorial ideas. Dakota Johnson, Adria Arjona, and Kyle Marvin complete Covin’s excellent foursome balancing on the threshold between desire and stability. And in-between swim aquarium fish strongly reminiscent of high church officials.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: This animated musical follows the journey of its main character, an anthropomorphized stone. On a path filled with mysterious encounters and hidden symbols, Stone of Destiny is driven by a desire for freedom.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2025

films.syn: Social outreach workers Amin and Mitchell from a poor part of town must contend not just with a zombie apocalypse and alien invasion, but also with unscrupulous developers and a girlfriend’s missing dog. This Dutch horror comedy is a perfect example of light “midnight” horror entertainment featuring unforced satire, here aimed primarily at the issue of gentrification. Director Michael Middelkoop has created a brisk addition to the trend of self-ironic, intelligent B-movie fun, managing to include local themes while still relying mainly on original, universally understood absurd ideas, spiced up with a touch of the disgusting and grotesque.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2024

films.syn: The long-awaited, first Czech Viet-feature is finally here! This authentic portrayal of a community that has become an organic part of modern Czech history is brought to us courtesy of Dužan Duong, a standout, exceptionally talented representative of the first Vietnamese generation to grow up in the Czech Republic. The third millennium has hardly begun and 17-year-old Kien with his crazy red hair returns to his family and their market stall in Cheb after ten years spent in Vietnam. However, instead of the warm welcome he had anticipated, he finds an estranged father, a careworn mother and a younger brother who doesn’t cut him any slack. Told with lightness and wit, this story about cross-generational conflict and much else besides is an affectionate and bold milestone in the debate on cultural identity.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2025

films.syn: Siblings Tom, Susan, and Derek come to visit their grandfather, who recently became a widower. They each have their own worries, and what is more, little Tom can’t get to sleep. But when Susan conjures forth amazing tales by tossing three special words into their grandmother’s old straw hat, they find that stories can be immensely powerful. Not only can they lessen your fears or sorrows, they can also bring people together and offer them hope. This feature-length, stop-motion adaptation of Arnošt Goldflam’s Of Unwanted Things and People, which has been shown at the Berlinale and Annecy festivals, among others, is a visually rich bouquet of fairy tales whose inventiveness and humanity will touch hearts great and small alike.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Sixteen-year-old Michele works as a cowboy on the open plains. Together with his colleague, 21-year-old Alexandra, he offers tourists horseback rides across the vast fields. But nothing has been the same since the dramatic events of last winter. Special Jury Mention in the International Competition at the 19th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2025.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: The moment they greet each other at their friends’ wedding, we know that Leili and Pasha were once a couple. But something split them apart. We see their story in flashback. The start of their romance was literally explosive, and it looked as if Pasha wouldn’t survive. But their mutual attraction would not be deterred by his burns and his slight concussion, and the couple slowly moved from an initial infatuation to a more serious phase in their relationship, when it was time to make more difficult decisions than where to go for dinner. And thus came the moment of separation… A charming mix of genres, Iranian director Ali Behrad’s second feature film is a vibrant portrait of Tehran and its inhabitants, who lose none of their élan even in the face of a difficult political situation.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2025

films.syn: Defeated in combat, Ángel returns home to his village in a remote part of the Peruvian Andes. When he arrives, however, he finds the place has completely changed. What was the 18th century is now the present day. What has become of the ideals of the revolution he fought for? The people who live in Peru today, what are they fighting for? The Anatomy of the Horses takes the viewer on a visually and intellectually stimulating journey through the space-time continuum, during which director Daniel Vidal Toche reflects upon whether the struggle against oppression and exploitation in Peru will ever come to an end. Through the character of Ángel, and also Eustaquia, a girl searching for her sister, he also questions whether revolutionary thinking should be consigned to the past.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Christmas Eve, a broken tooth, and just one dentist on call – thus begins the strange odyssey of the newly sober Cliff and the lonely Didi through the streets of Baltimore. Jay Duplass has shown his sense for distinctive characters and unpredictable situations on numerous occasions as a director, screenwriter, and actor. Directed with a light and empathetic touch, The Baltimorons sketches out a melancholically humorous duet between two people who don’t even realize that they deserve to be main characters. But with each stop on their path towards understanding themselves and each other, it becomes clear that we all are the makers of our own fortune, and that, if we don’t change anything, nothing will change.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Departures from realism take many forms in Latin American cinema. Six years after the neon-lit dystopian near future of Divine Love, in which Brazil is dominated by conservative evangelical values, Gabriel Mascaro returns with yet another novel vision. In order for Brazil to develop economically, the country gives priority to its younger generations, while older people are put away in government colonies so they will not “get in the way.” The nearly 80-year-old Tereza, however, refuses to accept her fate and decides to escape. A socio-critical exploration of discrimination against the elderly and a Gulliverian odyssey across the Amazon, Blue Trail emanates its protagonist’s vivaciousness, charm, and untamed yearning for freedom.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: At the 1982 Cannes Film Festival, Wim Wenders invited several of his esteemed colleagues to a hotel room, where he filmed their reflections on the future of film. This exclusive documentary survey, Room 666, inspired two Czech producers to engage in a similar undertaking in collaboration with the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival. During last year’s festival, they thus invited around thirty Czech or Czech-based filmmakers from all generations and asked them “what makes Czech film Czech?” The result is an exciting mosaic not just of views and opinions, but also of mannerisms and personalities.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2025

films.t: The Death of the Beautiful Deer
films.syn: Four names determined the successful adaptation of Ota Pavel’s short stories – director Karel Kachyňa, cameraman Vladimír Smutný, editor Jiří Brožek and actor Karel Heřmánek. Kachyňa cemented his reputation as a masterful narrator when, aided by resourceful editing, he organically combined motifs from different stories to craft a composition in which the shimmering, joyful mood, enhanced by poetic lensing, starts to dissipate beneath increasingly dramatic tones. The idyllic 1930s have now been replaced by the German occupation, and Heřmánek’s enchanting Jewish Electrolux salesman finds himself an outcast, who resolves to do something extremely dangerous for the sake of his sons.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Jiří Brožek); production year 1986

films.syn: For the past three months, Candice has been exploding every day. Sometimes even two or three times a day. Her record is seven times. She currently has 192 explosions to her name. The French creative duo Poggi and Vinel presents another incomprehensible yet poignant exploration of the remote corners of the human soul. Best Film in the Labo Competition at the 19th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2025.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: Fearless young Mei leaves China for Rome in search of her older sister, who has gone missing. Yun had gone to work in the Eternal City some time earlier, and it is possible that she has become entangled in the Italian capital’s criminal underworld concentrated in the multiethnic neighborhood around Piazza Vittorio. There, the foul-mouthed head cook at a fading restaurant has been forced to take over from his father, who has suddenly disappeared. A colorful and entertaining mix of genres featuring elements of film noir, thriller, romance, kung fu, and comedy, this exceptionally capable and consummately filmed mosaic is also an unassumingly human portrait of the world of immigrants.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Endocrinologist Maurizio Bini, the central figure of the documentary The Good Doctor​, is a department head at the Niguarda state hospital in Milan. His patients include couples who are having difficulty conceiving, and also people undergoing transition. Bini doesn't judge, but tries to give each individual complex care, thus treating not only their body but also their spirit. Although the film relates specifically to Italy, the issues it raises are absolutely universal, among them, the importance of a public healthcare system that provides care to all who need it. The camera never shows the protagonists from up front but always in profile, as if it was just another person attending the meeting with the doctor. This approach gives the film the kind of intimate feeling that its subject definitely deserves.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: The hills of Iceland, the ocean, and the country’s endless roads winding through the landscape form the backdrop for Hlynur Pálmason’s fourth feature film – this time about the silent disappearance of love and a marriage falling apart. Melancholic hygge is mixed with elements of magical realism, thus lending Pálmason’s signature style a new element: humor. The juxtaposition of pain with absurdity paints a picture that is both light-hearted and deeply moving. The authentic performances of the married couple and their children (played by the director’s own offspring) add a sense of warmth and sympathy. An important role is also played by the faithful border collie Panda, who was awarded the Palm Dog award at Cannes for best canine performance.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Spring is in the air, and Nicolau has just turned twenty-four years old, but he doesn’t feel like throwing a big party. He is beginning to sense that his dream of being a professional musician is falling apart, he still lives with his parents, and he pines for his former girlfriend. Though he lacks the energy to move forward, fate throws several opportunities his way to take control of his life again. With his debut feature – a sun-drenched Lisbon tale about the carefree naiveté of youth that brings to mind the films of Rohmer – João Rosas follows on not just his shorts Entrecampos (2012), Maria do Mar (2015), and Catavento (2020), in which he depicted Nicolau’s childhood and adolescence, but also the legacy of earlier Portuguese auteur filmmakers.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Leo and Diana, a rich couple, bring a broken television to a recycle point, where they meet Salif and his son, two scrap dealers. Diana asks them to come to their house to collect more items. Once there, Leo watches them with mistrust as they collect objects, until he sees that the scrap dealers have something they want themselves. Winner of the Grand Prix in the International Competition at the 19th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2025.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2023

films.t: The Mysterious Gaze of the Flamingo
films.syn: Eleven-year-old Lidia is growing up in a loving community of trans women in a mining town in northern Chile. It is 1982, and a mysterious and deadly illness is ravaging the area. Many are convinced that it is spread by the gaze of two men who fall in love with each other. Despite hostile rumors and attitudes, Lidia is not afraid to confront others, especially when the situation spirals out of control. Diego Céspedes’s directorial debut won the Un Certain Regard section at Cannes. A story about queer life at a time that was less open to otherness than today, it is a modern western about fighting prejudice, surviving in a hostile environment, and the complexity of love – which can be a refuge for one but a source of danger for another.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: In the middle of the lake lies an island – silent, abandoned, without the clear promise of anything unusual. Bětka, her older sister Marie, and their friend Alma are spending the summer here, the days flowing like still water. When they randomly visit the island, the natural landscape around them begins to change – and the emotional one inside them as well… Vojtěch Strakatý’s second feature film is a gentle study of girlhood, the yearning for a different world, and the fragile search for happiness, which may lie elsewhere – or not exist at all. In a poetic Bohemian summer where the buzzing of insects mixes with the sound of the rustling grass, we observe the girls’ friendship as something mysterious and half-dreamed. The only thing we know for sure is that the other side of summer is when summer ends.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Celebrated in a number of film versions, James M. Cain’s controversial novel attracted the attention of major studios immediately after its publication in 1934. The rights were ultimately acquired by MGM, which nevertheless had to wait a decade before the censors relaxed. Cast alongside the exquisite Lana Turner was John Garfield, whose seven-year contract with Warner Bros. was coming to an end. Shortly after the Second World War came a film noir par excellence, featuring a cast headed by a darkly charismatic antihero, a drifter who succumbs to the charms of a femme fatale and agrees to a radical proposal to remove the impediment to their all-consuming passion. Frank Chambers and Cora Smith are still considered one of the most magnetic on-screen couples of all time.

ap.p: The Life and Times of John Garfield
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Life and Times of John Garfield); production year 1946

films.syn: A group of young people set out into the Texas countryside. The sun is scorching, the air heavy, and in an abandoned house somebody is waiting who won’t ask you your name – only how fast you can run… When Tobe Hooper unleashed his low-budget horror on the world in 1974, nobody could have guessed that they were witnessing the birth of one of the greatest cult films of all time. The Texas Chainsaw Massacre gave us the iconic Leatherface, a character whose raw brutality and quiet anger has gotten under the skin of multiple generations of moviegoers. In the late 1980s and early 1990s, the film was one of the most popular titles on VHS – played, banned, copied, adored. It is a film that does not age. It only rots. And we keep watching.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1974

films.syn: A film about the all-consuming experience of mourning. Benedict Cumberbatch plays a recently widowed man who, besides falling apart under the weight of his grief, must contend with the feelings of his two young sons who have just lost their mother. The dark silhouette of a crow – that symbol of pain and the incomprehensible – stalks their home as a reminder of a loss that cannot be ignored. The only way forward is straight ahead. Director Dylan Southern transforms the source material into a raw, poetic portrait of grief that is profound, personal, and terrifyingly universal. The Thing with Feathers has already been screened at Sundance and the Berlinale.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: University professor Ali lives a comfortable life until the moment his mother dies. Was her death caused by Ali’s father and, by extension, Turkish society’s patriarchal culture? Ali’s mind dreams of cold-blooded vengeance, a desire that begins to take on real contours when he encounters a mysterious vagrant capable of doing any job. Alireza Khatami’s third feature film is one of the year’s best genre benders: what begins as a realistic moral drama turns into an existential, nightmarish thriller full of violence, layered metaphors, and the posthumous influence of Abbas Kiarostami or David Lynch.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: It’s the end of summer. Danielius, a new father in his mid-thirties, leaves his family in Norway and travels to his native Lithuania to sell his parents’ flat. He tries to reconnect with old friends, but the strong bond he once had with them is now broken. Instead of rushing back to his young family to escape the deafening loneliness, he decides to stay, allowing himself to be guided by his solitude. In his feature debut, director and cameraman Vytautas Katkus indirectly builds on his own short filmmaking endeavours, in which he works deftly with an authentic space familiar both to himself and his protagonists, while also adopting a loose conception of time. Here, time seems to have stopped completely in a world which lights up the fragility of the human soul and images of a home that is no longer ours.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: A celebration of life and reconciliation and a colorful postcard from the early 1990s. Wai-Tung is an immigrant from Taiwan living happily in New York with his boyfriend. When he enters into a sham marriage with the temperamental painter Wei-Wei in order to get her a green card and placate his traditionally-minded parents, it would seem that they have found the perfect arrangement… until, that is, his parents arrive in New York. Lee’s groundbreaking queer romantic comedy was a winner in Berlin and launched its director’s illustrious career.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1993

films.syn: A tender horror flick, an experimental melodrama. Any attempt made to categorise this unconventional cinematic experience seems inadequate. Greek director and musician Alexandros Voulgaris, a.k.a. The Boy, brings us an unusually intimate, yet expressively powerful study of an artist on the brink of middle age. All fears, anxieties and hopes are embodied in the character of Margo, a songwriter who was once famous but who now isolates herself in her apartment. A party held to celebrate her 40th birthday and the emotions that are born there unexpectedly help Margo enter a new stage in her life.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Garfield’s boxing champion Johnny Bradfield becomes a suspected murderer overnight. Fearful of the ruinous intervention of blind justice, he goes on the run and eventually ends up on a date farm in Arizona, an unofficial reform school for young offenders. Will his confrontation with these affable adolescents and with the kind-hearted blonde Peggy restore Johnny’s shaken faith in the impartiality of the judiciary? Warner Bros. Studios installed Busby Berkeley behind the camera, until that time a respected director of lavish musicals, who succeeded in crafting an agreeably forthright crime drama featuring magnetic performances from the cast. The Warner clan were rubbing their hands: they had a true film star in their midst.

ap.p: The Life and Times of John Garfield
ap.sel: Officially selected (section: The Life and Times of John Garfield); production year 1939

films.syn: Hayk, an introverted child, lives with his aunt Narine in a remote Armenian village. While Narine cares for him as if he were her own son, Hayk is finding it difficult to fit in with the local teenagers, who amuse themselves trying to toughen him up. When his young mother Anahit returns home after a lengthy period abroad, she upsets the patriarchal order in the village with her striking appearance and rebellious nature, ultimately inciting a conflict for which no-one is prepared. This cryptic, visually and aurally mesmerising film, viewed through the eyes of a child forced to grow up too soon, is dominated by the all-pervading motif of the wind. Its rustling stirs the tension in a radicalising conservative society, while its wailing heralds the irreversible consequences of raging human emotion.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Perhaps they were once tigers, creatures that roamed free and allowed no-one to dictate the terms. Yet now they are docile rabbits wracking their startled brains to figure out just how they got so tame. This is the way things seem for Jan, a vet who believes all his life decisions are being made by his enterprising wife Olga. With a view to regaining the wilder aspects of his past, the best he can come up with is to feign illness and get himself committed to a psychiatric facility, thus extricating himself from his wife’s influence. Do men really have it that bad? Is it so difficult to work things out with women? Are real men now on the verge of extinction? And can you turn your life around at this late stage? This tragicomedy examining human relationships and gender roles provided a great opportunity for actor Jiří Bartoška.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Jiří Bartoška); production year 2016

films.t: Time Is Running Out and the Water Is Rising
films.ot: Času je málo a voda stúpa
films.syn: “He was that stone in the water. Water flowed over him and he didn’t move. Everything brimmed over and he just stood there” – keyboardist Jaro Filip on his musical buddy of many years. In 2025 we mark thirty years since the untimely death of an exceptional figure of Slovak culture, rock and art-rock musician and filmmaker Dezider Ursiny. Ursiny crowned his modest yet remarkable career as a documentarist with a film essay exploring fundamental issues of human existence and controversial themes such as freedom, death, love, suffering, dignity, euthanasia and suicide. With humility and a gift for crafting refined audiovisual commentary, joining Ivo Brachtl he gives the floor to thinker Eduard Tomáš, Rabbi Karol Sidon, and writers Daniela Hodrová and Daniela Fischerová.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past); production year 1997

films.syn: The observational documentary screened in the Competition section at this year’s Berlinale traces a year in the lives of students and teaching staff at various schools in Ukraine. What at first glance appear as routine activities – lessons, welcoming first-year pupils, school-leaving exams, or the sound of the last bell – acquire fresh significance in the context of war. The conflict itself is never explicitly shown on camera; nevertheless, its presence has deeply penetrated the mosaic of daily life. Despite the pervasive sense of unease, classes are still conducted in destroyed buildings and air raid shelters, becoming a symbol of the defiance and perseverance of Ukrainian society. In fact, the children are taught the most important thing of all: not only how to stay alive, but also how to appreciate the pleasure of being alive.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: The backdrop might remind some people of the TV news from the 1980s, while others may recall the setting of the classic horror film The Hills Have Eyes. But what we are actually seeing is an urban combat facility in West Germany being used to train British soldiers before deployment in Northern Ireland. A thought-provoking film shrouded in an atmosphere of ruination, which director Feargal Ward masterfully navigates through disturbing territory. Yet Tin City doesn’t remain in the past and, along with various mannequins, new questions emerge with every passing minute. Are similar places destined to fall into decline? What do they tell us about the historical events they help to shape? And what space, if any, should terrorists be given in a public environment?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: By train on an outing, by train off to war. A film from a time when dining cars still had their own kitchens, but also a time when trains carried people to their deaths. Named Best Film at the IDFA, Trains sets out on a journey through collective memory, with hope and euphoria alternating with suffering and destruction. Polish director Maciej J. Drygas has edited together footage from forty-five archives into a documentary collage ranging from scenes of fashion shows in train cars to footage of mutilated soldiers – all without additional commentary. Trains confirms that, although the times may change, Franz Kafka’s words that frame the entire film remain searingly topical: Hope really isn’t for everyone.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: Germany, September 2014. A Syrian refugee camp has opened on the outskirts of Berlin. Visual artist and filmmaker Ammar al-Beik has a cubicle assigned to him for seven months and, in order to survive here, he has to film, document, and rebel against the conditions of life in exile, and also against the established rules of documentaries and features. His phone camera is always switched on; he transforms his tiny room and the entire dismal compound into a universe with its own laws. Ammar’s explosive film is the result of ten years of editing; the intensive autobiography intersects the history of Europe and the Middle East, and film history, too. The singular cinematographic form is flanked with memorable individuals who, like exiled Ammar al-Beik, are merely searching for freedom and truth.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: The Soviet Union in the year 1937. Newly appointed local prosecutor Kornev receives a letter written by an unjustly imprisoned man in his own blood. Thanks to his stubborn persistence, the young dedicated communist manages to visit the prisoner, who is being harassed by agents of the secret police. He even makes it to the general prosecutor’s office in Moscow. But besides bringing him to the attention of the authorities, his activities also cause him to question his undying faith in the regime. The suspiciously silent corridors of Loznitsa’s adaptation of Georgy Demidov’s eponymous novel are filled with the ghosts of Gogol and Kafka, meticulously staged geometric camerawork, and above all the many symptoms of totalitarianism that seem to reappear in history over and over again.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: João wins the main part in a period drama about the gender-nonconforming João Liberada, a character persecuted by the Portuguese inquisition. As the film’s production moves forward, the actress finds herself getting into conflict with the director over how the legacy of this character – who, though fictitious, is inspired by historical records – should be depicted. Her critical stance embodies the central dilemma of Paula Tomás Marques’s debut feature: can one properly express the subjectivity of a queer individual when the very existence of queer people has not been reflected by history – in fact, has been denied by it? Her inventively layered film asks pertinent questions about the complex nature of telling historical stories while coming up with its own queer counter-history.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: In the forest there lives a magical unicorn capable of healing any wound. All you have to do is touch its horn and everything in life is immediately brighter and more colorful. But is that what everybody wants?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2022

films.syn: Harris Dickinson, known for portraying the naive Carl in Ruben Östlund’s 2022 film Triangle of Sadness, returned to Cannes this year in a new role: as a debut director. His freshman film Urchin follows the young Mike as he repeatedly tries to escape the clutches of his drug addiction. This raw portrait of darkness and hope – which dims with each setback but is never extinguished – reflects Dickinson’s personal experience working as a volunteer at a community center. Frank Dillane fleshes out Mike as a fragile soul full of contradictions in a performance that earned him the Best Actor award in the Un Certain Regard competition.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: An uncrowned masterpiece of last fall’s movie season, Venice Grand Jury Prize winner Maura Delpero’s second feature returns to the time and place of her father’s childhood. The end of the Second World War is in sight, including in the village of Vermiglio high in the Dolomite mountains of northern Italy. But the sudden arrival of the deserter Pietro shakes up the quiet routine of the local teacher’s family and has a fateful influence on his eldest daughter Lucia. In this carefully composed, breathtaking opus, the intimate and the epic are locked in a natural embrace. Encounters with dignified beauty are often muted, as is the evocative depiction of Vermiglio and the plight of its inhabitants.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2024

films.syn: What would it be like to become an animal? And would this transformation also bring relief? While we watch flickering shots of nature and people, someone speaks of sentiments, memories, and fears. With the aid of an unsettling music score director Lorenzo Pallotta crafts what might essentially be described as an adventurous atmosphere, nevertheless, his exploration of mysterious places and deep-seated feelings is dominated by a sense of melancholy and, at times, an almost depressing uncertainty. And the deliberate vagueness of the entire film, coming from several directions, creates an irresistibly enigmatic mood.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: The Irish documentary We Beg to Differ follows a group of people who feel that the system has forgotten about them. Living on the margins, amidst the dark green of Ireland’s countryside and the gray of its society, they seek out ways of feeling the pulse of life. They find a refuge in diffing – driving dangerously in old cars, doing donuts on meadows and in empty parking lots, the smoke of the tires mixing with adrenaline and dust to briefly drown out everything else. In their language of togetherness, silence is replaced by the roar of the engine and emptiness by shouting. We Beg to Differ is an evocative meditation on the yearning to belong, on resistance born of movement, and on how beautifully it hurts to be different. It is a portrait of a generation that creates its own society when existing society rejects them.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2024

films.syn: Alice and her two children are once again in court to see whether they will stay in her care or will have to be returned to their father. The pressure builds, and each of them gradually succumbs to its weight. We Believe You captures, with haunting precision, the moment when personal testimony comes into conflict with the soulless mechanisms of justice. Working with minimalist expressive means for maximum impact and set in one room with several characters and points of view, the film unspools a drama about responsibility, fear, motherhood, and mistrust. About how difficult it is to speak when every word counts. And about the uncertainty of whether anyone is even listening.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.t: We've Got to Frame It! (a conversation with Jiří Bartoška in July 2021)
films.ot: Musíme to zarámovat! (rozhovor s Jiřím Bartoškou v červenci 2021)
films.syn: Jiří Bartoška, charismatic commentator on the world around him, who possessed one of the most fascinating Czech(oslovak) destinies of the past fifty years, was certainly not one for self-admiring glances in the mirror of memories. The president of the Karlovy Vary film festival vigorously rejected all suggestions for a biographical work or film portrait; he was irritated by the pathos associated with official versions of personal life narratives. Thus all the more valuable (and hitherto unseen!) is the bard’s affable, informal exchange with producer Milan Kuchynka, in which he touches upon a myriad themes, from his grammar school days and the Velvet Revolution, to his encounters with stars – and this conveyed with playful ease, blistering irony and affectionate wisdom.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tribute to Jiří Bartoška); production year 2025

films.t: What Does that Nature Say to You
films.syn: Working with motifs in the style of Eric Rohmer and Woody Allen, the filmmaker sends his protagonist, a man well into his thirties who still hopes to become a poet, on an unplanned visit to his girlfriend’s family. Here, he must face situations that alternate between torturous banality and bitter absurdity, with conversations that lay bare the values of the middle-class household. But even the main protagonist is not spared the film’s subtly ironic gaze. Director Hong Sang-soo, who has been a regular presence at prestigious festivals for nearly thirty years, showed his film at this year’s Berlinale.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.t: When a River Becomes the Sea
films.ot: Quan un riu esdevé el mar
films.syn: After a period of thirteen years Pere Vilà Barceló returns to the Crystal Globe Competition with an uncompromising, introspective probe into the soul of a girl who is sexually abused. The heroine of his sixth film is Gaia, a young archaeology student, whose relationship with herself, and with those around her, is forever marked by a traumatic event. Initially, Gaia cannot find the words to describe her situation, let alone the courage to speak about it. Eventually, however – like an archaeological excavation – she begins to uncover fragments of the past in order to piece her life together. The Catalan filmmaker was able to provide a realistic depiction of her situation by choosing to emphasise the actual process of coping with the trauma, a process which can't be rushed.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: When a young girl picks up the phone in 1992, everything changes – the disintegration of the country brings with it the collapse of personal assurances and subsequent traumas. And while we observe fragments of a child’s memories being pieced together, we are addressed by a pragmatic adult voice hoping to find equilibrium. This extremely fragile, yet also analytically reserved film avoids all retro sentiment, nevertheless, its analogue patina has immediate appeal. Iva Radivojević moves hypnotically between the familiar and the disturbingly unfamiliar, between the matter-of-fact and the poetic magic of dreams. How much can we believe our own recollections, how often do we go round in circles revisiting them? If the books written by Annie Ernaux were films, this is what they’d look like.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2024

films.syn: A small bark-beetle girl lives peacefully in a tree in a forest. However, a fire caused by irresponsible humans burns the forest to ashes. Her hand is burned to charcoal and she is separated from her family. Lost in a human town, she has to face the dangerous world of giants on her own.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: Tireless and implacable critic of contemporary Israel Nadav Lapid is back with the explosive Yes, which this year was shown in the Cannes film festival’s Quinzaine des cinéastes section. Musician Y. divides his time between everyday family life and wild parties at which he and his wife earn a living performing degrading acts for Israel’s rich elite. One day, however, Y. is asked to compose a new national anthem. All this against the backdrop of the shocking events of October 7, 2023. Nadav Lapid knows no compromise. He throws his protagonists into frantic, twisted, and opulent situations, unafraid to turn them into caricatures in order to emphasize his view of a controversial situation in a controversial country.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Few hold such fascination for mystery aficionados as the elusive murderer known as the Zodiac. When British director Charlie Shackleton failed to secure the rights to a book written by a former traffic policeman convinced of the killer’s identity, he decided to make a film about a film that never got made. This experimental work is both a multilayered and entertaining documentary, which deviates from the true crime genre for the very way in which it rejects self-centered respectability. This clever and playful piece, whose generous voice-over leaves even more to the imagination, was awarded at this year’s Sundance festival. A true crime phenomenon like no other.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: A group of high school students and their teachers set off for a class trip to Bulgaria. When their bus breaks down, they find themselves stranded in an old hotel near the mountains. The atmosphere grows tense when the quiet and withdrawn Tsotsa decides to talk about his best friend’s recent suicide. Why did Andrij choose to end his life? And wouldn’t it have been better if Tsotsa hadn’t brought it up? Like his previous outings, Serbian director Miroslav Terzić’s third film is characterized by an overwhelming, meticulously crafted sense of tension. 3 Weeks After takes us into the vulnerable world of adolescents, where innocence is mixed with cruelty. It also exposes the mechanisms of bullying in a society that closes its eyes at decisive moments when looking away is the last thing we should do.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: Thirteen years after Milan Daniel suffered a serious head injury in a racially motivated attack, his assailant is set to be released. What feelings does this moment awaken in a traumatized man who, though he survived, will forever suffer the consequences of that fateful day? Straddling the line between fiction and documentary, the feature debut by Slovak directors Šimon and Anna Domček is an exceptionally cohesive mosaic of fragmentary pieces of everyday life, memories, dreams, and subjective perceptions. Besides exploring the experience of someone seeking to escape the shadows of the past – shadows that weigh heavily on future generations as well – the film also takes an unusual approach to the subject of racial intolerance.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: The ocean is a paradise for Fran the shrimp. Her deadly claws take whatever they desire. For the blind fish Milva, it’s a daily struggle to survive. Fran considers her beautiful and wants her to see the ocean the same way she does. Can they overcome their differences?​

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2025

films.syn: Niki works two jobs, but the little money she earns is barely enough to cover the living expenses for her and her two young children. One day, when the children are left unsupervised, they accidentally set the kitchen on fire, and so the Swiss authorities place them with a foster family on the other side of the country. Though forbidden from contacting her children, Niki decides to track them down. The first Swiss film to be screened in Karlovy Vary’s Crystal Globe Competition, Happy Family draws its strength from a determined yet ambivalent protagonist whose actions shed light on a rigid social system while reflecting the conflict between parental instinct and personal responsibility. Adding to the film’s strong dramatic arc is an exceptionally compelling performance by Anna Schinz.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: It’s 1940 and Henri Marre has arrived in Vichy. He has no money or contacts; however, he carries in his suitcase copies of his self-published patriotic treatise Notre salut (Our Salvation) and is intent on taking advantage of the regime change in order to acquire the position he has always wanted. The ambitious official gradually becomes part of the collaborationist government structure, unaware that his career rise is inextricably linked with moral decay. Emmanuel Marre, this year’s winner of the Best Screenplay Award at Cannes, puts forward a chilling, contemporary portrait of opportunism. Without depicting the brutality of war itself, he exposes the corrupt soul that helps mould historical evil.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.t: A Matter of Life and Death
films.syn: Returning to England from a mission in the final days of the Second World War, RAF squadron leader Peter Carter is forced to jump out of his burning plane without a parachute. While the next world tries to locate him among the newly registered deceased pilots, the miraculously-saved young man manages to fall in love with an American radio operator named June. Representatives of the afterlife, however, don’t intend to give up without a fight… This extravagant, imaginative romance about the strength of love and its delirium-inducing effect on the human mind is a legendary example of Pressburger’s narrative talent, spectacularly developed by Powell’s genius for unconventional and courageous filmmaking. The picture’s first festival screening was held on 3 August 1947 at the Spa House in Mariánské Lázně.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1946

films.syn: If the quality of a biographical documentary is measured by its ability to instill in viewers previously unfamiliar with the subject the desire to get to know that person and to spend time within their “magnetic field,” then A Pint of Ink is a successful film. Another reason is that Ester Geislerová, daughter of the Japanologist, translator, journalist, educator, and calligrapher Petr Geisler (1949–2009), has managed to capture her father’s exceptional status in late-twentieth-century Czech culture (and more) without ever losing sight of the intimate, familial, joyful, and painful dimensions. Through photographs, home videos, letters, and personal recollections, she composes a portrait of a charismatic charmer who remained mysteriously elusive even to his closest family.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: The lives of a mismatched group of guests and employees become entangled in a run-down hotel. Some have come in search of peace and a brief escape from their daily routine, while others long for change – or even love. A lonely clarinetist crosses paths with a young man looking for a romantic adventure, an unhappily married couple, an idiosyncratic hotel staff member, and also an alien sent from the planet Minerva 2 in order to report on the state of Earth. A mosaic of fourteen interwoven stories emerges through fleeting situations, awkward moments, interior monologues, and quiet observations. This experimental film by Miroslav Krobot and Lubomír Smékal is loosely based on the stage production of the same name by the S 23 Theatre Company, whose non-professional actors put together stage performances based on the dialogical acting method.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: The Swing (2018), Dancing on the Edge of a Volcano (2023), and this year A Sad and Beautiful World. Lebanese director Cyril Aris is a regular visitor to Karlovy Vary, and we are glad to have him. After showing two of his documentaries, this year we are presenting his fiction debut, a love story that, over the course of several decades, follows a couple who have, without exaggeration, been fated to be together. We watch Nino and Yasmina at various stages in life: when they fall in love, as an established couple, and as parents. All along, their relationship is somehow affected by the political reality of Lebanon. Mounia Akl and Hasan Akil excel as the mesmerizingly realistic couple.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Ilias arrives on a remote island to claim his late father’s inheritance. But the longer he is forced to stay on the island, the more his initial indifference begins to fade. As he interacts with the local community, he uncovers his father’s past and, with it, a portrait of a man which differs significantly from his own memories. His gradually awakening emotions are intensified by his encounter with the local girl Kalliopi, by sudden spasms in his body, and by mysterious power outages that affect the entire island. This feature-length debut paints a tender picture of a world that is both real and mystical – a place where, despite distant echoes foreboding the possible end of the world, we encounter love, reconciliation, and unexpected understanding.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Fiftysomething Gabrielle is a respected surgeon and head of a hospital department. Having dedicated her life to her career, she has little time for her marriage or for a mother suffering from dementia. When a young novelist turns up at the hospital seeking inspiration for a new book, the carefully constructed equilibrium of Gabrielle’s world gradually begins to shift. Director Charline Bourgeois-Tacquet considered the film after the death of her mother, who lost her battle with cancer in 2017. Instead of a story of illness, however, she decided to focus on a woman of similar age, who appears invincible and capable of carrying the weight of responsibility on her shoulders. This sober portrait of Gabrielle thus examines the borderline between professional success, caring for others and the need for closeness.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: After many years away, Jonás returns to the countryside to start work as a stonemason. In a place marked by the harshness of life, he opens himself up to something intangible – a force that permeates the landscape, bodies, and time itself. An evocatively told story of a silent man whose enigmatic nature stems from the dark side of humanity and from his contact with the sacred, the film moves along the boundary between the physical and the spiritual. Thanks to compelling sound design, a hypnotic visual style, and a rejection of traditional storytelling, Axel Bertha delivers an absorbing cinematic experience that explores human cruelty as part of a cycle of destruction from which humanity has yet to find a way out.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: Marie-Lou is the director of a nursing home, where she is trying to implement a new, more humane approach to caring for her clients. However, she runs into resistance from the staff, who are used to the old way of doing things. Meanwhile, theatre director Mari is presenting a new play while struggling with advanced cancer. When these two women meet by chance, a powerful bond forms between them, founded on mutual understanding and deep philosophical discussions on life and love, but also on capitalism and social structures. Ryûsuke Hamaguchi follows up on his Oscar-winning Drive My Car with a new film whose meditative and deeply emotional tone won over audiences at the main competition in Cannes, where its two leads shared the award for Best Actress.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: With his directorial debut, British actor and rapper Ashley Walters (nominated for an Emmy and a Golden Globe for his portrayal of a detective in the miniseries Adolescence) delves into the dark world of gangs, humiliation, and violence at a juvenile detention center. The film’s protagonist, Troy, arrives as a helpless newcomer whose only chance for survival is to submit to his sadistic fellow prisoners. Troy’s loyalty is constantly tested, and any weakness or hint of emotion or sympathy is harshly punished. But every action has a reaction. Winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at this year’s Berlinale, Animol features Walters’s co-star from Adolescence, Stephen Graham.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: The supermarket as a pillar of modern consumer society. Behind its sliding doors hides a microcosm filled with monotonous routine, unpleasant customers, and rigid rules – and it is all reflected in the emotionless face of young store assistant Sakai, which seems to have been drained of all life. The arrival of the ambitious part-time worker Ogawa, who dreams of opening her own hair salon, finally offers a ray of hope that he might break free from his constant apathy. But it’s not easy to escape from a toxic environment where empathy and individuality are suppressed in the name of standardized customer service. This unusually energetic social satire, winner of the FIPRESCI Award at this year’s Berlinale, is filled with absurd humor and sudden bursts of bloody violence.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2025

films.syn: A gently defiant pensioner drives his wife of 44 years to distraction in the understated comedy Autumn Spring, marking an assured old-school return for director Vladimír Michálek and cinematographer Martin Štrba. With help from longtime friend and former theatre colleague Eda (Stanislav Zindulka), deceptively dignified 75-year-old Fanda Hána (Vlastimil Brodský) delights in impersonations, from touring country estates to posing as subway inspectors. Though he constantly bickers with his wife Emílie (Stella Zázvorková), their bond remains unmistakable. Drawing on decades of experience, the trio delivers performances rich in restraint, playfulness and quiet charm.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings – Classics); production year 2001

films.syn: Annette and her adoptive son Joel travel to South Korea to meet his biological mother. But the long-anticipated meeting is complicated by the language barrier and repressed emotions. The atmosphere of uncertainty is amplified by the clinking of cutlery in the traditional restaurant and by a Korean version of “Clair de Lune.” Ban Dal (Half Moon) is a delicate exploration of the fragmented identity of the adopted Joel, but also a sensitive portrait of two women who, despite their different cultural backgrounds, share similar insecurities and a sense of motherly love.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2026
