films.syn: Jean-Michel Basquiat rose to fame from the streets of New York in the late 1970s and early 1980s, where his unassuming graffiti art caught the attention of the artistic elite. Almost overnight, a star was born – only to fade just as quickly. Originally a painter, now-renowned director Julian Schnabel chose Basquiat’s story to make his cinematic debut. Appearing in both major and minor roles are big-name stars such as Christopher Walken, Dennis Hopper, Willem Dafoe, Gary Oldman, and David Bowie, but dominating the pack is the then virtually unknown Jeffrey Wright, who portrayed Jean-Michel Basquiat with astonishing authenticity.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tributes); production year 1996

films.syn: Miloš Šejn, lying, unsleeping. And, most importantly, creating. This documentary essay follows an artist whose works are “born of wonder” and who is able to effortlessly navigate his longed-for escape from the city. Instead of endless sensory input, the film offers a space for concentration and perceptiveness – a space which quite possibly exceeds the seventy minutes spent in the theatre. Debut director Jakub Kučera invited editor Alexander Kashcheev and musician Oliver Torr onto his creative team, and their efforts have helped to boost the impact of this unconventional portrait of an elusive figure. When observation leads to contemplation.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: In all her films, director and editor Valeria Sarmiento has questioned the relationship between memory and the unconscious. Is it better to remain silent, hiding secrets so that things do not change (as in Secretos, 2008), or to seek true access to the most painful memories (as in Huellas, 2023)? In Behind the Rain, Sarmiento reflects on the very concept of repression. Sofía has just finished her psychology studies in Valparaíso (the city where Sarmiento was born) and returns to her hometown, Valdivia. Her return coincides with the discovery of a young girl's body, which awakens in her memories of childhood sexual abuse. Like a scratched film that looks like rain, Sofía must decide whether to stop the memory from resurfacing or to look beyond the rain, beyond the buried fears of an entire country.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: Rwanda, 2012. Nearly twenty years after the genocide of the country’s Tutsi population, community tribunals are still being organized with the goal of healing social divisions and fostering reconciliation. Vénéranda, a survivor of the genocide, moderates a dialogue between victims and the families of perpetrators. But when she learns that her daughter is pregnant, she must face the shadows of her own past. The first Rwandan film to be screened at Cannes lays bare a country that seems to be healing on the surface but continues to bleed within. How difficult is forgiveness? How to find justice and inner peace? This social but also intimate intergenerational drama is defined by extraordinarily strong female characters who rightly sense that sorrow and hope sometimes follow the same path.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: “I understand that the gym isn’t everything, but when I see someone going to the gym, they just seem like a better person to me.” An animated documentary about bodybuilding. Special Jury Mention in the National Competition at the 20th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2026.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2025

films.syn: A tale of two young men and the girl they love, Martha, played by the ethereally beautiful Magda Vášáryová. Their madcap ideas and pranks flitting between children’s playfulness and provocation seemingly spring from an inexhaustible fount of joy. They swap bizarre costumes as well as masks, and no situation can be foreseen; nor can its outcome, a fact reinforced by dynamic lensing, editing and expressive music. In contrast to the protagonists’ eccentric actions, however, the mise-en-scène is laden from the outset with the chaos of all-consuming decay and with dark references to the past. The threesome’s merry escapades start to look increasingly like a dance on the edge of the abyss, into which they too will inexorably fall. FIPRESCI Award in 1990.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1969

films.syn: In his latest film Pedro Almodóvar blends a personal drama with a metafictional reflection on the creative process. Following two plot lines, he tells the story of Raúl, a respected screenwriter and film director, and Elsa, an ad director and the heroine of his new script. The latter immerses herself in work as a coping mechanism after the death of her mother. While Elsa faces mental exhaustion and reassesses her life, Raúl, seeking inspiration, increasingly exploits the lives of the people closest to him. Via his distinctive approach, Almodóvar explores the ethical limits of artistic expression and asks whether self-fulfilment through art is also a process that ultimately destroys human relationships.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: After years of saving money from the small bribes they collect, sixty-year-old Marina and her husband Gosha from Bulgaria are preparing for their dream trip to St. Petersburg to witness the White Nights. But when Russia invades Ukraine and the travel agency vanishes with all their savings, the couple’s dream collapses along with their illusion of control over their moral principles and the relationship they have with each other. Kristina Grozeva and Petar Valchanov, recipients of the 2019 Crystal Globe, return to Karlovy Vary with a tragicomic portrait of a generation forced to reassess its values as they question everything that is considered black and white in post-Soviet society.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: Just because you can’t restore a film negative doesn’t mean you can’t breathe new life into it. Which is exactly what Canadian filmmaker Erin Weisgerber has done, using excerpts of films by Alexander Sokurov and Irakli Kvirikadze. Stories of migrations, shifting borders and unstable identities. Given its vibe, this is a film that will appeal to the Boards of Canada fanbase and many others besides.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: Besides being an unexpected Greek contribution to the Western genre, director Vasilis Georgiadis’s sweeping historical epic Blood on the Land is also a sophisticated parallel to the biblical Parable of the Prodigal Son or Odysseus’s voyage home. Set in the scorching mountains of Thessaly, the film centers on a feud between irreconcilable brothers from a landowning family and the local peasants’ growing resistance against their feudal oppressors, which escalates into violent conflict. This critical and commercial success was released just before the rise of the anti-leftist military junta, which unjustly condemned it to oblivion.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1965

films.syn: A little toadstool called Bobel has just one dream: to open a bistro selling homemade cakes. But how will he convince the other mushrooms not to be afraid of accepting food from a poisonous toadstool? A film about the power of friendship and about overcoming prejudices.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: Nine-year-old Elisabeth returns home from boarding school, into the middle of the jungle where her parents work. She can’t wait to see them, but couldn’t they all live together in the city? It’s so boring in the jungle. Or maybe not? Things take a turn when her parents have to unexpectedly leave, and Elisabeth is left to look after her brother Leo – who runs off and disappears. A family adventure full of real and imaginary animals can begin. Let yourself be enchanted by the colorful jungle and its adorable inhabitants, and let’s keep our fingers crossed that we find the right path back home – while maybe making a few new friends along the way.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Bára Basiková is an icon of Czech rock and other music genres. To what extent can her public, media-distorted image differ from the person she really is? The answer comes in the form of the latest long-term documentary study from Helena Třeštíková, whose empathy, coupled with admirable self-reflection and openness on the part of the protagonist, gives rise to a fascinating film portrait: over the course of fifty years we follow a woman who demonstrates remarkable strength as she faces the challenges of both her professional and private lives.​

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: Nastia’s Zoom lessons for her mother on how to use a laptop are disrupted by an unstable internet connection – and by resurfacing family traumas.​ Special Jury Mention in the International Competition at the 20th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2026.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2025

films.syn: This is not a documentary about an exceptional footballer. It is a documentary about Eric Cantona. And of course, any look at this multifaceted phenomenon has to start with his mastery of football. Originality, elegance, and an explosive nature characterized (and continue to characterize) this former playmaker on and off the pitch and have contributed to his cult status. As an outspoken champion of absolute authenticity – his sole weapon against destructive hypercorrectness – he has naturally found himself in many spectacular situations that formed ideal material for a pair of filmmakers chronicling his life and career. Where the French failed to understand the force of nature that is Cantona, there begins the story of Manchester United and Sir Alex Ferguson, a figure to whom the film rightly devotes considerable screen time.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: In the 1950s, if the Karlovy Vary festival screened a film from a capitalist country, it usually involved an individual’s struggle against a corrupt society – and the Australian Western by New Zealand-born director Cecil Holmes was no different. This feature-length film romanticizing the legendary outlaw Fred Ward was long considered lost in its home country, until a complete copy was recently found at the National Film Archive in Prague. After more than seventy years, the myth of Captain Thunderbolt, the “Robin Hood of the Australian bush,” can thus be seen again in all its original glory.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1952

films.syn: The friendship between a young capybara and a little chick saves a group of hens from the clutches of an evil farmer. A story about yearning for freedom and about a friendship between animals who couldn’t be more different.​

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: A man and a woman meet by chance in a village in southern Tuscany. The man is a British writer come to talk about his book, the woman is French and owns a small local art gallery. When they go to see magnificent landmarks, it is only logical that people assume they are a couple. And God knows why, but the woman initiates a game in which she takes on the role of his wife. After some reluctance, the man joins in the game. Soon enough, we don’t know where the game ends and the truth begins – or vice versa. Renowned Iranian filmmaker Abbas Kiarostami’s first film shot in Europe earned Juliette Binoche the Best Actress Award at the 2010 Cannes Film Festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tributes); production year 2010

films.syn: Following a trilogy of low-budget films, two of which (Mirrors in the Dark and And Then There Was Love...) were screened in Karlovy Vary, Šimon Holý returns with the international co-production Chica Checa. Once again, the story revolves around a female protagonist: here, the widowed village mail carrier Zdena (Pavla Tomicová), who tries to fulfill the last wish of her ailing mother. A series of unexpected events brings her closer to her son Lukáš (Jan Cina) and awakens in her a longing for a different life. Holý once again confirms his talent for observation and his ability to create a vibrant portrait of his characters’ inner conflicts, all while giving Tomicová ample space to fully express her acting abilities.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: The end of the American occupation of Japan meant that, among other things, the country had to come to terms with a horrific legacy of the past, the impact of which had thus far been silenced by the censors – the atom bombs that were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Director Kaneto Shindō was the first to render this oppressive memento on the big screen. Children of Hiroshima, based on the book by Arata Osada, who witnessed the Hiroshima bombing himself, is a softly contoured portrait of the survivors, whose bodies and souls bore indelible traces long after the war had ended. The film, awarded the Peace Prize at Karlovy Vary, was seen as a strong political gesture at the time of production and was not given its official American premiere until 2011. Second Grand Prix and FIPRESCI Award in 1966.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1954

films.syn: Distinctive filmmaker Zdeněk Tyc offers up a story about a father and son, who have nothing in common except their first name, Richard, and an apartment on a housing estate. The burly, good-natured, 30-something factory worker listens to heavy metal and occasionally lets his girlfriend into his life. The frail, retired teacher, who raised the boy after his mother's departure, is the embodiment of empathy. However, their tranquil, shared reality, which embraces both the hardcore band Našrot and Bergman’s Cries and Whispers, is disrupted by the sudden death of the mother. Young Richard sets out on a peculiar initiation journey with bizarre encounters and moments of unexpected enlightenment. Tyc plunges headfirst into existential themes with the support of a stellar cast headed by Tomáš Vravník and Vladimír Javorský.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: The mesmeric Anna Ferzetti (the president’s daughter Dorotea in Sorrentino’s La Grazia) brings vitality to her role as a spirited English teacher sent to a high school in the Roman suburb of Rebibbia to take on a class of maladjusted students. At least this is how the youngsters are viewed by the staff, who immediately mistrust the new professoressa for her natural authority and capacity to connect with the troublemakers. The film’s masterful combination of high-energy ensemble scenes and moments of melancholy intimacy works via an evocative directorial approach founded on an innate ability to see through the “camouflage” of young people who are just starting to make sense of the world.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: “I love the Danube, that silent witness to our history; how many times have we wished that it could talk”, stated András Kovács. The Hungarian director had recently completed his hitherto most ambitious film Cold Days, an adaptation of the novel of the same name by Tibor Cseres. The public followed the production with a sense of anticipation and also trepidation, since the story explored the dark and, to this day, painful events of the Novi Sad massacre. In 1946 four men share a prison cell, accused of planning war crimes committed by Horthy’s army. As they await their trial, they reminisce about what happened, returning to those “cold days” on the banks of the Danube. Their aim is not merely to exonerate themselves before the tribunal but also, above all, to do so in their own eyes.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1966

films.syn: While the participants of a biotech conference are meeting in a high-rise building, Seo Young-cheol, one of the scientists, has different plans. He has created a pathogen that he believes will help to build a better human society, and he has decided not to put off for tomorrow what can be done today. But the pathogen causes people to mutate into bloodthirsty zombies that go on to quickly infect others. Naturally, this development interrupts the normal course of the conference and the entire building finds itself in lockdown. Director Yeon Sang-ho is hardly a newcomer to the zombie genre. Peninsula, the sequel to his famous Train to Busan, was shown at KVIFF in 2021.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2026

films.syn: Can a war – like being in love or life itself – ever be too short? Two Belgian soldiers meet amidst the fighting of the First World War. Pierre is a shy young farm boy, while the charismatic tailor Francis swears by his theatrical “band of rejects,” who offer some of the few opportunities for entertainment and escape on the front lines. With the increasing horrors of the war, the two men’s attraction grows stronger – as do their thoughts of escape and their fear of being discovered. In his third and most mature film yet (following Girl and Close), Belgian director and screenwriter Lukas Dhont again explores queer identity and new aspects of masculinity with his typical sensitivity and aptitude for dramatic tension.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Alain Gomis’s monumental film inhabits an otherwise overlooked in-between space: during its three-hour runtime, it moves between France and Guinea-Bissau, a wedding and a memorial service, tradition and modernity, joy and sorrow, fiction and documentary. It is an innovative film shaped by the kinetic synergy between fluid camerawork and compelling editing. Gomis’s approach may circumvent narrative conventions, but this is what makes his film so engaging. It does not dictate, nor does it try to find a beginning, a middle, and an end. Instead, it captures and lets go again – the interactions between family members, togetherness and conflict, reality and transgression, a sense of home and a fragmented identity.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Five minutes of faltering and searching, one minute of enchantment. Indian artist and photographer Sohrab Hura sets off into the mountains and, once there, employs vague movements and specific sounds in order to shape our expectations. This thought-provokingly ambiguous and, in its gestural simplicity, highly effective film tells us that the legacy of Michael Snow lives on.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: Misael works with wood. After his day is done he likes to take it easy, indulging in simple pleasures – and it doesn’t actually matter that the back of his chair is only made of string. But then a situation occurs in his uncomplicated life that could completely derail him. After a period of twenty-five years, Argentinian filmmaker Lisandro Alonso returns to his groundbreaking film Freedom, conducting a casual dialogue with it while also drawing on the best works that employ the concept of “emptied narration”. This focused, ascetic yet vibrant film effortlessly captures that most elementary form of human communication and once again searches for the limits of freedom.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: Freedom or death. This poetically and also aggressively forthright film takes us to the auditorium of the National University of Colombia, which is named after the poet León de Greiff. Instead of a celebration, however, we witness a memorial service; blood is seeping into the floorboards of the stage. Reinforced with a revolutionary spirit, this experimental short film operates in a paradoxical atmosphere of a heightened, enigmatic haze.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: In a Nepalese village in the middle of a forest inhabited by wild elephants lives Pirati, a leading figure and healer in the Kinnar community, which provides refuge for third-gender people rejected by their families. She plans to leave her adopted family and to live with the man she loves, but when one of her daughters disappears, she must take the investigation into her own hands and choose between her own freedom and her sense of responsibility for others. An emotional, action-packed film that mixes social criticism with a sense of mystery, Elephants in the Fog explores the ambivalent position of a community that is both feared and marginalized. Thanks to a stunning performance by its lead actress, the film was awarded the Jury Prize in the Un Certain Regard section at Cannes.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: New York, 1961. With his jazz trio, Bill Evans is at the peak of his career, but just a few days after recording a new double album, his bassist and musical kindred spirit is killed in a traffic accident. Overcome with grief, Evans turns his back on music for the first time since childhood and leaves New York. Everybody Digs Bill Evans, a delicate blues portrait of one of the 20th century’s greatest jazz geniuses, conjures up an enchanting play of light and shadow to open a window onto his melancholy soul. The film, which won the Silver Bear for Best Director at this year’s Berlinale, reminds us that sometimes an intermission is part of the music.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Monika, a doctor, is happy in her relationship and is expecting a child. She still gets along well with her former husband Petr, and so she decides to tell him about her pregnancy in person. The two of them had had difficulties conceiving. Their afternoon meeting for coffee extends into evening, so they have plenty of time to talk – about what might have been, and also about what might be. Director, screenwriter, and editor Bohdan Karásek pays homage to mumblecore, a genre founded on dialogue. The conversation between the two main characters, excellently portrayed by Marie Švestková and Jiří Havelka, opens numerous questions faced by more than a few men and women in middle age.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: Grief is a strange drug. It gets under our skin, it survives in our heart chambers, it distorts reality. How does one deal with a sudden tragedy and with the questions that remain unanswered even a year later? A mother, a daughter and a teenage boy initially face their shared trauma alone, but they then travel together to faraway Tenerife, where they experience manifestations of guilt, the prospect of forgiveness, and also inscrutable visions of the past. Winner of this year’s Un Certain Regard at Cannes, the film is propelled by a softly mesmeric energy, authentic emotions and breathtaking moments, when the filmmaking craft becomes sacral magic. Everytime casts rays of light deep into the shadows of the human soul and emerges as the cinematic equivalent of a sun that never sets.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Drought, ghost, accident. Three scenes, three missteps of human life; one icon which may or may not play a role in them. Tinkering with spirituality and humour, these vignettes reopen the question as to what role images play in human existence. Strong in their simplicity, these compositions are supplemented with animation from Paulina Ziółkowska. How fine is the line between miracle and superstition?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: Every family has its traditions, and some even have a family profession. For the Smiths, it is shooting B- and C-grade horror movies. They may not be the most successful works of cinema, but for parents Jack and Ellen, making a movie is the only time the whole family can get together. When a real dead body shows up on the set of their latest film project, however, horror starts to spill over into reality. Kevin Bacon as the husband and director (in the film and in real life) and Kyra Sedgwick as his wife (in the film and in real life) savor this moment of absolute cinematic freedom. A combination of all possible genres, Family Movie already made a splash during its world premiere at SXSW in Austin, Texas.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2026

films.syn: What is it like to return to your native country but not to return home? It’s 1949. Thomas Mann, accompanied by his daughter Erika, arrives in Germany after an absence of sixteen long years in order to receive two awards, one in American-occupied Frankfurt, the other in Weimar, controlled by the Soviets. In the course of their journey, the pair receive news of a family tragedy. Disarming in its directorial style, this subtly layered piece can be interpreted in various ways: as a thought-provoking probe into post-war society, an intimate family drama, a road movie meandering between myth and reality, and as a surprisingly topical film about the role of the intellectual in a time of change. The leads are superbly played by Hanns Zischler and Sandra Hüller, with exquisite lensing from cinematographer Łukasz Żal.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Sixteen is a difficult age. Besides having to choose a high school (and pass entrance exams), it’s also a time of finding oneself – emotionally, sexually, and just sort of in general. Matty knows that he wants to study art, that he likes boys, that he doesn’t like his mother’s new partner, and that he can rely on his friends – but he definitely did not expect to fall in love during exams. Radek is great, but their relationship isn’t, and so the difficulties start to mount. An exclusive sneak preview of director David Semler’s new Czech Television miniseries, Filter.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: Not only did Martha lose her oldest son, but to this day she doesn’t know what happened to him or his remains. After years of searching in vain, she meets Sandra, who offers her one more possibility, perhaps her last hope: to set out for a remote place where the line between the living and the dead is blurred. The directorial duo of Juan Miguel Gelacio and Esteban Hoyos García gives voice to Colombian women who, after their children’s disappearance, took the search into their own hands. The film’s subdued, focused narrative calls attention to one of the most painful consequences of the country’s long-lasting armed conflict while portraying the search for peace and reconciliation in a place that has never witnessed a farewell.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Romanian director Cristian Mungiu won his second Palme d’Or with his latest outing, which follows a Romanian-Norwegian family as it moves to a remote part of Norway. Their seemingly trouble-free integration into the local community becomes more complicated when the parents are accused of violent behavior toward their children. Mungiu takes a nuanced look at questions of identity, parenthood, and the possibilities of co-existence in a culturally divided Europe. One family’s drama grows into a morally ambivalent social and legal conflict that pits traditional religious values against progressive notions of child welfare. Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve excel as the film’s two central figures.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Olga lives the quiet life of a retiree, earning extra income by renting out one of her rooms. It would seem that she has everything perfectly organized and under control, and only a few minor details could possibly upset her happy routine. But then nine-year-old Cristian enters her life. This sensitive, humanist, and bittersweet film shows that the shell in which we wrap ourselves in order to avoid the outside world merely hides our own fragility. Flies was shown in the main competition at this year’s Berlinale.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: A mountain hut in the northern Alps and the three women who tend to it at different times. Nature blossoms, bears fruit, and is again covered in snow; tourists come and go, and Anne, Hélène, and Suzanne listen to stories, observe the changes, and face utter solitude… Director Manon Coubia’s Belgian-French debut reflects her own experience from living in such a place, closely observing the life of nature high in the mountains while simultaneously retelling a fragment of a fictional story. Shot in natural lighting on classical celluloid, the film brings out the poetry of fleeting existence and lets viewers experience the meditative calm and breathtaking scenery of Europe’s high mountains.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: After several years studying in Europe, Elsa returns home to Costa Rica, where she finds her family in disarray. Her younger sister is trying to cope with adulthood while living in their dilapidated family home, her father has a succession of younger partners, and her mother seems to be interested only in republishing the collection of erotic poems she wrote before becoming a mother. Elsa is convinced that she is the only stable one in the family, and so she tries to put everything in order. But stability is a relative concept, and – as so often happens – we all have our secrets. This refreshing family drama earned its three female leads the Best Actress Award in the Un Certain Regard section at this year’s Cannes Film Festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Seen through the eyes of two young women, life in contemporary Myanmar can look quite oppressive. Working at a textile factory in industrial Yangon, they face exhausting work, social repression, and economic uncertainty. Although the grueling pace of everyday life stifles opportunities for human connection, both women continue to dream of intimacy and escape. When they grow closer, they set in motion the previously silenced fibers of their own emotions. Aung Phyoe’s long-anticipated directorial debut unfolds in shades of silence, subtle gestures, and unspoken wishes. In a captivating rhythm that oscillates between tenderness and harshness, the film explores how women’s desires survive in a country where intimacy and love between women remain socially unacceptable.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: The images are almost idyllic: a sprawling house in the countryside, a married couple in love, and a young son. Nevertheless, the family’s stability is soon disrupted by a visit from the police who turn up at the door with a serious allegation. What secret is the husband hiding? The latest film by Austrian director Marie Kreutzer once again depicts events from a female perspective, offering up a truly gripping, emotionally charged study of a woman who is forced to confront her sudden misgivings about the man she loves. As a devoted mother and broken woman on the brink of a destroyed life, caught between trust and deception, she finds herself descending to the very depths of her emotions. French actress Léa Seydoux excels in the main role.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Block C of the maximum security prison houses inmates convicted of fraud, robbery, and murder. One of them is Anggoro, who manages to hold his head high despite bullying from gangs and a tyrannical warden. But when the arrival of a young new prisoner triggers a series of mysterious, brutal murders, even the greatest enemies must join forces to survive and defeat the supernatural culprit. Supposedly, all you have to do is maintain a positive aura… But how? Indonesian genre wizard Joko Anwar returns to Karlovy Vary with a cinematic Gesamtkunstwerk that perfectly balances gore, biting comedy, and uncompromising political commentary – a film in which bursts of laughter are immediately followed by uncomfortable reflections on corruption, exploitation, and social inequality.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2026

films.syn: Pierfrancesco Diliberto, known as Pif, established himself as a director of Italian film comedies with his debut The Mafia Kills Only in Summer, which he introduced to Karlovy Vary audiences in person twelve years ago. Pif has his own unique tone, in which tenderness encounters refreshing (self-)irony and the intimate blends with the political and social – and all this portrayed in a liberating, direct manner. The emotions of Pif’s Arturo, a successful real estate agent with a non-existent love life, resonate in his absorbing passion for Sicilian dolci. Will his encounter with the enchanting Flora change his outlook on life? Pastries, desserts and a curious take on the Catholic faith in a romantic comedy which is also a homage to the filmmaker’s beloved Palermo.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: “Puppeteer, tell us a story we don’t know yet!” the audience calls out to a traveling thespian. And so he starts to recount a story about a boy born of the forbidden love between brother and sister, who had many adventures, who spent seventeen years tied to a rock, and who perhaps was also… a hedgehog? But that’s not as important as how, after overcoming all these obstacles, he ended up becoming the pope. Young Gregorius (excellently portrayed by Jan František Uher) is a charming mix of naivete and determination, and it is a pure joy to watch his wanderings through mythical lands. Director Tomasz Mielnik’s wild, absurd comedy is based on the final novel by Thomas Mann.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: Films from far-flung Mexico were hugely popular during the first few years of the Karlovy Vary festival, a fact also reflected by the success of Emilio Fernández’s social drama Hidden River, discovered by European festivals shortly before. In a reference to the political orientation of President Alemán Valdés, the story of the young teacher Rosaura expresses the hope that a better future is possible without the aid of rifles – primarily thanks to the country’s modernisation and education. The quiet strength of the protagonist is underlined to this day by the evocative images of Gabriel Figueroa, one of Mexico’s most talented cinematographers (and later collaborator of Luis Buñuel).

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1948

films.syn: Fifty-year-old Murad’s life is shaken to the core when he learns that his younger brother is gay. Murad would like to support his brother, but their traditional Muslim family is against it. As a result, he finds himself subjected to pressures from all sides – from his father, who has close ties to the local imam, and from his brother’s circle of friends as well. He would like to help everyone, but as he slowly falls into a spiral of conflicts and mounting difficulties, he finds that he, too, is in need of help. Another integral part of this family drama is the theme of migration and dialogue – not just between different religions, but within communities themselves. For his fourth feature film, director Nader Saeivar collaborated with Jafar Panahí, who contributed as producer and editor.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: Eleven-year-old Iris lives a quiet, though also somewhat empty, life in a sleepy coastal town – until, that is, her father unexpectedly returns. Although he has come because of a funeral and is initially not interested in getting to know his daughter, things change when Iris proves to be a good partner for his petty thefts and scams. Myrsini Aristidou’s feature debut sensitively captures the fleeting moments of a complicated relationship between two people finding their way to one another. This heartwarming story was the first Cypriot film to premiere at the Sundance Film Festival, where it won the Audience Award.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: In the remote forests of eastern Cambodia lives a community of indigenous inhabitants. An unnamed forty-year-old businessman arrives with seemingly selfless intentions: he claims he is merely a tourist seeking to discover the life of his “brothers”. In actuality, however, he is gathering information for the possible expropriation of their land. Italian globetrotter Giovanni C. Lorusso lives up to his reputation as a filmmaker balancing on the line between fiction and documentary. Through unique locations, mesmerizing camera work, and immersive sound design, he captures the slow inner transformation of his protagonist along with the rich cultural and spiritual life of a community facing a modern form of colonialism.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: “God does not count against you time spent in hot water,” says one of the characters in this heartwarming road movie. The main character, Layal, a college professor caught between different worlds, must drive her son Daniel across the entire United States to his father in order to save his high school education. Shown at this year’s Sundance Film Festival, this distinctive feature film debut sparkles with bittersweet insights, yet sticks to the rules of the genre: as its protagonists drive toward their destination, they must find their way to one another – and to themselves.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.t: How to Divorce During the War
films.syn: Marija tells her husband Vytas that she wants a divorce – and this only a few hours before the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Their marital crisis thus suddenly becomes something much bigger: the couple have to navigate the separation process at a time when, because of the war, nothing is certain anymore and their life in Vilnius is drastically changing. In his third feature film, Lithuanian director Andrius Blaževičius introduces unexpected flashes of absurd humour as he deftly weaves an intimate family drama with sweeping historical events. The film had its world premiere screening in the World Cinema Dramatic Competition at this year’s Sundance festival, where Blaževičius won the Directing Award.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.ot: Kdyby se holubi proměnili ve zlato
films.syn: Not just the Best Documentary Award at this year’s Berlinale turned pigeons to gold for modern Czech documentary film. Have you ever mourned someone who is still alive? Shooting on her iPhone, director Pepa Lubojacki tries to understand why her beloved older brother and two cousins live unhoused while struggling with addiction. Avoiding the siren song of sentimentality and shot in a DIY aesthetic enriched by the creative use of stylized remembrances, graphic interventions, and artificial intelligence, this disarmingingly personal film explores family history, the causes and consequences of addiction, and the limits of personal integrity. What is the right expression of love – to save, or to let go?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: This year’s gallery of artistically inspiring portraits of uncompromising eccentrics (among them The Hanging of Stuart Cornfeld, Robert Richardson: The White Devil and A Pint of Ink) features another unobtrusive stand-out in the shape of Igor Luther, a key figure of Slovak and European cinematography. Ivan Ostrochovský’s perspective is rare, dynamic and also meditative, while Luther himself co-authored the project during the last few months of his life. Works such as Juraj Jakubisko’s Birds, Orphans and Fools, Volker Schlöndorff’s The Tin Drum and Andrzej Wajda’s Danton, in the persuasive words of their creators, wouldn’t have the same timeless energy today if it weren’t for Luther’s visionary endeavours.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings – Classics); production year 2026

films.syn: In 2007, French actress Juliette Binoche and British dancer and choreographer Akram Khan put their established and esteemed careers to the test. Working together, they spent seven months creating the unique performance In-I, which they then presented at a hundred different places around the world. Each artist visited the comfort zone of the other with the shared intention of analyzing a romantic relationship with ruthless authenticity. Many years later, the respected actress revisited hours of footage from rehearsals and the gripping performance itself in order to create a captivating documentary study that pulls the viewer deep into the creative process.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tributes); production year 2025

films.syn: Ten-year-old Kozue, who definitely is not one of the popular kids at school, secretly spends her time tossing various objects into the school’s incinerator. When university student Jinta comes to her classroom and invites the children to a shadow play performance, something awakens inside Kozue, and her path toward adulthood begins. In this poetic tale based on a short story by Japanese author Kaori Ekuni (nicknamed the “female Murakami”), sunny summer days mix languidly with scenes of everyday life to reveal a silent yet unsettling confrontation with a world that often seems impenetrable to children’s eyes. Understanding family relationships, mortality, and one’s own emotions is significantly more complicated than turning things into ash.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: Who has the hairiest chest? Jim Queen! Who has the biggest muscles? Jim Queen! The firmest butt? Jim Queen! Yes, him! The gayest gay in Paris. The influencer who has protein for breakfast and the love of all of “Gay Paree” for dinner. But watch out! There’s a virus going around called Heterosis, which dissolves your six-pack (nooo!), forces you to watch football (that thing with the ball?) and have children (yuck) – with a woman no less (ugh!). But Jim Queen won’t stand for it, and so he boldly strikes out in search of a cure, joined by his improbable companion Lucien, who has no muscles at all and hasn’t so much as kissed a man. So let’s raise our rainbow flags and set off on an animated mission to rescue the gay world – all of us together, regardless of whether we love men, women or bears.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2026

films.syn: The emerging film career of Ken Loach, modest titan of European filmmaking, is strongly associated with the Karlovy Vary festival. After his feature debut Poor Cow, one of the most striking entries in the KVIFF competition in 1968, Loach returned to the spa resort two years later with his drama Kes. The story of 15-year-old Billy, whose only ray of light in his straitened and grim circumstances is his friendship with a wild kestrel, is ranked by the BFI among the top ten greatest British films of all time. This powerfully authentic picture about the tough transition from childhood to adolescence competed in Karlovy Vary in 1970, winning the Grand Prix for Best Film.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1969

films.syn: The director’s passion for using film to think about other films brings him into the home of Kim Novak, where this remarkable actress remembers – decades after the fact – her introduction to the chaotic world of Hollywood productions… and her subsequent departure in the interest of preserving her own integrity. The recollections of this movie icon go far beyond mere behind-the-scenes details. Organically interwoven with archival footage, the exclusive interview avoids tabloid superficiality, culminating in Novak’s reflections on Vertigo and her connection to it, while also touching on more universal human themes such as the desire for creative freedom and for recognition from those closest to us.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: A dual portrait of a relationship affected by one partner’s gender transition. Filmmaker Ollie Launspach decides to document his transition through the emotions of his partner Sterre, but the more he tries to understand her emotions, the more he is lost in his own. As a result, the film loses its previously planned contours and it becomes necessary to restructure it using the language not only of cinema, but also of literature – the domain of the author Sterre. An enchanting narrative experiment that asks how much we actually know the ones we think we are closest to.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2025

films.syn: It’s a hot summer below Vesuvius. A group of French students have set off on their last school trip before they go their separate ways. The Classical ruins, the petrified bodies of Pompeii’s ancient inhabitants and the elegant Roman statues provide the setting for seemingly banal coming-of-age dramas – squabbles, summer romances, ill-concealed rivalries, and unspoken desires. On the edge of the fabled volcano we witness the low-key yet increasingly powerful eruptions of those who came to learn something about history and also about themselves. This masterfully constructed directorial debut from cinematographer Marine Atlan goes deeper than the majority of films about adolescence. A film of subtle intensity, subliminal tension and profound catharsis.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: This adaptation of the eponymous 2017 novel by Colombian author Pilar Quintana takes us to the island of Santa María off the coast of Chile, where forty-something Silvia earns a living harvesting seaweed. When Silvia adopts a stray puppy, an intense bond develops. In her third feature film, which premiered at the recent Cannes Film Festival, Dominga Sotomayor continues her exploration of nature and human nature, this time with the addition of an animal character. But the dog is more than a metaphor; it is an integral part of the film’s world with its own distinctive personality. To what extent can nature or an animal belong to us? And how much can we tame it?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Postcolonialism is a long-running theme in the films of iconic South American director Lucrecia Martel. In her first feature-length documentary, she focuses on the situation in Argentina following the 2009 murder of indigenous activist Javier Chocobar. Despite clear evidence of guilt, the trial of his accused murderer does not begin until nine years later. Martel follows the course of the trial, revisits the moment of the murder, and gives voice to people for whom the case represents an extreme escalation of oppression that has lasted for generations. Martel premiered her auteur true-crime documentary last year in Venice, and it was named Best Film at the BFI Festival in London.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.t: Last night I stayed within myself and this morning I decided to live here
films.ot: Vannacht logeerde ik in mijzelf en vanochtend besloot ik er te blijven wonen
films.syn: Can we eat the fruit of paradise among the new buildings of the modern metropolis? This poetically meandering film blends an inquisitive mood with strong impressions; sterility encounters grime, and spontaneity is here reflected in a colourful palette. An eloquent, dreamlike film hovering somewhere between Herzog and Chytilová.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: Eight-year-old Leo lives with his dad and a giant shark, which crashed through the roof of their home. Yes, you read that correctly. The shark is Leo’s best friend, to whom he can confide all his secrets. He can’t really talk to his dad; he must be missing mum, who’s been gone five years now. Then Anya the au pair bursts into their lives, and their world suddenly changes. It’s more cheerful and Leo discovers that the metal shark doesn’t have to be his only friend. An enchanting film for parents and children about how to talk together and how to grieve together. About how the world of adults is sometimes hard to understand, and how children’s opinions really should be taken seriously. And, above all, it’s about learning how to breathe again.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: A schoolteacher learns that her son is not going to pass the state exams. She has to choose between cheating and keeping a clear conscience.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: In Manitoba there’s something in the air and no-one can capture it quite like Canadian filmmaker Rhayne Vermette, who shot her second feature film on a broken 16mm Bolex camera. In the Red River Valley people gather for the unveiling of a new sculpture and suddenly they are plunged into darkness. Reports on the television tell them that the sun will come to its senses and everything will be fine. This magical, taciturn and shimmeringly exquisite film unfolds in a mystical aura with a hint of sci-fi and is a testament to the power of analogue film. Mysteries are there to be experienced; we shouldn’t look for explanations. And the most wonderful procession is the one headed into the unknown – or into the night.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: The near future. Winter. A run-down movie studio that has long not seen any stars – unlike the rockets with which tourists can now fly into space. And in the middle of it all is the lonely janitor Zha, who occasionally finds company in the form of a cat or the VR goggles that his boss gave him in lieu of his wages. With his goggles, Zha escapes into a world that is somehow more real and more comprehensible – a world where you can plan a trip to the Moon with a beautiful girl. This inventive animated film, shown in the Perspectives section at this year’s Berlinale, uses absurd humor and a pervasive sense of melancholy to depict the Little Man’s dream of light pillars – so beautiful, and yet so unattainable.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: “Here we have a film that has been made in the masterful grip of a young director,” Germany’s Hamburger Echo wrote in a review of Lissy, the first true classic by director Konrad Wolf. This still relevant story, based on the novel by Prague native Franz Carl Weiskopf, follows a young working-class woman who yearns for a better life, but her path toward this dream brings her uncomfortably close to the growing machinery of the Nazi regime. A fundamentally humanist drama with excellent cinematography by Werner Bergmann and a delicate, moving performance by Sonja Sutter in the title role, Lissy asks us to ponder what we are willing to ignore if we feel that we can benefit from it. Third Grand Prix in 1957.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1957

films.syn: Andrej wants to stop causing trouble and start behaving himself. To spend the summer helping his grandmother, and mainly not to drink alcohol – because when he drinks, he does things like climb a tree from which he can’t get down anymore. But his plan doesn’t count on him meeting and falling in love (or something) with Míša. And sometimes love is worth fighting for, even if it’s alongside your boring cousin Peter. A summer full of challenges can begin! This debut by Slovak director Martina Buchelová is a celebration of cinematic freedom that is humorous and inventive in terms of both style and narrative. Come enjoy summer like when we were teenagers.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: This Kafkaesque courtroom drama set in nineteenth-century Liverpool recounts the trial of a corpse with neither name nor past. Dozens have gathered for this absurd ceremony – and perhaps to deliver justice. Best Film in the Labo Competition at the 20th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2026.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2025

films.syn: “You don’t make up for your sins in church. You do it in the streets.” The third film by one of America’s most distinctive filmmakers, Martin Scorsese, draws on his personal experiences from Manhattan’s Little Italy neighborhood. Charlie (Harvey Keitel), torn between his Catholic faith and his work for the local mafia, gets a chance at greater influence, but his ambitions are complicated by Johnny Boy (Robert De Niro), an irresponsible young man whom he has taken under his wing. Imbued with an unforgettable 1970s soundtrack, Mean Streets not only presaged Scorsese’s long-standing collaboration with De Niro and Keitel, but also hinted at the future direction of his work. In this film, we find the seeds of the themes that Scorsese would later develop in his most acclaimed works.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tributes); production year 1973

films.syn: Beginning filmmakers often draw on their own lives, but few infuse their debut with such a memorable combination of originality, skill, and intensity as Vladlena Sandu. She was just six years old when, following her parents’ divorce, she moved from Crimea to Grozny, which Russia’s 1994 invasion of Chechnya turned into hell on Earth. Her unique and colorful multimedia collage recalls the films of Andrei Tarkovsky and Sergei Parajanov, but from a broader perspective it remains a fundamentally personal film exploring the landscape of her childhood, where innocent imagination is mixed with generational trauma, unending circles of violence, and the cruelty of war.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Some people make their own pancakes, some people want to steal them. How will it all turn out? The most treacherous weapons are at play: a snake that likes to bite people’s rear ends, and a hot-air balloon.​

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: Youthful fragility and self-discovery are frequent motifs of the contemporary coming-of-age genre, but few filmmakers also address social issues – and do so in a poetic manner or with a spiritual dimension. Estonian director Ivan Pavljutskov is definitely among the latter group. In his feature debut, fifteen-year-old photographer Morten finds himself caught between two worlds – between two girls, between nature and civilization, between everyday reality and the mystical, between what is right and what others want. As it explores the depths of the Baltic forests and of a young boy’s soul, Morten will charm viewers of all ages with its warmth and understanding for all its characters.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: A family of tiny mushroom flies is happily living in its mushroom dwelling. But with the start of the mushroom season, their troubles begin. Can the enterprising insects hide their home from the sharp eyes of mushroom hunters?​

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: Rosa – the director Rosa Friedrich herself – was never that interested in porn, until her friend Timo expresses a wish to star in an erotic film. So Rosa agrees to help him get his project off the ground. However, the closer it gets to the shooting date, the more Timo feels embarrassed and doubtful about having involved himself in the first place. His face is ultimately replaced with the help of AI, and Rosa, together with a dominatrix, three trans women, a food-porn creator, a sex coach and other protagonists, continues with the film. A playful look at the kind of porn that can be worlds apart from the depersonalised, omnipresent industry, the kind which gives rise to emotions, misgivings and the uniqueness of each individual body and experience.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: Walking, a time for reflection. Thomas works on a building site; his wife Carla calls him from hospital – something has happened. When she eventually tells him about it, she seems frightened of her own feelings – and Thomas withdraws into himself. In her magically ordinary film, alternating unvarnished, stark moments with exceptionally fervent episodes, Angela Schanelec captures the fragility of those decisive points during our endless navigation through the construction site of life. Like the director’s previous films, this piece is also a colourful miniature, receptive to the subtle nuances of existence. Even the quietest moments can be exhilarating.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: Have you ever wondered what would happen if a traditional English man from a Christian family married someone other than a traditional English woman from a Christian family? For instance, what if he married Saga, for whom he would then move from London deep into the woods of Finland, where they then have a child? If this is the kind of story you’ve been waiting for, then wait no further… Director and screenwriter Hanna Bergholm’s Nightborn explores motherhood and the life of new parents from a fresh and occasionally bloodthirsty perspective. Because sometimes, instead of baby food, you need a vial of O-positive as you draw the shades, so not a single ray of sunshine falls on your little bundle of joy. Which family members will live to hear baby’s first word? And will that word be “flesh”?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2026

films.t: No Peace Under the Olive Tree
films.ot: Non c’è pace tra gli ulivi
films.syn: The Italian drama No Peace Under the Olive Tree, awarded a Special Honourable Mention at the 6th Karlovy Vary festival, is an epic tale of poor shepherds who unite against their oppressor – the cruel and amoral nouveau riche Bonfiglio (superbly portrayed by Folco Lulli). The directorial style of Giuseppe De Santis is rooted in Neorealist conventions; however, for greater viewer accessibility the film is enhanced with elements of lyricism, idealism and melodrama. The rural story, shot amid the rugged, scorched rocks near the director’s native town of Fondi, thus enjoyed commercial success, although the critics of the day (particularly those from Western Europe) gave it a noticeably cooler reception.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1950

films.syn: We all know that lying doesn’t pay. But lying to your young nephew is a far greater risk to take. This is something that middle-aged Candela learns first-hand. How to deal with the fact that she ran over the boy’s dog while not ruining his birthday? Maybe, just maybe, dogs don’t die – instead, they head off every now and then on a pilgrimage to a sacred dog tree. Nobody Barks is a dark and at times absurd comedy about family ties, little white lies, and how even bad things can sometimes lead to good.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2025

films.syn: Long night’s journey into day. Olivia lives with her father, who works in a slaughterhouse. And since Olivia is awake mainly at night, their paths don’t cross. Then, one day, her father doesn’t come home. This at first comforting herbarium of brief life moments gradually assumes more sinister contours; levity becomes apprehension, cosiness gives way to depression. Contemplating the asymmetry of the lives we share with our loved ones, the film nevertheless always maintains its ascetic, elusive and magical tone. Not much is spoken here, and if so, only in whispers; an overflowing pot will often say more than words. Not since Tarr’s The Turin Horse has there been such an evocative scene involving the consumption of boiled potatoes.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.t: Only Beautiful Things to Look At
films.syn: The film is set in the mid-1980s, when the state used its laws to continually influence the most intimate facets of its citizens’ lives. Ingrid (Aňa Geislerová) is an ambitious doctor, whose mission is to bring children into the world, to terminate unwanted pregnancies, and to participate in the sterilisation of Romany women. The melancholy woman has greater misgivings about her private situation than she does about her professional life, that is, until she is caught “off guard” by a new friendship with a charismatic Romany orderly. Spontaneous Agáta presents to Ingrid the human contours of a national minority reduced by the communists to a demographic problem. Ostrochovský’s beguiling drama returns to a hitherto unresolved issue of Czechoslovak history, where the option of having children was determined by the state.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: Director Marie Lukáčová’s rap fairy tale is an unusual take on a traditional genre. You won’t find a knight on a white horse here – its main protagonist Jasna manages to save herself from the wicked ruler Volk. When Volk sends her on a journey from which she is not expected to return, Jasna – with a little bit of help – discovers his scheme in time, overcomes a test of her fear, and ultimately defeats her oppressor. This tale in three acts weaves together environmental and feminist viewpoints and visually blends the aesthetics of an autumn forest with the original use of 2D and 3D animation. As in any good fairy tale, everyone lives happily ever after.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2025

films.syn: There was once a little seed which was growing quite contentedly somewhere inside a soft, sweet fruit. But then this fruit burst one day and the tiny, round seedlet dropped out into the big, unfamiliar world, where other seeds take root in the earth, while birds and animals flit and scamper about close by. The little seed observed all this for a while, then it decided it didn’t want to remain in one place like the others; it wanted to see the world. And so it turned its newly germinated roots into little legs and set out to boldly go where no seed has gone before. A story for children and adults which, without a single word, tells a tale about making a seemingly impossible dream come true.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: New York in the 1980s is changing literally before one’s eyes. The city offers the promise of getting rich quick, but at the same time it is increasingly permeated by a gray zone of shady deals and dangerous connections. The good-natured engineer Irwin (Miles Teller), his straight-laced wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson), and their two sons lead a quiet, middle-class life – until, that is, Irwin’s charismatic brother Gary (Adam Driver) shows up with a lucrative side deal. Is this their chance to finally live the American dream? As a former police officer, Gary knows how to navigate the city’s unpredictable streets. But will he realize before it’s too late who he’s gotten himself mixed up with this time?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: An allegory of searching, loss, displacement, and the discovery of new meanings and commonalities. Three men – Yi-En from China, Junior from Congo, and Hamzah from Palestine – share a spartan apartment in a seemingly abandoned building in Paris. Besides this joint living arrangement, the group is bound together by their shared experience of life in exile and the fleeting nature of their possessions, relationships, and sense of home. Director Isabelle Tollenaere’s fiction film debut is set in one of Europe’s great cities and in a replica of Paris built in China – a metaphor for the immigrants’ old dream of life in a new home and its gradual transformation into a new dream about their old home.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2026

films.t: Past the Hill of Napoleon’s Hat
films.syn: On a misty early-spring morning, Martynas picks up his father from a psychiatric hospital. As they travel to visit his grandparents in a small town in Lithuania, they pass a familiar strangely-shaped hill. It feels like eternity since they all played there together. The poetically titled Past the Hill of Napoleon’s Hat is an oppressive portrait of one fleeting day in the life of an estranged family forced to confront something they have ignored for many years. The coming of spring and the long-anticipated reunion, however, awaken within the father the hope that, this time around, something might change in their fragile relationship.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2025

films.syn: It’s summer, and the tourist season on the Adriatic is in full swing. Loner Rio earns extra money as a kitchen help at a local hotel, but he also commits minor thefts at the expense of foreign visitors. When the young worker Andrea learns about his thieving, the two come to an unusual agreement: they will steal together and share the profits. But this pragmatic alliance grows into an unexpected closeness. Croatian filmmaker Mate Ugrin’s feature debut follows on from several distinctive Balkan films from recent years. Through clever metaphors, subtly elliptical editing, and an evocative use of atmosphere, Petty Thieves paints a portrait of solidarity among people who never stop dreaming of a better future in the face of a tourism industry that pushes them to the margins.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: Although Hassan has retired from his job at the water authority, his neighbors are used to him always helping them out. This time, the situation is serious: The entire town is without water, and tensions are rising among the population with every passing day. Hassan would like to help them all, but he also needs time to mourn a friend who recently died under unclear circumstances. Lebanese director Karim Kassem skillfully works with various cinematic genres to create an elegant double portrait of an aging man and the town of which he has been a part all his life. He does so with a sense of nostalgia, subtle humor, and an almost meditative melancholy, mixed with a touch of detective work.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: A daughter, a mother with severe dementia, and a stepfather. Who has the right to make decisions for someone who can no longer decide on their own? Directed by American filmmaker Lance Hammer, Queen at Sea lays out a clear starting situation, but everything that follows raises uncomfortable questions with no clear answers. This drama about how everyone’s good intentions are not necessarily compatible with one another won the Jury Prize at the Berlinale, where Anna Calder-Marshall and British New Wave icon Tom Courtenay, who portray the central married couple, received the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: On dark and rainy nights, Miles creeps the streets of London, photographing the city’s hidden corners and the people that populate them. The products of these voyeuristic forays, published under the pseudonym Rain Catcher, earn him great renown on social networks and among high culture. With time, however, he starts to notice the same mysterious woman in his photographs – a woman who follows his every move and slowly begins to threaten all his work and his very existence. Michele Fiascaris’s suggestive feature-film debut uses his film’s gloomy atmosphere to explore the city’s underbelly – and the disquieting human mind. The audience is invited to immerse themselves in Miles’s paranoia as he uncovers reality one step at a time.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: How best to understand Iran, a country that, though it has recently been in the news on a daily basis, in many ways remains a mystery? Actress and documentary filmmaker Pegah Ahangarani looks at her country’s history through personal stories. In five portraits of people in her life, be they family or others who have in some way influenced her, she finds commonalities with her own past and with important moments in Iranian history, including the Iran-Iraq war, the revolution, and the recent Women, Life, Freedom movement. Working with extraordinary sensitivity, Ahangarani weaves together archival materials in order to show the world that personal and collective history cannot be separated, because at the end of every story there is always a human being.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Jana Hojdová, a former cinematography student at Prague’s FAMU, sent an email in order to get a contact for Robert Richardson, one of the most distinguished cinematographers on the scene today. It must have been a great surprise for her to receive a reply from the man himself. What started as a student exercise and master’s degree project soon evolved into a creative partnership and personal friendship. The more improbable the film’s premise seems, the more fascinated we become by its portrait of a distinctive and uncompromising artist, three-time Academy Award winner, and acclaimed collaborator of such directors as Oliver Stone, Martin Scorsese and Quentin Tarantino.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: What do we need to see so that we have the impression we’re observing authentic, natural scenery? Viktoria Schmid travelled to Spain, Lithuania and Lower Austria in order to capture unconventional images of seemingly ordinary tracts of landscape. Here, beaches and forests are seen in unexpected colours and contours, which come across as both natural and original. Exquisite, thought-provoking, analogue landscape painting. A visual ASMR that commands our attention.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: In the early 17th century, a soldier arrives in a remote German village to claim the run-down estate he has supposedly inherited. Despite his distinctively scarred face, the soft-spoken young man is otherwise delicate in appearance. The locals are initially skeptical of him, but his hard work and discipline win them over – until, that is, he is expected to have a child with the daughter of one of the villagers, and his carefully constructed identity threatens to be exposed. Markus Schleinzer follows up Michael and Angelo with another meticulously sketched, painful psychological portrait of an individual facing the pressures of majority society. For her dazzling portrayal of Rose, who can only be free when putting on a pair of breeches, Sandra Hüller was awarded the Silver Bear for Best Leading Performance at this year’s Berlinale.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: “I am someone else.” Director Mark Jenkin is a master of 16mm film – as demonstrated by the scene depicting a storm at sea – and he is also an all-round craftsman. His thus far most accessible mystery sci-fi piece follows two Cornwall fishermen (George MacKay and Callum Turner), who get themselves caught up in a weird time loop. This magical film, steeped in a subtly haunted atmosphere, is at once unsettling and engaging in the way it is focused on every gesture, action, movement and creaking of the deck. Its understated, intense and utterly consummate cinematography doesn’t adhere to concepts and just lets things take their course. A film, in which each shot is unobtrusive yet laden with possible meanings.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: A disillusioned elderly inhabitant of Vienna’s Alterlaa housing development seeks to end her life, only to find even the most drastic of escapes rendered impossible by rigid design. Special Jury Mention in the International Competition at the 20th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2026.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: Seventeen-year-old Nikola spends his summer vacation aimlessly hanging out with friends. But this seemingly carefree teenager must bear the burden of looking after his mother, who is suffering from depression. With his friends, he tries to put on an air of nonchalance and self-confidence, but all the while his home situation is only getting worse and the tension between Nikola’s public life and his private reality gradually becomes unsustainable. At this point, he finds refuge with Klara, who offers him a space of peace and vulnerability. This delicate coming-of-age film set in the suburbs of Ljubljana offers intimate closeness wrapped in a summer aesthetic.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2026

films.syn: Gary “Gal” Dove (Ray Winstone) has decided to retire from his life as a bank robber and moves from London to Spain with his wife. But Gal’s unpredictable former associate Don Logan (Ben Kingsley) has different plans, and visits him with an offer for one final job. Filled with gallows humor, Oscar-winning director Jonathan Glazer’s debut demonstrates his love for gangster films as well as his ability to take an exceptionally innovative and absolutely unpredictable approach to the genre. Thanks in part to visionary producer Jeremy Thomas, his spontaneous and at times surreal journey into the subconscious is today considered a modern classic. World premiere of the digitally restored version.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 2000

films.syn: Three decades after the end of Croatia’s war of independence, long-lost Luka returns to his elderly mother without any sign of aging or war injuries. But the warmth of the long-awaited reunion is offset by the fact that the suddenness of the son’s return is just too unbelievable. The nostalgically-laden Shallow Ground listens to the echoes of deep scars in society and lets them resonate in a gentle space framed by the heartwarming patina of 16mm film. An intimate tale inspired by the disappearance of the director’s uncle, the film reflects the experience of thousands of families for whom the war has never really ended.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2025

films.syn: Shaban wants to provide for his family, but the city doesn’t exactly welcome aging men from the countryside with open arms. Although he works hard at everything he does, it still is not enough. Additionally, those around him see his money-making efforts as a measure of his human dignity. How far are people willing to go, and what all can they endure when they are forced to fight for their very existence? Kosovo filmmaker Visar Morina won the Best Director Award at KVIFF in 2015 for his debut Father. Shame and Money, a surgical unmasking of materialism, earned him the Grand Jury Prize from the Sundance Film Festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Renowned Hungarian director Ildikó Enyedi’s latest film has a surprising protagonist: a majestic ginkgo tree on a university campus in Germany that, its roots firmly planted in the ground, quietly observes its surroundings for more than a century. In 1908, it witnesses the arrival of the school’s first female student and the discoveries she makes, in 1972 it follows a student who develops an unexpected relationship with a geranium, and in 2020 a neuroscientist from Hong Kong begins a surprising experiment in the garden. The three eras and three stories are differentiated by the use of different styles, but taken together they are a masterfully directed and quietly political celebration of human curiosity that, with a smile on its face, reveals the insignificance of humanity in the face of nature’s magnificent mysteries.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: If you were to ask ten-year-old Noel about his greatest wish, he would probably answer that he would like to be more like his sister. But he is a boy, and so certain aspects of the world of girls are off-limits to him. A seemingly ordinary visit to the hairdresser, however, becomes the proverbial last drop that causes Noel’s cup of patience to run over. The subtle Sister of Mine is a sensitive exploration of the soul of a child suffering the injustices caused by a lack of understanding and unnecessarily rigid social norms.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2026

films.syn: Have you ever noticed that scissors look a little bit like a crocodile? Maybe yes, maybe no, but for a little girl who is trying to have fun while her mother is working, this realization pulls her out of her boredom and into a world where anything is possible.​

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2025

films.syn: A horse reflects on memory, upsetting the daily routines of the residents of Los Santos, San Andreas, during an interview for his new book Someone to Steal Horses With.​ Special Jury Mention in the Labo Competition at the 20th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2026.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2025

films.ot: Stallion y la Bola de Cristal
films.syn: Passion often stirs in the darkness – and undertaking the journey towards authenticity sometimes requires a little sorcery and magic. And it is these latter which are harnessed by a young man whose path to self-acceptance leads through fantasy. Suppressed desire fights its way out until it isn’t clear whether or not we simply imagined it all. A seductive film of powerful gestures and everlasting impressions.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: Cinema has long been drawn to the subject of adolescence as an important period in life when our view of the world and of ourselves radically changes. Strange River nevertheless shows that there still is more to discover in the subgenre of the “coming-of-age” film.
