Jaume Claret Muxart’s feature debut takes audiences on a visually captivating, poetic journey along the Danube as it tells the tale of the emotional and sexual awakening of sixteen-year-old Dídac, including how his personal transformation affects the rest of the family. Mirroring the river, the film lets itself be carried along by an unpredictable stream as it gradually blurs the line between dream and reality in order to capture the fragility and uncertainty of youth.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: It’s the late 1980s. Three friends – Pepe, Milan and František – are making the most of Karlovy Vary’s nightlife. While their days are dampened by the tedious, at times, absurd workplace reality of late socialism, their nights are given over to decadence. Naturally, women are essential to their plans, and who says you can’t spend a night with your mate’s girlfriend as well? Except there’s a virus going around that causes a disease no-one dares mention, with currently no cure. AIDS. Věra Chytilová’s jagged, expressive directorial style is complemented by the poetic sensibilities of Sklep Theatre, whose founders appear in the lead roles. This sombre farce blends an image of a society jaded by empty regime slogans with a portrait of friendship which, in the face of threat, disintegrates into cold egoism.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings – Classics); production year 1988

films.syn: In a world where speech is a forbidden form of intimacy, a local outsider in a Spanish village must choose between a loveless marriage and the promise of true connection with a kindred stranger.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2025

films.t: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
films.syn: Camp Miasma, the cult slasher franchise from the eighties, is back! Enthusiastic director Kris is obsessed with the idea of restoring the series to its former glory while simultaneously purging it of the (by contemporary standards) problematic elements typical of genre films from that era. But when she meets actress Billy (Gillian Anderson) from the first film, they both plunge into an intoxicating, bloody delirium that completely blurs the line between the silver screen and reality. Working with love and admiration, director Jane Schoenbrun breaks down the slasher genre into its elementary particles, only to reassemble it in a new, more empathetic, and more open spirit. The result is a work they have described as Portrait of a Lady on Fire in the world of Friday the 13th.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2026

films.syn: The subject of fathers who prioritize their careers over everyday life and thus lay the groundwork for later trauma is a relatively common one in contemporary cinema. Renowned Spanish filmmaker Esteban Garcia (an outstanding Javier Bardem) returns to his home country after many years away to shoot a new movie. He has even written the main character for his actress daughter, whom he hasn’t seen in many years, but even he doesn’t know to what extent his decision was influenced by his confidence in his daughter’s acting abilities. “Through the story of a father and his daughter, we wanted to talk about power relations, hierarchy and the world of cinema,” says director Rodrigo Sorogoyen, who showed the film in competition at Cannes.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Fierce, emancipated, bold, intoxicating, subversive, sensual, rebellious! A description of The Bride’s main protagonist Mary/Ida/Penelope, and of the film itself – a fresh reinterpretation of one of the most famous stories of all time, that of Frankenstein and his bride. With her second stint behind the camera, Maggie Gyllenhaal firmly establishes herself as a producer, director, and screenwriter alongside her remarkable career as an actor. Set in 1930s Chicago, her provocative dark romance is a stylized ride in which monsters and torrents of words come to life in order to launch an assault on the patriarchy and express a sentiment that generations of women have always hesitated to say aloud: “I would prefer not to.”

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tributes); production year 2026

films.syn: Years after retiring, former European boxing champion and Olympic medalist Pavel “Hoff” Hoffmeister (Milan Ondrík) accepts a lucrative offer to return to a world that used to be his entire life. Instead of a boxing ring, however, he’ll be getting into an MMA cage to fight the feared Hungarian Béla Kardos (Ján Jackuliak). Can a father-son trainer duo (Pavel Rímský and Martin Finger) help the determined Hoff get back in shape and succeed in a world of new rules and also in the minefield of strained family relationships? Applying their knowledge of the genre and its best examples (Rocky, Fists in the Dark, The Wrestler), the creators of this eagerly anticipated film depict the world of dramatic encounters in the octagon with a sense of respect but also with subtly humorous detachment.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: This compelling courtroom drama was one of the first attempts to present an unflinching criticism of the communist regime. The filmmakers skilfully upended the scheme of ideologically driven works advocating just punishment for embezzlers of socialist property. Managing director Kudrna, the key defendant in a high-profile trial, is guilty of financial crime, yet, without this act of misconduct, in a collapsing economy he wouldn’t have been able to secure the construction of a new power plant. Perhaps even more daring are the revelations that the deputy minister who pressured Kudrna into taking on the project is a spineless individual and that the judiciary is subordinate to the state apparatus. The Defendant earned directors Ján Kadár and Elmar Klos the Crystal Globe at the Karlovy Vary IFF in 1964.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1964

films.syn: Simon is an introverted and not particularly interesting office worker who quietly admires his co-worker Hanna from afar. But the arrival of a new colleague, James, shakes Simon’s existence to its very core. He looks exactly like Simon, but he is charismatic, extroverted, and popular. As James slowly takes over Simon’s life, the socially weaker of the two sinks deeper into a crisis of identity. In his adaptation of the novella by Fyodor Dostoevsky, director Richard Ayoade creates a captivating world that blends dark humor, psychological thriller, and an almost Kafkaesque nightmare. Precisely because of this connection to European cultural tradition, Jesse Eisenberg, who plays a dual role in the film, has chosen to personally present The Double at this year’s festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tributes); production year 2013

films.syn: Svilengrad, southeastern Bulgaria. Veska has recently returned to her hometown in order to oversee a nearby archeological dig. By coincidence, she runs into Saïd, an old acquaintance whose car has been stolen. When Veska offers to drive him to a meeting, she is caught up in a smuggling operation and sets out on a dangerous adventure that forces her to confront her past and her own desires. Director Valeska Grisebach continues her exploration of a genre ordinarily dominated by men. Her muted gangster movie, winner of the Jury Prize at Cannes, relies on an exceptionally captivating protagonist but also works as a study of Bulgaria’s diverse border region.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Pari and Hanna, roommates and friends, live in modern-day Tehran. Pari is a curator and director of an independent theatre group; Hanna is a dancer, who wants to get out of Iran as soon as possible. The situation of both women becomes more complicated, but their friendship is strong in the face of political oppression. The Friend’s House Is Here is a rewarding cinematic experience, conveying a sense of freedom and hope, even though it originated under very different conditions. Just a few days after the June War in Iran, the crew, headed by directing duo Hossein Keshavarz and Maryam Ataei, took to the streets of Tehran to make a film about a generation that no longer wants to live according to imposed rules and is striving to achieve one of the fundamental human rights, the right to freedom of artistic expression.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2025

films.syn: Benjamin has just finished college, but instead of finally entering adulthood, he finds himself consumed by restlessness, apathy, and Mrs. Robinson – the wife of a family friend. When Benjamin later falls in love with her daughter Elaine, his aimless wandering becomes a frantic rush forward. Perhaps no film in the history of cinema has captured the uncertainty, fury, and also the tenacity of young people with such intensity as The Graduate. A defining work of the New Hollywood, the film was influenced by the European New Wave and the burgeoning counterculture of the 1960s and earned Mike Nichols an Oscar for Best Director. It also introduced cinema to a new type of American (anti)hero, an unforgettable soundtrack by Simon & Garfunkel, and, above all, the extraordinary acting talent of Dustin Hoffman.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tributes); production year 1967

films.syn: Fresh parents Karl and Emilie are looking forward to a weekend at a seaside hotel, where they plan to announce their child’s name and thus officially welcome him to the world. A day before the celebration, however, Karl’s mother Vibeke shows up, with whom he hasn’t spoken in several years. Building on the tradition of contemporary Nordic cinema, debut filmmaker Mads Mengel tells the intimate story of a family that threatens to fall apart when old wounds are opened up. What begins as a close-knit celebration turns into an uncomfortable confrontation with an unresolved past that won’t let the film’s protagonists forget who they really are – or where they come from.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: Are you a fan of The Elephant Man, Kafka, The Fly, or Zoolander? Then you probably know that they would not have been made without the crucial contribution of Stuart Cornfeld, one of the most fascinating producers in American independent film. Spanish artist and filmmaker Joan Bofill has shot an inventive portrait of this eccentric visionary, whose enthusiasm was more than a little infectious. Reminiscing about their creative partner are David Lynch, Steven Soderbergh, Guillermo Del Toro, David Cronenberg, and producer Mark Johnson. An unusually crafted biographical documentary, founded on the filmmaker’s friendship with this plainspoken “geyser of creativity” and painted with both film camera and painter’s brush.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings – Classics); production year 2025

films.syn: Documentary filmmaker John Wilson’s cinematic debut, shown at this year’s Sundance Film Festival, is a kind of personal epilogue to his successful series How To with John Wilson, which ran for three seasons on HBO. Working with an ironic contrast between the film’s images and its narration, he translates his unique way of seeing into a web of metaphors that explores the complexity of a world in which even something as solid and seemingly reliable as concrete crumbles and falls apart. Can we find answers from people who are dead certain of their view of the world?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: If we could rid ourselves of all our pains, would we still be ourselves? The film’s broken, traumatized protagonist comes to teach at a high school in a small mountain village where everyone seems suspiciously happy. He soon learns that it is all thanks to fifteen-year-old Matteo and his supernatural gift. Filled with intense music and visuals that recall the tradition of Italy’s giallo genre, The Holy Boy is an allegorical exploration of loss, fatherhood, adolescence, and the freedom of the individual versus the needs of the collective. The film had its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.t: The Ink-Stained Hand and the Missing Thumb
films.syn: If the world had an edge, it might look something like the remote corner of northern India where Santosh and Rajji live, collecting highway tolls in dilapidated booths. Work and endless waiting are blurred together. Bound by the power of love, but also by the need to constantly move around in search of work, they dream of the happiness that awaits them in a new place… until one day, a sudden tragedy turns their lives upside down. As melancholic as it is tender, The Ink-Stained Hand and the Missing Thumb is the story of everyone who has suffered an unexpected loss. It is a heartfelt romance bordering on magical realism, a fleeting memory of a loved one fading into oblivion.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2026

films.t: The Killing of a Chinese Bookie
films.syn: “Years ago, Martin Scorsese and I were talking and in one night made up this gangster story about this nightclub owner who owes a lot of money and is talked into killing someone who isn’t really the person he thinks he’s going to be killing.” Thus describes John Cassavetes the origins of this film, with which the Karlovy Vary film festival continues its ongoing Cassavetes master class. Ben Gazzara shines as the charismatic owner of a strip club in this dark character study passing itself off as a neo-noir crime drama. With his melancholic glimpse into the male psyche, Cassavetes created a metaphor likening the captains of Hollywood (whom he detested) to gangsters.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings – Classics); production year 1978

films.syn: Northern Italy, September 1943. A group of Allied prisoners of war escapes from a prison train headed to Germany. They soon meet up with local partisans and a multinational group of desperate refugees. All share the same goal – to cross the Alps and make it to neutral Switzerland. Lauded in its time and unjustly forgotten today, The Last Chance – filmed as the last battles of World War II were still raging – presages the coming era of Neorealist cinema. By using a minimum of studio shots and working with real soldiers escaped from Italian prison camps, director Leopold Lindtberg further amplified his film’s urgent moral message. The film premiered at the first festival in 1946.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1945

films.syn: Of the fourteen eight-thousanders, the second-highest, K2, has always presented a deadly challenge, grimly defying all who have attempted to climb this mountain in the winter months. More than a quarter of a century after his first of several visits to the Karlovy Vary IFF, renowned American documentarist Amir Bar-Lev returns with a nerve-shredding yet also touching story of a few resolute individuals who decided in 2021 to conquer the snow-clad “savage mountain”. This breathtaking spectacle, transporting us to places the majority of climbers will never reach, offers a comprehensive reflection of what is often naïve human folly in the face of nature and her extremes. The film also considers the gradual commercialisation of extreme outdoor sports that goes hand in hand with the rise of social media.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Young Irina dares to hope that she might find refuge with her grandmother after she and her daughter escape a toxic relationship. But no – her grandmother has very different ideas about what Irina’s life should look like. And on top of it all, a real summer storm is brewing that only brings further darkness and heaviness. The masterful use of elements of horror brings out the claustrophobic atmosphere of a house where fear and love meet hope and understanding. Finnish director Helmi Donner’s graduation film celebrated its world premiere in the Cannes Film Festival’s La Cinéf section for student film.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2025

films.syn: Mariama, an asylum-seeker from Senegal, has just turned eighteen. Stella, at first glance a withdrawn woman in her forties, has recently decided to break free from the clutches of addiction and to give her life a fresh start. In their attempt at finding their place in a world where nothing comes for free, the two women meet and form an unexpectedly strong bond. Following her 2018 debut Pause, Cypriot producer and director Tonia Mishiali returns to Karlovy Vary with a vivid, heartwarming, and hopeful story about how family bonds and motherly love can be found in the most unlikely places.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Crystal Globe Competition); production year 2026

films.syn: New York in the late 1980s. Actor Jimmy George (Rami Malek) is recuperating from serious health complications, but he is determined to return to the stage for what may be one of his final roles. Thanks to the play’s rehearsals and a new romance, he finds meaning in life, but his friends remain on alert. Ira Sachs’s ninth feature film, part intimate relationship drama and part melancholy look back at New York’s queer community, captures that community’s distinctive energy and fragility during the AIDS epidemic. Instead of presenting awareness of one’s mortality in a sentimental manner, however, it shows it as a celebration of life, love, and art.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: 22 June 1986. Estadio Azteca, Mexico City. The start of the World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. While almost the whole world is familiar with the goal of the century and Maradona’s infamous “Hand of God,” the real story behind the “match of the century” is even more dramatic. The Falklands War, national pride, political tensions, and the players’ lives all formed the backdrop to a game that inspires passionate debate to this day. Forty years later, Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco’s documentary looks back on this historic match through a combination of archival footage and interviews with former players. This fascinating story of rivalry, memory, and reconciliation reminds us why, for ninety minutes, football is capable of capturing the whole world’s attention.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: ​Charli XCX: for some, an uncompromising and visionary cultural icon, for others a “famous, but not quite,” singer who mostly exists on the margins of the pop-music industry – until, that is, she releases her sixth studio album, Brat. This stylish, pulsating mockumentary about a star getting ready for her first arena tour presents Charli XCX in an exaggerated yet surprisingly honest role, a role that she says she was born to play. Imbued with a healthy dose of irony and self-reflection, young Scottish photographer and filmmaker Aidan Zamiri’s feature film debut looks at all the things that come with unexpected mainstream success while also showing us the vulnerable side of this at first glance always confident 365 party girl.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Afterhours); production year 2026

films.t: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
films.syn: Harry Lehman has lived as a pickpocket since the eighties. But New York has changed. Wallets filled with cash have been replaced by credit cards, people are constantly staring at their phones, and the old tricks no longer work. One day, when Harry steals a flash drive whose true value he is unaware of, he finds himself in a dangerous race against time and through the city’s streets. Director Noah Segan has created a nostalgic portrait of a man living in a world he can no longer understand. His melancholy crime drama starring John Turturro is an homage to the old New York and a reflection on all the things that are disappearing in our digital age.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: As FBI agent Terry Husk (Jude Law) investigates a series of robberies in the Pacific Northwest, he cannot shake the feeling that these are not just economically motivated crimes, but that behind them lies a much more dangerous ideology. The trail leads him to a violent neo-Nazi organization whose ambitions go far beyond ordinary criminality. Director Justin Kurzel’s The Order is based on the non-fiction book The Silent Brotherhood about the real-life investigation of a right-wing group that was active in the United States in the 1980s. His tense thriller, a combination of procedural drama with a chilling portrait of radicalization, reminds us how easily extremist ideas can grow into organized violence.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tributes); production year 2024

films.syn: Mrinal Sen’s The Outsiders is a searing exploration of the depths of abject poverty. Faced with an irredeemable system of exploitation, a father and son decide that working only exacerbates social inequalities, so they refuse to do so. The film’s raw realism blurs the lines between protagonists and antagonists until all that remains are bitterness and suppressed rage, which serve as the central duo’s guiding credo and the driving force behind their personal rebellion. Their anarchist philosophy, disrupted by the son’s marriage to a girl named Nilamma, is reflected in the father’s nihilistic declaration: “People have always worked hard, and still they die of hunger. I would rather die than work.” Special Jury Prize in 1978.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1977

films.syn: Before Palestine, the Zionist Congress set its sights on the colonisation of the Ugandan highlands, where it sent an expedition in 1904 to explore their potential as a Jewish homeland. One hundred and twenty years on, the director scouts locations in the region for a possible period film. This authentic and, at the same time, deliberately artificial documentary functions admirably on numerous levels; here, the material blends with the poetic, the practical with the elusive. No man’s lands don’t exist; even the filmmaker could be a coloniser.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: We all know this situation: visitors are coming, so the toys need to be put away. But that’s so boring! Playing with toys is so much more fun. And then things happen! The wild race can begin.​

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.syn: Hotel manager Lucius must come to terms with the loss of his life’s work, his home, and the home of his daughter. Is there a chance that the Argentine developer Facundo might change his plans to purchase the Intercontinental Hotel in order to demolish it and then build a reimagined version? How to differentiate between pathological obsession and simple human attachment or nostalgia? The poetic figures move through poetic images and break through the two-dimensionality of the screen in search of true depth. The film, which playfully incorporates documentary footage, premiered in the Orizzonti section at the Venice Film Festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2025

films.syn: Layal has achieved a minor miracle. In the middle of a war zone, she has created an oasis of peace – a gas station guided by three simple rules: no men, no weapons, and no politics. When her younger brother faces enlistment, she is willing to do anything to keep him from being drafted. Only her older sister can help, but they have been estranged for a long time. In the middle of the fighting, can such things as love, humor, forgiveness, and empathy survive? In her fiction debut, Yemeni director Sara Ishaq shows that the answer is “Yes.” Her film gives a voice to the women whose husbands, brothers, and fathers have disappeared in the war, leaving them to face life on their own. Fortunately, they have each other.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: The Karlovy Vary IFF’s nearly fifteen-year friendship with Mark Cousins, whose stunning film essays have impressed countless viewers over the years, is firmly rooted in a shared passion for the world of cinema and in the festival’s sincere admiration for this inimitable Northern Irish filmmaker, writer, curator, film critic and traveller. After what are now legendary series The Story of Film: An Odyssey and Women Make Film, the magnetic storyteller brings us another saga, this time devoted to documentary film. Of his sixteen hour-long chapters embracing the entire history of the tenth muse, Cousins selected for Karlovy Vary the part that centres on the 1980s, an era that was fundamental for our region from a socio-political perspective.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: “A political film must not only be revolutionary and radical, but also artistically and culturally enriching”, stated director Glauber Rocha, a key figure of Brazil’s Cinema Novo movement. His debut, awarded in Karlovy Vary in 1962, thus brings us an array of magical scenes of rituals performed by the inhabitants of the Bahia fishing region; at the same time, it nevertheless raises a critical question – how can mysticism maintain its relevance in the fight against oppression and exploitation? Rocha’s loosely structured narrative, drawing on the documentary film aesthetic, is rhythmically and conceptually akin to the sea, whose calm surface can at any moment be roiled by the barravento, a sudden, violent and destructive wind.​

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1962

films.syn: Photographer David spends his days documenting the changing face of the city, while at night he wanders its dark streets. One day, when he sees an unfamiliar woman at a party, he cannot take his eyes off her and is compelled to follow her. The next morning, he wakes up in her body. David’s desperate search for his own leads him ever deeper into a world where the line between Self and Other is constantly being blurred and identity is a mere fragile illusion. Arthur Harari follows on from his award-winning Onoda: 10,000 Nights in the Jungle with a mysterious thriller about a man trapped in a labyrinth of other people’s lives that also presents us with an unsettling meditation on body, memory, and the desire to be someone else.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Three Colors: Blue is the first in Krzysztof Kieślowski’s trilogy of films named for the colors of the French flag, in which he explored the contemporary meaning of the French Revolutionary ideals of liberty, equality, and brotherhood. The meticulously crafted Blue is a meditation on the possibility of free choice for someone agonizingly bound to the past. After a car accident kills Julie’s daughter and husband (a renowned composer), she desperately tries to cut all ties to the past, dissociating herself from her previous life, including her own creative work. With the help of her husband’s former collaborator, she ultimately rejoins the musical score that is human society. For her portrayal of Julie, Juliette Binoche was awarded the Volpi Cup for Best Actress at the 1993 Venice Film Festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Tributes); production year 1993

films.syn: In 2014, Shakhta, Dancer, and Potter volunteered for the army in order to fight in the Russo-Ukrainian conflict in eastern Ukraine. Although the horrible things they experienced during two years on the front accompany them for every second of their existence, they try to return to civilian life. But the Russian invasion in 2022 forces them to again confront the war. Filmed over the course of twelve years, this documentary uses a fragmentary cinematic language to evoke the trauma experienced by its protagonists, and thus to help us imagine the unimaginable: how to accept that some live while others die, and that – faced with one’s own death – what remains above all is the desire to live.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings); production year 2026

films.syn: Thirty years since first being shown at the festival, this cult classic – without which British cinema of the nineties wouldn’t have been half as cool – returns to Vary in a brand-new restored version. Despite the intervening decades, this original and sarcasm-laden rebellion against consumer culture based on the novel by Irvine Welsh has retained the authenticity and forceful energy of a defiantly raised middle finger. The iconic soundtrack (including tracks by Iggy Pop and Underworld) perfectly captures the frenzied pace, reminiscent of a wild drug-fueled ride, with which the film portrays its likable gang of eccentric slackers as they go through their daily lives of (in)action. Trainspotting was also a defining moment in the careers of Ewan McGregor, Robert Carlyle, and the other members of the ensemble cast.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Out of the Past – KVIFF 60/80); production year 1996

films.syn: One would think that every road movie needs its central setting: the road. But Francisco Marise’s hybrid film senses that every trip, road, or journey requires us to stop every now and then. It is just such moments, when the film’s Argentinian truck driver protagonists turn off their engines and stop driving, that form this film’s starting point. Interweaving intimate observations with subtle glimpses of transcendence, Truck Driver paints a collective portrait of people who share a strange dimension of time within the silence of the asphalt wilderness – at motels, on the side of the road, and in tire shops, savoring the pure joy of the present moment while longing for loved ones far away.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Proxima Competition); production year 2025

films.syn: Crocodile, crocodile, you’ve worn out your shoes and what have you turned yourself into? Anything and everything! The day is long, especially for a little boy who has a lot to learn. Good thing he has his trusted crocodile helper.​

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2024

films.t: Two Mountains Weighing Down My Chest
films.syn: Chinese artist and filmmaker Viv Li’s infectiously energetic, endearingly quirky, but also profoundly personal and exceptionally incisive self-portrait was one of the most pleasant surprises at this year’s Berlinale. Working with a DIY style, the director captures herself caught between Berlin’s pulsating alternative culture scene and the more conservative environment of contemporary China. Along the way, she reveals subtle culture clashes in a world that is globalized and polarized all at once. Shot in a playful yet sincere tone, her film explores the never-ending search for personal identity, home, and sense of belonging.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: When John Smith arrived at the Toronto IFF in 2024, he was surprised at the standard of the hotel he had been assigned as an avant-garde filmmaker. He then encountered a man in the lift who was staying in a room thirteen storeys higher up – the greater the star, the higher the floor. And since strangers don’t usually speak to one another in lifts, Smith had to make this film in order to pass on an important message to him.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: Los Angeles 2028: possibly the last punk-noir joyride through the city. Living on the edge of legality is the new norm; the protagonists here have to find their scratchcards in order to be able to afford them. This depressing yet defiantly energetic piece by Canadian filmmaker Charlotte Zhang feels both contemporary and drifting. We observe a tangible decline, captured with searing ordinariness; a deterioration the characters witness and in which they participate. This is carefully planned but also wonderfully intuitive filmmaking, following – in the future – the text of the song “This Bitter Earth” by Dinah Washington from 1960. Clichés about Third World countries are outdated, dystopia has long since become our reality.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2025

films.syn: “Erosion is a slow process that we notice when things crumble or break.” Artist and animator Nicolas Piret once again demonstrates his remarkable craftsmanship and entirely understated technique as he returns to the theme of equilibrium between people and nature. On this occasion he takes us on a neat excursion to a deserted Venice, although there’s also something unsettling here. Eleven sheets of paper, countless enchantments – and the creative antithesis of the souvenir magnet.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: Most people will be familiar with the opera Carmen, but can it be interpreted in an innovative manner that will also attract young audiences? Sébastien Laudenbach’s latest animated film tells us that the answer is yes. This adventure set on the side streets of sunny Seville tells the story of the orphan Salvador and his friend Belén, who, together with a gang of other street urchins, try to prevent a dark prophecy concerning the free-spirited beauty Carmen from coming true. This modern adaptation calling for women’s and community solidarity will captivate you with its opulent visual design characterized by the constant movement of broken lines, a rich palette of tropical colors, and an imaginative musical accompaniment in which original melodies blend with instrumental motifs evoking Bizet’s famous operatic score.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Folklore is more than a traditionalistic nod in the direction of folk costumes. Folklore is the Met Gala, folklore is burning an effigy of Morana, folklore is the consumption of aspic. Via the language of TikTok and the girlband Čokovoko, this riotously playful yet intellectually pithy film paraphrases influencer babble; the mood board is covered with a collage of superficiality and boundless creativity. Dr LeGrand’s ADHD, which wasn’t endorsed by Leda Footwear.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: Thirty years have passed since the theatre release of the cult film Whisper which, in the mid-1990s, evoked the atmosphere of the clubs of the time and the trends associated with them. Anna (Tatiana Dyková) travels from the country and arrives in Prague, where she meets Speedy (Jan Čechtický), his brother Filip (Jan P. Muchow), Kytka (Martin Myšička) and their flatmate Irma (Kateřina Winterová). Anna gradually eases herself into city life and becomes a part of the relationships that new friends cultivate among themselves. The unmistakable music tracks used in the film were created by the band Colorfactory.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Special Screenings – Classics); production year 1996

films.syn: One of the largest pig breeding facilities in the former GDR closed its gates a long time ago, yet its past reveals valuable testimonies. Voices filter through abstract shots of the site as this insistent yet also contemplative film tries to find traces of life amid the dilapidation. An urbex, which gives a fresh voice to people for whom today’s ruins once represented an opportunity.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Imagina); production year 2026

films.syn: A perfectionist illustrator accidentally creates a little wolf with an ink nose who is not afraid to leave the paper and give his playful nature free rein. But what a mess he makes! A gentle film about how difficult it is to face one’s own mistakes, but also about how nobody is perfect – and that’s okay.​ Best film in the National Competition at the 20th Pragueshorts Film Festival 2026.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Pragueshorts at KVIFF); production year 2025

films.syn: Berlin in the role of Ankara, Hamburg as Istanbul. The winning film of this year’s Berlinale is a meticulous analysis of a struggle against power that could be set anywhere and doesn’t lose its momentum for even a second. Playwright Aziz and his wife Derya run afoul of the regime, and although they overcome the loss of their home and their jobs thanks to the help of friends and family, it is unclear whether this conflict can remain entirely without victims. The new situation tests the relationships within the family, especially as regards the couple’s teenage daughter.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: We find ourselves in the quiet fog of the Bekaa Valley on the border between Lebanon and Syria. Quietly, against the backdrop of the seemingly ordinary rhythm of life, the stories of the local inhabitants unfold with the potential to imperceptibly, and thus all the more powerfully, shake the entire region. Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep is a film about women who are treated as the solution to one’s problems, and about men who affect the lives of the people around them. Palestinian director Rakan Mayasi’s debut film was significantly influenced by the story of his grandmother, who was forced into marriage at age fourteen. The result is not so much a straightforward narrative, but rather a space in which to deeply feel the injustices that continue to reign over the region today.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Horizons); production year 2026

films.syn: Zampano lives with his father, a former trapeze artist, with whom he has a complicated and uneven relationship. His father spends his days lounging about and drinking, and so it is up to Zampano to look after their day-to-day life. When his father’s former circus comes to town, Zampano senses an opportunity to break free from his father and to perform alongside Nina, the trapeze artist he is in love with. Ironically, however, he suffers from vertigo and a fear of heights. Teilo Quillard’s aesthetically captivating film combines impressive trapeze performances with intimate moments to create a captivating tale of courage, family bonds, and conquering one’s fears.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Future Frames: Generation NEXT of European Cinema); production year 2025
